B2.q: Why does Ayo choose not to tell Rosa what she has noticed?
o: She thinks the number is wrong.
She wants to keep the information secret from the hospital.
She does not trust Rosa.
She wants to protect Rosa from more fear until she is sure.
B2.hint: Ayo'nun yaptığı bağlantıyı neden Rosa'yla paylaşmadığını düşün.
B2.why: Ayo, sayının doğru olsa bile Rosa'yı sakinleştirmeyeceğini düşünüyor; Rosa'nın korkusunu artırmak istemiyor.

text: On Sunday night Rosa came to Ayo's office with red eyes. She was a strong woman, and in two years of night shifts Ayo had never once seen her cry. "Doctor," she said, "I need to tell you something."

"Sit down, Rosa." Rosa remained standing, her hands pressed flat against her uniform as though she were trying to keep it from coming apart. "My daughter Lina is nine. Last Sunday she came to the hospital because I was working a double shift and my sister was away. She stayed with me for two hours. She played in the corridor, and she washed her hands in the bathroom at the east end."

Ayo felt a coldness spread through her chest. "The east end of the sixth floor?" "That bathroom." Rosa's voice was very small. "This morning Lina had a headache. Tonight she's coughing, and she says her legs hurt."
"It could be an ordinary cold," Ayo said gently. "Children catch them all the time."

"It could be. But I don't believe in 'could be' any more. Not on that floor." Ayo glanced at the calendar on her wall. Counting from last Sunday, the interval between the visit and the first symptoms was exactly the interval she had been recording all week. She said nothing. Rosa was already holding on to her composure with both hands, and a number, however accurate, would not help her hold it. Instead Ayo stood up, took her coat from the hook and said, "Bring her in. I'll examine her myself, and I'll do it tonight."
C1.proof: I'll examine her myself, and I'll do it tonight
C1.q: What decision does Ayo take at the end of the scene?
o: To examine Lina personally and without delay.
To send Rosa home for the rest of the week.
To close the east bathroom at once.
To ask Mr. Garrow for advice.
C1.hint: Ayo, sayıyı söylemek yerine ne yapıyor?
C1.why: Ayo Rosa'ya sayıyı söylemek yerine eyleme geçiyor: Lina'yı bizzat ve o gece muayene edeceğini söylüyor.

eps.title: Not Necessary
eps.recap: Ayo, altıncı kat doğu banyosundan su örneği alınmasını talep etti; Mr. Garrow bunun gereksiz olduğunu ve geçen ay rutin testin yapıldığını yazdı. Ancak kayıtlarda böyle bir test görünmüyordu.

text: On Monday morning, Ayo wrote an email to Mr. Garrow. She wrote it very carefully. "Dear Mr. Garrow, I would like to take water samples from the bathroom at the east end of the sixth floor. Could you please give permission? Thank you, Dr. Bennett."
The answer came in ten minutes. Mr. Garrow wrote: "Dear Dr. Bennett, this is not necessary. We tested the water last month. The results were normal. Please do not worry. Best wishes, J. Garrow."
Ayo read the message twice. Last month? That sounded good. But Ayo wanted to see the paper with the results.

She went to the office where the hospital keeps all its water records. A young assistant helped her. They looked in the folder for September. They looked in October. They looked in all the folders for the year.
"I am sorry," said the assistant. "I cannot find any water test for the sixth floor. Not last month. Not this year."
A2.proof: I cannot find any water test for the sixth floor.
A2.q: What does Ayo discover?
o: The water test was done by the laboratory.
The water in the hospital is always clean.
Mr. Garrow's story about a water test may not be true.
The records office is closed on Mondays.
A2.hint: Garrow geçen ay test yapıldığını yazıyor; asistan ne buluyor?
A2.why: Garrow geçen ay su testi yapıldığını söylüyor ama kayıtlarda altıncı kat için hiçbir test yok; bu, söylediğinin doğru olmayabileceğini gösteriyor.

text: On Monday morning Ayo wrote a careful email to Mr. Garrow. "Dear Mr. Garrow, may I take water samples from the bathroom at the east end of the sixth floor? Thank you, Dr. Bennett."
The answer came in ten minutes. "Dear Dr. Bennett, this is not necessary. We tested the water last month and the results were normal. Please do not worry. Best wishes, J. Garrow."
Ayo read the message twice. Last month. That sounded good, but she wanted to see the paper with the results.
She went to the records office, where a young assistant helped her. They looked in the folder for September. They looked in the folder for October. They looked in every folder for the year.

"I'm sorry," said the assistant. "I cannot find any water test for the sixth floor. Not last month, and not this year." Ayo stood in the corridor and thought: a man who writes 'do not worry' so quickly has usually something to worry about.
B1.proof: I cannot find any water test for the sixth floor
B1.q: What does Ayo discover about Mr. Garrow's reply?
o: The test was done by another hospital.
The test showed that the water was dirty.
The assistant refused to help her.
The water test he talks about cannot be found in the records.
B1.hint: Garrow'un söylediği testi kayıtlarda bulabildiler mi?
B1.why: Garrow geçen ay test yapıldığını söylüyor ama kayıtlarda altıncı kat için hiçbir su testi yok; söylediği doğru olmayabilir.

text: On Monday morning Ayo wrote a very careful email to Mr. Garrow. "Dear Mr. Garrow, I would like permission to take water samples from the bathroom at the east end of the sixth floor. Many thanks, Dr. Bennett."

The reply came within ten minutes. "Dear Dr. Bennett, this is not necessary. The water was tested last month and the results were normal. Please do not worry yourself over nothing. Best wishes, J. Garrow."
Ayo read the message twice. Last month. It sounded reassuring, but she wanted to see the actual results with her own eyes.
She went to the records office, where a young assistant helped her search. They looked through the folder for September, then October, then every folder for the whole year.

"I'm sorry, Dr. Bennett," said the assistant at last. "There is no water test for the sixth floor. Not last month, and not this year. Perhaps Mr. Garrow keeps his own copy?" Ayo thanked her and stood for a moment in the corridor. A man who writes 'do not worry' so quickly, she thought, is usually a man who has something to worry about.
B2.proof: A man who writes 'do not worry' so quickly
B2.q: What does Ayo conclude about Mr. Garrow's reply?
o: It was written quickly because he wants to stop her investigation.
It was a normal reply from a busy manager.
It was sent to the wrong person.
It shows that he is a very kind man.
B2.hint: Cevabın on dakikada gelmesi ve kayıtların olmaması birlikte neyi gösterir?
B2.why: Garrow çok hızlı cevap veriyor ve yazdığı test kayıtlarda yok; Ayo bunun soruşturmayı durdurmak için yazılmış olabileceğini düşünüyor.

text: On Monday morning Ayo wrote a very careful email to Mr. Garrow. "Dear Mr. Garrow, I would like permission to take water samples from the bathroom at the east end of the sixth floor. Many thanks, Dr. Bennett."

The reply came within ten minutes. "Dear Dr. Bennett, this is not necessary. The water was tested last month and the results were normal. Please do not worry yourself over nothing. Best wishes, J. Garrow."
Ayo read the message twice. Last month. It sounded reassuring, but she wanted to see the actual results with her own eyes.
She went to the records office, where a young assistant helped her search. They looked through the folder for September, then October, then every folder for the whole year.

"I'm sorry, Dr. Bennett," said the assistant at last. "There is no water test for the sixth floor. Not last month, and not this year. Perhaps Mr. Garrow keeps his own copy?" Ayo thanked her and stood for a moment in the corridor. A man who writes 'do not worry' so quickly, she thought, is usually a man who has something to worry about. And a man who cites a test that does not exist is either mistaken or lying, and Garrow did not strike her as someone who made mistakes about his own building.
C1.proof: Garrow did not strike her as someone who made mistakes about his own building
C1.q: What can be inferred from Ayo's last thought?
o: That she thinks Garrow knows nothing about the building.
That she suspects Garrow is lying rather than making an honest error.
That she believes the assistant is lying.
That she wants Garrow to be promoted.
C1.hint: Garrow'un 'kendi binasında hata yapmayacak' biri olması neyi ima eder?
C1.why: Ayo, Garrow'un bu tür bir hatayı yapmayacağını düşünüyor; yani yanlış bilgiyi bilerek verdiğinden şüpheleniyor.

eps.title: The Roof
eps.recap: Ayo gece yangın merdiveninden çatıya çıktı ve soğutma kulesinin yeşil, yosunlu bir su havuzuna sahip olduğunu gördü. Kuleden yükselen buhar, altıncı katın doğu kanadının hava girişine doğru sürükleniyordu.

text: At midnight, Ayo decided to look at the hospital roof. She took the stairs for fire emergencies, because Mr. Garrow's office was next to the lift. The stairs were dark and cold.

At the top, she pushed open a heavy metal door. The wind hit her face. In front of her was a big grey machine, as tall as a house. It made a low, rattling noise. It was the cooling tower. It helps to keep the hospital air cool in summer.
Ayo walked closer with her torch. Water was falling inside the tower. At the bottom, there was a pool. The water was not clear. It was green, thick and slippery.
A little steam rose from the tower. It was almost invisible, but the torch showed it clearly. The wind was blowing the steam to the left.
Ayo followed it with her light. On the left, there was a wall with a large metal box. It was an air intake. Under it, a small sign said: 'Sixth floor, east wing'.
A2.proof: Under it, a small sign said: 'Sixth floor, east wing'.
A2.q: Why is the direction of the steam important?
o: The steam shows that the tower is very cold.
The wind is too strong to work on the roof.
The steam will damage the hospital roof.
The air from the tower may enter the sixth floor east wing.
A2.hint: Buharın nereye gittiğine ve metal kutunun üzerindeki tabelaya bak.
A2.why: Kuleden yükselen buhar rüzgârla altıncı kat doğu kanadının hava girişine gidiyor; yani kulenin havası o kanada girebilir.

text: At midnight Ayo decided to see the hospital roof for herself. She took the fire stairs, because Mr. Garrow's office was next to the lift. The stairwell was dark and cold, and every step echoed.

At the top she pushed open a heavy metal door, and the wind hit her face. In front of her stood a large grey structure, as tall as a house, making a low rattling sound. It was the cooling tower, the machine that keeps the building's air conditioning from overheating.
She walked closer with her torch. Water was trickling down inside the tower, and at the bottom there was a pool. It wasn't clear. It was green, thick and slippery, with a film on top.
A faint mist rose from the tower. It was almost invisible, but the torch beam made it glitter. The wind was carrying it steadily to the left.
Ayo followed the mist with her light. On the left, set into the wall, was a large metal grille. It was an air intake. Beneath it a small sign read: 'Sixth floor, east wing'.
B1.proof: The wind was carrying it steadily to the left.
B1.q: What is the connection between the mist and the sixth floor?
o: The wind blows mist from the tower into the air intake of that wing.
The mist is produced by the sixth floor bathrooms.
The mist comes from the kitchen on the roof.
The mist shows that the tower is broken.
B1.hint: Rüzgâr sisi nereye taşıyor ve tabela ne diyor?
B1.why: Rüzgâr kuleden çıkan sisi doğrudan altıncı kat doğu kanadının hava girişine taşıyor. Bu, damlacıkların binaya girebileceğini düşündürüyor.

text: At midnight Ayo decided to see the hospital roof for herself. She took the fire stairs, because Mr. Garrow's office was next to the lift. The stairwell was dark and cold, and every step echoed.

At the top she pushed open a heavy metal door, and the wind hit her face. In front of her stood a large grey structure, as tall as a house, making a low rattling sound. It was the cooling tower, the machine that stops the building's air conditioning from overheating.

She walked closer with her torch. Water was trickling down inside the tower, and at the bottom there was a pool. It wasn't clear. It was green, thick and slippery, covered with a film that the beam turned to oil.
A faint mist rose from the tower. It was almost invisible, but the torch made it glitter like fine glass. The wind was carrying it steadily to the left.

Ayo followed the mist with her light. On the left, set into the wall, was a large metal grille. It was an air intake. Beneath it a small sign read: 'Sixth floor, east wing'. She remembered the rattling sound she had heard beneath the board three nights before, and suddenly she understood that she had been hearing the hospital breathe.
B2.proof: she had been hearing the hospital breathe
B2.q: What does the final sentence mean?
o: Ayo imagines that the hospital is alive.
The rattling sound was part of the same system that moves air through the building.
The patients were breathing loudly.
The cooling tower was making music.
B2.hint: Ayo'nun duyduğu 'çıngırtı' sesi neyin parçası?
B2.why: Ayo, bir önceki gece duyduğu sesin binadaki havayı taşıyan sistemin parçası olduğunu anlıyor; 'hastanenin nefes alması' bunu anlatıyor.

text: At midnight Ayo decided to see the hospital roof for herself. She took the fire stairs, because Mr. Garrow's office was next to the lift and she had no wish to explain herself. The stairwell was dark and cold, and every step echoed.

At the top she pushed open a heavy metal door, and the wind hit her face. In front of her stood a large grey structure, as tall as a house, making a low rattling sound. It was the cooling tower, the machine that stops the building's air conditioning from overheating.

She walked closer with her torch. Water was trickling down inside the tower, and at the bottom there was a pool. It wasn't clear. It was green, thick and slippery, covered with a film that the beam turned to oil.
A faint mist rose from the tower. It was almost invisible, but the torch made it glitter like fine glass. The wind was carrying it steadily to the left.

Ayo followed the mist with her light. On the left, set into the wall, was a large metal grille. It was an air intake. Beneath it a small sign read: 'Sixth floor, east wing'. She remembered the low, rhythmic rattle she had heard beneath the board three nights earlier, and suddenly she understood that she had been listening to the building breathe, and that it had been breathing in whatever the tower exhaled.
C1.proof: it had been breathing in whatever the tower exhaled
C1.q: What hypothesis does Ayo form at the end of the passage?
o: That the roof door was left open by accident.
That the cooling tower is too noisy for patients.
That droplets from the dirty tower water are drawn into the building's air supply.
That the green water is a sign of good maintenance.
C1.hint: 'Kulenin soluduğunu bina içine çekiyordu' cümlesi bir bulaş yolu hakkında ne söylüyor?
C1.why: Ayo, kirli kule suyundan çıkan damlacıkların hava girişiyle binanın içine çekildiğini düşünüyor; bu, hastalığın olası bulaş yolu.

eps.title: The Book Nobody Opens
eps.recap: Ayo, havalandırma odasında üstünde toz olan, kimsenin açmadığı bir bakım defteri buldu. Defterin kapağında 'Çıkarmayın – G.' yazıyordu.

text: After the roof, Ayo went to the ventilation room on the sixth floor. It was a small room full of pipes, boxes and wires. It was hot and noisy. Nobody came here except the workers, and the workers came only in the day.
She shone her torch around the room. There was a fire extinguisher on the wall. There was a broken chair. Behind the extinguisher, in a dark corner, she saw the edge of a thick black book.
She pulled it out. The cover was covered with dust. Ayo cleaned it with her sleeve. There was a title in white letters: 'Maintenance Log: Water and Cooling'.
Below the title, someone had written on a small paper label with blue pen: 'Do not remove. G.'
Ayo held the book. The letter G was not a name. But in this hospital, there was only one person with a name beginning with G who looked after the pipes.
A2.q: What does the label on the book suggest?
o: Mr. Garrow wanted the book to stay in that room.
A patient left the book there by mistake.
The book is a gift for Ayo.
The book belongs to a worker called George.
A2.hint: 'G.' harfi ve 'çıkarmayın' notu birlikte kimi gösteriyor?
A2.why: Defterin üzerindeki 'G.' harfi, borulardan sorumlu Garrow'a işaret ediyor; defterin o odada kalmasını o istemiş olabilir.

text: After the roof Ayo went to the ventilation room on the sixth floor, a small, hot, noisy room full of pipes, boxes and cables. Nobody came here except maintenance workers, and the workers came only in the daytime.

She swept her torch around the room. There was a fire extinguisher on the wall, and a broken chair in the corner. Behind the extinguisher, in the darkest corner of all, she saw the edge of a thick black book.
She pulled it out. The cover was grey with dust, and she wiped it with her sleeve. White letters spelled out a title: 'Maintenance Log: Water and Cooling'.
Below the title someone had stuck a small paper label and written on it in blue ink: 'Do not remove. G.'
Ayo held the heavy book in both hands. The label did not give a full name. But in the whole hospital there was only one person whose name began with G, and whose job was to look after the pipes.
B1.proof: whose job was to look after the pipes
B1.q: How does Ayo identify the person behind the label?
o: By recognising his handwriting.
By combining the letter G with the person responsible for the pipes.
By finding his name in the book.
By asking the workers in the ventilation room.
B1.hint: Sadece 'G.' harfi var; Ayo kimi nasıl tahmin ediyor?
B1.why: Etiket yalnızca 'G.' diyor ama hastanede boruların bakımından sorumlu ve adı G ile başlayan tek kişi Garrow; Ayo iki bilgiyi birleştiriyor.

text: After the roof Ayo went to the ventilation room on the sixth floor, a small, hot, noisy room full of pipes, boxes and cables. Nobody came here except maintenance workers, and the workers came only in the daytime.

She swept her torch around the room. There was a fire extinguisher on the wall, and a broken chair in the corner. Behind the extinguisher, in the darkest corner of all, she saw the edge of a thick black book.

She pulled it out. The cover was grey with dust, and she wiped it with her sleeve. White letters spelled out a title: 'Maintenance Log: Water and Cooling'. It was exactly the kind of book that a hospital is legally required to keep, and exactly the kind of book that nobody expects to be read.
Below the title someone had stuck a small paper label and written on it in blue ink: 'Do not remove. G.'

Ayo held the heavy book in both hands. The label did not give a full name. But in the whole hospital there was only one person whose name began with G, and whose job was to look after the pipes. She noticed that the dust on the cover was thicker than the dust on the shelf, which meant that the book had been put there carefully, and left.
B2.proof: the book had been put there carefully, and left
B2.q: What does the dust on the book tell Ayo?
o: That the room is not cleaned by anyone.
That the book is very old and worthless.
That someone hid the book deliberately and nobody has touched it since.
That Ayo is the first person to enter the room.
B2.hint: Defterin üzerindeki tozun rafınkinden fazla olması neyi gösterir?
B2.why: Defterin üzerinde raftakinden daha fazla toz var; bu, defterin kasıtlı olarak konduğunu ve sonra kimsenin dokunmadığını gösteriyor.

text: After the roof Ayo went to the ventilation room on the sixth floor, a small, hot, noisy room full of pipes, boxes and cables. Nobody came here except maintenance workers, and the workers came only in the daytime, when the hum of the machines drowned out any conversation.

She swept her torch around the room. There was a fire extinguisher on the wall, and a broken chair in the corner. Behind the extinguisher, in the darkest corner of all, she saw the edge of a thick black book.

She pulled it out. The cover was grey with dust, and she wiped it with her sleeve. White letters spelled out a title: 'Maintenance Log: Water and Cooling'. It was exactly the kind of book a hospital is legally required to keep, and exactly the kind that nobody expects anyone to read.
Below the title someone had stuck a small paper label and written on it in blue ink: 'Do not remove. G.'

Ayo held the heavy book in both hands. The label did not give a full name. But in the whole hospital there was only one person whose name began with G, and whose job was to look after the pipes. She noticed that the dust on the cover was thicker than the dust on the shelf beside it, which meant that the book had been placed there carefully and then left alone, as a man might leave a letter he hoped would never be opened. She turned to the last page. Her hands were not quite steady.
C1.proof: as a man might leave a letter he hoped would never be opened
C1.q: What does the comparison to a letter suggest?
o: That the book is a love letter.
That the book was written for the patients.
That the hospital wants everyone to read it.
That the person who hid the book feared what it contained.
C1.hint: Hiç açılmasını istemediği bir mektup bırakan kişi neyden korkuyor olabilir?
C1.why: Karşılaştırma, defteri saklayan kişinin içindekilerin ortaya çıkmasını istemediğini, yani ondan korktuğunu düşündürüyor.

eps.title: Cold Water, Warm Water
eps.recap: Ayo, gizli bakım defterini açtı ve aylardır süren 'su sıcaklığı düşük' uyarılarını buldu. Soğuk ve ılık su, bakterilerin üremesi için tehlikeli olabilirdi.

text: Ayo sat on the broken chair and opened the black book. The pages were full of small, neat lines. Each line had a date, a short note and a name.

She read the first page. 'March. Water temperature low in the hot pipes of the sixth floor.' She turned the page. 'April. Water temperature low again.' She turned another page. 'May. Low. June. Low. July. Low.'
Her heart was beating fast. Warm water is dangerous when it is not hot enough. It is a perfect home for bacteria. Water that is too cold in a hot pipe stays at the right temperature for them to grow.
She counted the warnings. There were eleven in six months. Eleven times, somebody wrote the same sentence. Eleven times, nothing changed.
Ayo closed her eyes. "The hospital knew," she whispered. "The hospital knew for months."
A2.q: What is the main problem in the book?
o: The book has too many empty pages.
Warnings about low water temperature were written many times but nobody fixed the problem.
The workers wrote with the wrong pen.
The hot water was too hot for patients.
A2.hint: Aynı uyarının on bir kez yazılıp hiçbir şeyin değişmemesi neyi gösterir?
A2.why: Defterde aynı uyarı on bir kez yazılmış ama düzeltme yapılmamış; sorun biliniyordu ve ihmal edildi.

text: Ayo sat down on the broken chair and opened the black book. The pages were full of small, neat lines, each with a date, a short note and a name.
She read the first page. 'March. Water temperature low in the hot pipes, sixth floor.' She turned the page. 'April. Water temperature low again.' Then: 'May. Low. June. Low. July. Low.'

Her heart was beating fast. Warm water that is not hot enough is dangerous. It sits at exactly the temperature at which some bacteria love to multiply, and a hot-water pipe that stays lukewarm becomes a perfect nursery for them.
She counted the warnings: eleven in six months. Eleven times somebody had written almost the same sentence, and eleven times nothing had changed.
Ayo closed her eyes. "They knew," she whispered to the empty room. "The hospital knew for months, and nobody did anything."
B1.proof: eleven in six months
B1.q: What does Ayo understand from the repeated warnings?
o: That the water was too hot for patients.
That the workers wrote the notes by mistake.
That the hospital was aware of the water problem for a long time without acting.
That the book is only a training exercise.
B1.hint: On bir uyarı altı ayda yazılmış; Ayo bundan ne anlıyor?
B1.why: Altı ayda on bir uyarı yazılmış ama düzeltilmemiş; hastane sorunu uzun süredir biliyordu ama harekete geçmedi.

text: Ayo sat down on the broken chair and opened the black book. The pages were full of small, neat lines, each with a date, a short note and a name. Whoever kept this record had been careful, and had expected somebody to act on it.
She read the first page. 'March. Water temperature low in the hot pipes, sixth floor.' She turned the page. 'April. Water temperature low again.' Then: 'May. Low. June. Low. July. Low.'

Her heart was beating fast. Warm water that is not hot enough is dangerous. It sits at exactly the temperature at which certain bacteria love to multiply, and a hot-water pipe that stays lukewarm becomes a perfect nursery for them, while the people at the end of the pipe wash, drink and breathe the mist.
She counted the warnings: eleven in six months. Eleven times somebody had written almost the same sentence, and eleven times nothing had changed.
Ayo closed her eyes. "They knew," she whispered to the empty room. "The hospital knew for months, and nobody did anything."
B2.proof: had expected somebody to act on it
B2.q: What does the phrase about the careful record-keeper show?
o: That the writer was a doctor.
That the writer wanted to hide the book.
That the writer did not understand pipes.
That the person writing the warnings believed someone would respond to them.
B2.hint: Defteri özenle tutan kişi ne bekliyordu?
B2.why: Defteri titizlikle tutan kişi, uyarılara birinin tepki vereceğini bekliyordu; ama kimse bir şey yapmadı.

text: Ayo sat down on the broken chair and opened the black book. The pages were full of small, neat lines, each with a date, a short note and a name. Whoever kept this record had been careful, and had expected somebody to act on it, which made the silence that followed even harder to bear.
She read the first page. 'March. Water temperature low in the hot pipes, sixth floor.' She turned the page. 'April. Water temperature low again.' Then: 'May. Low. June. Low. July. Low.'

Her heart was beating fast. Warm water that is not hot enough is dangerous. It sits at exactly the temperature at which certain bacteria love to multiply, and a hot-water pipe that stays lukewarm becomes a perfect nursery for them, while the people at the end of the pipe wash, drink and breathe the mist without a suspicion in the world.

She counted the warnings: eleven in six months. Eleven times somebody had written almost the same sentence, and eleven times nothing had changed. A mistake happens once. A pattern repeated eleven times is a decision.
Ayo closed her eyes. "They knew," she whispered to the empty room. "The hospital knew for months, and chose to do nothing."
C1.proof: A pattern repeated eleven times is a decision.
C1.q: What is the writer's point in the final lines?
o: That ignoring eleven warnings was a choice, not an accident.
That mistakes are always repeated.
That Ayo made a decision to leave.
That the warnings were written in error.
C1.hint: Aynı şeyin on bir kez tekrarlanması bir hata mı, bir tercih mi?
C1.why: Tek bir hata bir kez olur; on bir kez tekrar eden bir durum bilinçli bir karardır, yani ihmal bir tercihtir.

eps.title: Postponed
eps.recap: Defterdeki her uyarının yanında aynı imza ve 'ertelendi' notu vardı. İmza, tesis müdürü Mr. Garrow'a aitti ve bakım masrafları nedeniyle işler sürekli ileri atılmıştı.

text: Ayo looked at the margin of the book. Next to every warning, there was a second line in blue ink. The handwriting was strong and fast. It said one word: 'Postponed'.
Under the word, there was a short signature: 'J. Garrow'.

She turned pages again and again. March: postponed. April: postponed. May: postponed. There was one more note in June, longer than the others: 'Repair too expensive this quarter. Wait for next budget.'
Ayo put her finger on the words. Mr. Garrow was the facilities manager. He controlled the money for the pipes. He was not stupid. He read every warning. He wrote his name every time.
Behind her, a pipe made a loud noise. Ayo jumped. Then she took out her phone and began to photograph every page.
A2.q: Why did Mr. Garrow write 'Postponed'?
o: He was too busy to read.
He wanted the patients to get sick.
He did not want to spend money on the repair.
He lost the book.
A2.hint: Garrow'un notunda tamiri ertelemesinin nedeni ne?
A2.why: Notta 'tamir bu çeyrekte çok pahalı' yazıyor; Garrow masraf yapmak istemediği için tamiri erteliyor.

text: Ayo looked at the margin of the book. Next to every warning there was a second line in blue ink, written in strong, fast handwriting. It said just one word: 'Postponed'.
Beneath the word was a short signature: 'J. Garrow'.
She turned the pages again and again. March: postponed. April: postponed. May: postponed. In June there was a longer note: 'Repair too expensive this quarter. Wait for next budget.'
Ayo put her finger on the words. Mr. Garrow was the facilities manager and he controlled the money for the pipes. He was not stupid. He had read every warning, and he had signed his name every time.

Behind her a pipe gave a sudden bang and she jumped. Then she took out her phone and began to photograph every single page, in order. She knew that a book can vanish overnight, but a photograph is much harder to destroy.
B1.proof: Wait for next budget.
B1.q: What does the June note show about Mr. Garrow's priorities?
o: That he did not understand the warnings.
That he wanted to help Ayo.
That the repair was already finished.
That he cared more about money than about fixing a dangerous problem.
B1.hint: 'Bir sonraki bütçeyi bekle' notu neyi gösteriyor?
B1.why: Garrow'un güvenlikten çok bütçeye önem verdiğini ve tehlikeli bir sorunun tamirini ertelediğini gösteriyor.

text: Ayo looked at the margin of the book. Next to every warning there was a second line in blue ink, written in strong, fast handwriting. It said just one word: 'Postponed'.
Beneath the word was a short signature: 'J. Garrow'.
She turned the pages again and again. March: postponed. April: postponed. May: postponed. In June there was a longer note: 'Repair too expensive this quarter. Wait for next budget.'

Ayo put her finger on the words. Mr. Garrow was the facilities manager, and he controlled the money for the pipes. He was not stupid, and he was not absent; he had read every warning and signed his name beside it, which meant that the delay was not neglect in the usual sense but a series of deliberate signatures.

Behind her a pipe gave a sudden bang and she jumped. Then she took out her phone and began to photograph every single page, in order, with the date visible each time. Her hands were cold, but her mind was perfectly clear, and she already knew whom she would show them to.
B2.proof: a series of deliberate signatures
B2.q: What distinction does the writer draw?
o: Between simple neglect and repeated, knowing decisions to postpone.
Between day and night shifts.
Between pipes and wires.
Between Ayo and the workers.
B2.hint: Unutmak ile imzalayarak ertelemek arasındaki fark nedir?
B2.why: Garrow'un her seferinde imzalayarak ertelemesi, bunun unutkanlık değil bilinçli bir tercih olduğunu gösteriyor.

text: Ayo looked at the margin of the book. Next to every warning there was a second line in blue ink, written in strong, fast handwriting. It said just one word: 'Postponed'.
Beneath the word was a short signature: 'J. Garrow'.
She turned the pages again and again. March: postponed. April: postponed. May: postponed. In June there was a longer note: 'Repair too expensive this quarter. Wait for next budget.'

Ayo put her finger on the words. Mr. Garrow was the facilities manager, and he controlled the money for the pipes. He was not stupid, and he was not absent; he had read every warning and signed his name beside it, which meant that the delay was not neglect in the usual sense but a series of deliberate signatures. Each one, taken alone, looked like a sensible man balancing a budget. Together they looked like something else.

Behind her a pipe gave a sudden bang and she jumped. Then she took out her phone and began to photograph every single page, in order, with the date visible each time, because she knew that a book can disappear but a photograph is harder to burn. In the dark little room, with the pipes humming around her, she felt for the first time that she was no longer alone with what she knew.
C1.proof: Together they looked like something else.
C1.q: What does the author suggest by this sentence?
o: That the signatures were forged.
That the individual decisions seemed reasonable but formed a pattern of serious negligence.
That Mr. Garrow was a different person each time.
That the budget had been balanced successfully.
C1.hint: Tek tek makul görünen kararlar bir araya gelince neye dönüşüyor?
C1.why: Her imza tek başına bütçeyi dengeleyen makul bir yönetici gibi görünüyor; ama hepsi birlikte ciddi bir ihmal örüntüsü oluşturuyor.

eps.title: A Private Test
eps.recap: Ayo fotoğrafladığı sayfaları Pete'e gösterdi. Pete, hastane laboratuvarında yapamadığı Legionella testini özel bir laboratuvardan aldığı bir kitle yaptı ve numunelerle sabaha kadar çalıştı.

text: At six in the morning, Ayo went to Pete's small laboratory in the basement. She showed him the photographs. Pete read them slowly. His face became pale.
"Eleven warnings," he said. "And my bacteria never grew on the normal plates. Ayo, I think I know why. Some bacteria need a special plate. I can get one."
He took out his phone and made a call. Forty minutes later, a young man brought a small box to the back door. Pete signed a paper, and paid with his own money.

Inside the box there was a special test kit for a bacterium called Legionella. Pete put on his gloves. He took water samples that Ayo brought from the sixth floor. He worked all morning. He did not eat. He did not speak.
At noon he put the plate in a warm machine and looked at Ayo. "Now we must wait," he said. "Three days for the real result. But this fast test... it takes only two hours."
A2.q: Why does this detail about Pete matter?
o: It shows that the hospital pays for everything.
It shows that Pete is very rich.
It shows that the young man is a thief.
It shows that Pete is ready to take personal risks to find the truth.
A2.hint: Pete testi neden kendi parasıyla aldı?
A2.why: Pete hastaneden izin veya para beklemeden, gerçeği bulmak için kişisel risk alıyor; kendi parasıyla ödeme bunu gösteriyor.

text: At six in the morning Ayo went to Pete's small laboratory in the basement and showed him the photographs. Pete read them slowly, and his face turned pale.
"Eleven warnings," he said. "And my bacteria never grew on the normal plates. Ayo, I think I understand now. Some bacteria need a special plate and special food. I can get a kit."
He made a phone call. Forty minutes later a young man brought a small box to the back door, and Pete signed for it and paid with his own money, without telling the hospital.

Inside was a test kit for a bacterium called Legionella. Pete put on his gloves and tested the water samples that Ayo had collected from the sixth floor. He worked all morning without eating or speaking.
At noon he put the first plate into a warm machine and looked up. "The full culture takes days," he said. "But this rapid test only takes two hours. We will know tonight."
B1.proof: without telling the hospital
B1.q: Why does Pete not tell the hospital about the kit?
o: He suspects that the hospital management does not want the truth to come out.
He is shy and does not like talking.
He is not allowed to use phones at work.
The kit is a gift from the hospital.
B1.hint: Pete testi hastaneye söylemeden neden yaptı?
B1.why: Pete, yönetimin gerçeğin ortaya çıkmasını istemeyebileceğinden şüpheleniyor; bu yüzden hastaneye haber vermiyor.

text: At six in the morning Ayo went to Pete's small laboratory in the basement and showed him the photographs. Pete read them slowly, and his face turned pale.

"Eleven warnings," he said. "And my bacteria never grew on the normal plates. Ayo, I think I understand now. Some bacteria need a special plate and special food. I can get a kit, but it won't come through the hospital."

He made a phone call. Forty minutes later a young man brought a small box to the back door, and Pete signed for it and paid with his own money, without telling the hospital. A purchase order would have passed through the facilities office, and the facilities office was precisely the place they could no longer trust.

Inside was a test kit for a bacterium called Legionella. Pete put on his gloves and tested the water samples that Ayo had collected from the sixth floor. He worked all morning without eating or speaking.
At noon he put the first plate into a warm machine and looked up. "The full culture takes days," he said. "But this rapid test only takes two hours. We will know tonight."
B2.proof: the facilities office was precisely the place they could no longer trust
B2.q: Why did Pete avoid the official ordering process?
o: Because the process was too fast.
Because the order would have gone through the office of the person they suspected.
Because the kit was free.
Because Ayo forbade him.
B2.hint: Resmî sipariş yolu neden güvenilir değildi?
B2.why: Sipariş tesis ofisinden geçecekti ve şüphelenilen kişi orada çalışıyordu; bu yüzden Pete resmî yolu kullanmadı.

text: At six in the morning Ayo went to Pete's small laboratory in the basement and showed him the photographs. Pete read them slowly, and his face turned pale.

"Eleven warnings," he said. "And my bacteria never grew on the normal plates. Ayo, I think I understand now. Some bacteria need a special plate and special food. I can get a kit, but it won't come through the hospital."

He made a phone call. Forty minutes later a young man brought a small box to the back door, and Pete signed for it and paid with his own money, without telling the hospital. A purchase order would have passed through the facilities office, and the facilities office was precisely the place they could no longer trust. It was an odd feeling for a scientist, he said, to conduct an experiment in secret from the people who owned the building.

Inside was a test kit for a bacterium called Legionella. Pete put on his gloves and tested the water samples that Ayo had collected from the sixth floor. He worked all morning without eating or speaking, and Ayo noticed that his hands, usually so quick, moved with a kind of reverence.

At noon he put the first plate into a warm machine and looked up. "The full culture takes days," he said. "But this rapid test only takes two hours. We will know tonight, Ayo, and after that nothing will be the same."
C1.proof: to conduct an experiment in secret from the people who owned the building
C1.q: What does Pete's remark reveal about the situation?
o: That Pete enjoys secrets.
That the building owner asked for an experiment.
That the staff must hide their work from the hospital's own management.
That experiments are forbidden in hospitals.
C1.hint: Pete'in 'bina sahiplerinden gizli deney' sözü ne anlatıyor?
C1.why: Laboratuvar çalışanlarının, hastane yönetiminden saklanarak çalışmak zorunda kaldığını gösteriyor.

eps.title: A Faulty Sample
eps.recap: Hızlı test, 6. kat musluğundan alınan suda Legionella'nın pozitif olduğunu gösterdi. Ayo sonucu Mr. Garrow'a götürdü; Garrow numunenin 'hatalı' olduğunu ve laboratuvarın yanıldığını söyledi.

text: That evening, Pete called Ayo to the basement. He did not say a word. He gave her a small paper with a result. On the paper, there was one word in red: 'POSITIVE'.
"Legionella," said Pete quietly. "It is in the water from the sixth floor. A lot of it."
Ayo took a deep breath. She felt two things at the same time: relief, because now she knew, and fear, because it was true. "We must tell Mr. Garrow," she said. "Now."
They went to his office on the top floor. Mr. Garrow listened with a hard face. He looked at the paper. He did not touch it.
"A faulty sample," he said. "Your machine is wrong, Pete. Test again with proper equipment. And please, do not tell the patients. Not yet."
A2.q: How does Mr. Garrow react to the result?
o: He refuses to accept it and tells them not to speak to patients.
He thanks them and closes the sixth floor.
He calls the police to protect Pete.
He is happy because it is good news.
A2.hint: Garrow pozitif sonuca nasıl karşılık veriyor?
A2.why: Garrow sonucu kabul etmiyor, 'hatalı örnek' diyor ve hastalara söylememelerini istiyor.

text: That evening Pete called Ayo down to the basement. He did not say a word. He simply handed her a small slip of paper with a result printed on it, and one word in red: 'POSITIVE'.
"Legionella," said Pete quietly. "It's in the water from the sixth floor. A lot of it."
Ayo took a deep breath. She felt two things at once: relief, because at last she knew, and fear, because it was true. "We have to tell Mr. Garrow," she said. "Right now."
They went up to his office on the top floor. Mr. Garrow listened with a hard face. He looked at the slip but did not touch it.

"A faulty sample," he said. "Your equipment is wrong, Pete. Test again with proper equipment. And please, say nothing to the patients. Not yet." He then looked at the clock, as if the meeting was already finished.
B1.proof: Not yet.
B1.q: What do Mr. Garrow's last words suggest?
o: That he will tell the patients tomorrow morning.
That he wants to delay telling the patients to protect himself.
That he is waiting for the real test result.
That he does not understand the problem.
B1.hint: 'Henüz değil' sözü Garrow'un ne istediğini gösteriyor?
B1.why: Garrow hastalara söylemeyi ertelemek istiyor; muhtemelen kendini korumak ve zaman kazanmak için.

text: That evening Pete called Ayo down to the basement. He did not say a word. He simply handed her a small slip of paper with a result printed on it, and one word in red: 'POSITIVE'.
"Legionella," said Pete quietly. "It's in the water from the sixth floor. A lot of it."

Ayo took a deep breath. She felt two things at once: relief, because at last she knew, and fear, because it was true. "We have to tell Mr. Garrow," she said. "Right now." It seemed to her, naively perhaps, that a man who had hidden a problem might be relieved to see it named.
They went up to his office on the top floor. Mr. Garrow listened with a hard face. He looked at the slip but did not touch it, as if the paper itself were infectious.

"A faulty sample," he said. "Your equipment is wrong, Pete. Test again with proper equipment. And please, say nothing to the patients. Not yet." Ayo felt the room become colder, and Pete looked at the floor, and nobody said anything more.
B2.proof: as if the paper itself were infectious
B2.q: What does this comparison show about Mr. Garrow?
o: That he is afraid of getting sick from paper.
That he is a doctor.
That he wants to avoid being connected with the result.
That he plans to frame the paper.
B2.hint: Garrow sonuç kâğıdına neden dokunmak istemiyor, ne düşündürüyor?
B2.why: Kâğıda dokunmamak, sonuçla ilişkilendirilmek istemediğini gösteriyor.

text: That evening Pete called Ayo down to the basement. He did not say a word. He simply handed her a small slip of paper with a result printed on it, and one word in red: 'POSITIVE'.
"Legionella," said Pete quietly. "It's in the water from the sixth floor. A lot of it."

Ayo took a deep breath. She felt two things at once: relief, because at last she knew, and fear, because it was true. "We have to tell Mr. Garrow," she said. "Right now." It seemed to her, naively perhaps, that a man who had hidden a problem might be relieved to see it named.

They went up to his office on the top floor. Mr. Garrow listened with a hard face. He looked at the slip but did not touch it, as if the paper itself were infectious. When he spoke, his voice was calm, and that was the worst part.

"A faulty sample," he said. "Your equipment is wrong, Pete. Test again with proper equipment. And please, say nothing to the patients. Not yet." Ayo realised that he had not asked a single question about the patients' condition, or about where the bacteria might have come from. He had only asked for silence.
C1.proof: He had only asked for silence.
C1.q: What does Ayo notice about Mr. Garrow's reaction?
o: That he asked many questions about the cause.
That he wanted to visit the sixth floor.
That he shouted at her.
That he showed no concern for the patients and was interested only in secrecy.
C1.hint: Garrow hangi soruyu sormadı, yalnızca neyi istedi?
C1.why: Garrow hastaların durumu veya nedeni hakkında hiç soru sormuyor; yalnızca sessiz kalınmasını istiyor.

eps.title: The Wrong Number
eps.recap: Ayo halk sağlığı birimini aradı ama telefonda yalnızca sıradan bir memura ulaştı. Memur, yazılı bir şikâyet formunun gönderilmesini ve haftalarca beklenmesini söyledi.

text: It was almost midnight. Ayo sat in the corridor on a cold plastic chair. She had Pete's paper in one hand and her phone in the other. She called the Public Health Office.
A woman answered after eight rings. She sounded tired. "Public Health. Office hours are nine to five."
"This is an emergency," said Ayo. "Several patients have a dangerous bacteria in their lungs. I think it is in the water of the hospital."
"Do you have an official test from an approved laboratory?" asked the woman. "No," said Ayo. "Not yet. But..." "Then please fill in a complaint form on our website. We answer in two or three weeks."
Ayo put down the phone. Two or three weeks. In that time, how many new people would come to the sixth floor?
A2.proof: We answer in two or three weeks.
A2.q: Why is the phone call not useful?
o: The woman was very rude and shouted.
The office is too slow and asks for official proof Ayo does not have.
Ayo called the wrong hospital.
The office promised to come immediately.
A2.hint: Telefondaki görüşme Ayo'ya neden yardımcı olmuyor?
A2.why: Ofis çok yavaş cevap veriyor ve Ayo'nun henüz sahip olmadığı resmî bir test sonucu istiyor.

text: It was almost midnight. Ayo sat in the corridor on a cold plastic chair, holding Pete's slip of paper in one hand and her phone in the other. She dialled the Public Health Office.
A woman answered after eight rings. She sounded exhausted. "Public Health. Office hours are nine to five."
"This is an emergency," said Ayo. "Several patients have a dangerous bacterial infection of the lungs. I believe the source is the water in our hospital."
"Do you have an official result from an approved laboratory?" asked the woman. "Not yet. But..." "Then please complete a complaint form on our website. We respond within two or three weeks."

Ayo lowered the phone. Two or three weeks. In that time, how many more people would be admitted to the sixth floor? She stared at the dark corridor for a long minute, and then she stood up, because she knew that waiting politely would not help anyone.
B1.proof: We respond within two or three weeks.
B1.q: What worries Ayo at the end of the call?
o: That the woman was tired.
That the website is broken.
That new patients may become infected while the office is slow.
That she forgot her phone number.
B1.hint: Telefon görüşmesinin sonunda Ayo'yu en çok ne endişelendiriyor?
B1.why: Ofis iki üç hafta içinde yanıt verecek; o sürede yeni hastalar da enfekte olabilir.

text: It was almost midnight. Ayo sat in the corridor on a cold plastic chair, holding Pete's slip of paper in one hand and her phone in the other. She dialled the Public Health Office.
A woman answered after eight rings. She sounded exhausted. "Public Health. Office hours are nine to five."
"This is an emergency," said Ayo. "Several patients have a dangerous bacterial infection of the lungs. I believe the source is the water in our hospital, and the hospital's management knows it."

"Do you have an official result from an approved laboratory?" asked the woman, in the careful voice of someone reading from a script. "Not yet. But..." "Then please complete a complaint form on our website. We respond within two or three weeks."

Ayo lowered the phone. Two or three weeks. In that time, how many more people would be admitted to the sixth floor? She realised that the system built to protect the public had been designed for problems that arrive politely and wait their turn. It was a good system, she thought, for a different kind of night. She stood up and began to walk, because she had to do something.
B2.proof: problems that arrive politely and wait their turn
B2.q: What criticism does the final sentence make?
o: That the patients are impolite.
That Ayo should be more polite.
That emergencies never happen.
That the health system is too slow and rigid for a real emergency.
B2.hint: Sistemin 'kibarca gelip sırasını bekleyen sorunlar' için tasarlanmış olması neyi eleştiriyor?
B2.why: Sistemin yavaş ve katı olduğunu, gerçek bir acil durum için yeterince hızlı çalışmadığını eleştiriyor.

text: It was almost midnight. Ayo sat in the corridor on a cold plastic chair, holding Pete's slip of paper in one hand and her phone in the other. She dialled the Public Health Office.
A woman answered after eight rings. She sounded exhausted. "Public Health. Office hours are nine to five."
"This is an emergency," said Ayo. "Several patients have a dangerous bacterial infection of the lungs. I believe the source is the water in our hospital, and the hospital's management knows it."

"Do you have an official result from an approved laboratory?" asked the woman, in the careful voice of someone reading from a script. "Not yet. But..." "Then please complete a complaint form on our website. We respond within two or three weeks."

Ayo lowered the phone. Two or three weeks. In that time, how many more people would be admitted to the sixth floor? She realised that the system built to protect the public had been designed for problems that arrive politely and wait their turn, whereas this one was growing in the dark, at body temperature, and had no intention of waiting for anybody's paperwork. She put the phone in her pocket, wiped her eyes with the back of her hand, and decided that if the official door was closed, she would simply have to find a window.
C1.proof: had no intention of waiting for anybody's paperwork
C1.q: What contrast does the author draw?
o: Between slow bureaucratic procedure and a fast-growing, urgent danger.
Between day and night.
Between Ayo and Pete.
Between water and paper.
C1.hint: Bürokrasi ile bakterinin hızı arasındaki fark nedir?
C1.why: Bürokratik süreç yavaş ilerlerken tehlike hızla büyüyor; yazar bu iki hız arasındaki uyumsuzluğu vurguluyor.

eps.title: Forty Degrees
eps.recap: Rosa'nın kızı Lina, hastaneye getirildi; ateşi 40 dereceydi ve doktorlar Legionella'dan şüphelendi. Ayo'nun elindeki tek kanıt Pete'in testi ve defterin fotoğraflarıydı.

text: At three in the morning, the doors of the emergency room opened. Rosa came in. She was carrying her daughter, Lina. Lina was nine years old. Her face was red. Her eyes were closed.
"She cannot breathe well," said Rosa. Her voice was shaking. "She has had a fever for two days. Ayo, please!"
Ayo put her hand on the girl's head. It was burning. She took a thermometer. She looked at the number and her stomach fell. It said: 40.1.
She remembered the east bathroom on the sixth floor. Rosa had told her that Lina washed her hands there last week. Ayo looked at Rosa. Rosa looked at Ayo. Neither of them spoke.
"Take her to the bed," said Ayo at last. "I am here. I will not leave her."
A2.q: What does the thermometer reading show?
o: That Lina is healthy and just tired.
That the thermometer is broken.
That Lina has a very high fever and may have the same illness as the other patients.
That Rosa has a fever.
A2.hint: Lina'nın ateşinin 40.1 olması Ayo için ne anlama geliyor?
A2.why: Çok yüksek ateş ve altıncı kattaki banyo bilgisiyle Lina'nın diğer hastalarla aynı hastalığa yakalanmış olabileceğini gösteriyor.

text: At three in the morning the doors of the emergency room swung open. Rosa came in, carrying her daughter Lina in her arms. Lina was nine years old. Her face was red and her eyes were closed.
"She can't breathe properly," said Rosa, her voice shaking. "She's had a fever for two days. Ayo, please!"
Ayo laid a hand on the girl's forehead. It was burning. She took out a thermometer, looked at the number, and felt her stomach drop. It read 40.1.
She remembered the east-end bathroom on the sixth floor. Rosa had told her that Lina washed her hands there last week. Ayo looked at Rosa, and Rosa looked at Ayo. Neither of them spoke.
"Put her on that bed," said Ayo at last. "I'm here. I'm not leaving her side." Rosa nodded, and tears ran down her face, but she did not make a sound.
B1.proof: Neither of them spoke.
B1.q: Why do Ayo and Rosa stay silent?
o: They are angry at each other.
They are too tired to speak.
They do not know each other.
They both realise that Lina may have caught the infection at the hospital.
B1.hint: İki kadın neden sessiz kalıyor?
B1.why: İkisi de Lina'nın bakteriyi hastanedeki banyodan almış olabileceğini fark ediyor.

text: At three in the morning the doors of the emergency room swung open. Rosa came in, carrying her daughter Lina in her arms. Lina was nine years old. Her face was red and her eyes were closed, and her small hands hung limply at her sides.
"She can't breathe properly," said Rosa, her voice shaking. "She's had a fever for two days. Ayo, please!"
Ayo laid a hand on the girl's forehead. It was burning. She took out a thermometer, looked at the number, and felt her stomach drop. It read 40.1.

eps.title: The Right Medicine
eps.recap: Ayo, Legionella şüphesiyle Lina'nın antibiyotiğini değiştirdi. Ertesi sabah kızın ateşi düştü ve nefes alışı rahatladı. Diğer hastalar için de aynı tedavi başlatıldı.

text: Ayo did not sleep. She sat next to Lina's bed. The little girl was hot and small and very quiet. Rosa stood at the window and did not speak.
Ayo looked at the paper with Pete's result in her hand. "Legionella," she said softly. "The usual medicine does not work for this bacteria. I need a different one."
She wrote a new order for the nurse. The nurse looked at it, then at Ayo. "This is not what we give for pneumonia," she said. "I know," said Ayo. "Please give it now."
At six in the morning, Lina opened her eyes. "Mama," she said. "I am thirsty." Rosa ran to the bed and laughed and cried at the same time.
Ayo checked the thermometer: 37.8. The fever was going down. She smiled for the first time in three days.
A2.q: Why did Ayo change the medicine?
o: Lina did not like the taste.
The nurse asked her to.
The hospital had no more medicine.
The usual medicine does not work against Legionella bacteria.
A2.hint: Ayo ilacı bu şekilde neden değiştirdi?
A2.why: Alışılmış ilaç Legionella'ya karşı etkili değil; Ayo bakteriye uygun bir antibiyotik seçti.

text: Ayo did not sleep that night. She sat beside Lina's bed, watching the small, flushed face on the pillow. Rosa stood at the window and did not say a word.

text: Ayo did not sleep that night. She sat beside Lina's bed, watching the small, flushed face on the pillow. Rosa stood at the window and did not say a word, because there was nothing in the world she could say.

Ayo looked at the slip with Pete's result. "Legionella," she said softly. "The usual antibiotics don't work well against it. I need a different one." It was a risky decision, since she had no official confirmation and no signed permission from anyone, but she had decided that a diagnosis was only worth as much as the courage to act on it.
She wrote a new order for the nurse. The nurse looked at it, then at Ayo. "This isn't what we give for pneumonia," she said. "I know," said Ayo. "Please give it now."

Ayo checked the thermometer: 37.8. The fever was falling. She smiled for the first time in three days, and then she remembered that five other patients were still waiting for the same medicine.

o: That diagnoses are always wrong.
That a correct diagnosis is useful only if the doctor dares to treat accordingly.

That courage is not needed.
B2.hint: Ayo tanı konusunda neye inanıyor?
B2.why: Doğru bir tanı, ancak doktor ona göre cesaretle tedavi başlatırsa işe yarar.

text: Ayo did not sleep that night. She sat beside Lina's bed, watching the small, flushed face on the pillow. Rosa stood at the window and did not say a word, because there was nothing in the world she could say.

Ayo looked at the slip with Pete's result. "Legionella," she said softly. "The usual antibiotics don't work well against it. I need a different one." She wrote a new order for the nurse. The nurse looked at it, then at Ayo. "This isn't what we give for pneumonia," she said. "I know," said Ayo. "Please give it now. If I'm wrong, the responsibility is mine alone."
At six in the morning Lina opened her eyes. "Mama," she whispered. "I'm thirsty." Rosa ran to the bed, laughing and crying at once.

Ayo checked the thermometer: 37.8. The fever was falling. eps.title: Off the Night Shift
eps.recap: Lina iyileşirken Mr. Garrow, Ayo'nun 'izinsiz laboratuvar testi yaptırdığı ve hastane kurallarını çiğnediği' gerekçesiyle onu nöbetten uzaklaştırdı. Ayo'dan kimlik kartını teslim etmesi istendi.

text: At nine in the morning, Ayo was called to the manager's office. It was large and bright. Mr. Garrow sat behind a big desk. Next to him stood a woman from the personnel department.
"Dr. Bennett," said Mr. Garrow. "We have a problem. You ordered a private test without permission. You touched hospital water. You scared the nurses. These are serious things."
"I saved a child," said Ayo. "Lina is alive because of that test."
"That is not important," said Mr. Garrow. "The rules are important. From today, you are not allowed to work on the night shift. Please give your card to Mrs. Prior."
Ayo looked at the card in her hand. Her name was on it. Her photo. She put it on the desk slowly. She did not cry. She was too angry for that.
A2.q: Why does Mr. Garrow remove Ayo from work?
o: He uses the rules as an excuse to stop her investigation.
He wants to give her a holiday.
He wants to promote her.
He is angry because Lina is alive.
A2.hint: Garrow Ayo'yu neden nöbetten uzaklaştırıyor?
A2.why: Kuralları bahane ederek Ayo'nun araştırmasını durdurmak istiyor.

eps.title: A Floor Plan and a Copy
eps.recap: Ayo uzaklaştırıldıktan sonra Pete bütün kanıtların kopyasını aldı. Rosa ise gizlice kat planını getirdi; plan, soğutma kulesinden gelen su borusunun 6. katın doğu ucuna nasıl ulaştığını gösteriyordu.

text: At noon, Ayo sat in her small car in the hospital car park. She had no pass, no job for tonight, and no plan. Then somebody knocked on the window. It was Pete, with a big paper bag in his hand.
"I copied everything," he said quickly. "The photographs, the test results, the notes. Three copies. One for you, one for me, one in my mother's kitchen."
Ayo smiled. A second knock. It was Rosa. She had a long roll of paper under her arm. "The floor plan of the building," she whispered. "I took it from the engineering room. Nobody saw me."
They unrolled the plan on the back seat. Rosa put her finger on a thick blue line. It came from the cooling tower on the roof, and went down to the sixth floor. It stopped at the east end.
"That is the line," said Rosa. "All the dirty water goes to the bathrooms at the east end. It is the same place where Lina washed her hands."
A2.q: Why did Pete make three copies?
o: To give them as presents.
To protect the evidence in case someone tries to destroy it.
To sell them.
Because he likes photocopies.
A2.hint: Pete kanıtların neden üç kopyasını yaptı?
A2.why: Biri kanıtı yok etmeye çalışırsa diye; kopyaları farklı yerlerde saklayarak onu güvene alıyor.

text: At noon Ayo sat in her small car in the hospital car park. She had no pass, no shift for the night, and no plan. Then somebody tapped on the window. It was Pete, carrying a large paper bag.

text: At noon Ayo sat in her small car in the hospital car park. She had no pass, no shift for the night, and no plan. Then somebody tapped on the window. It was Pete, carrying a large paper bag and looking over his shoulder like a bad spy.

eps.title: The Inspector
eps.recap: Ayo'nun kamu sağlığı birimine gönderdiği yazılı şikâyet bir müfettişin dikkatini çekti. Ms. Odell hastaneye geldi ancak Mr. Garrow ona yalnızca 'temiz' görünen bakım dosyalarını gösterdi.

text: On Thursday afternoon, a woman in a grey coat came to the front door of the hospital. She had a leather bag and a badge. The badge said: 'Ms. Odell, Public Health Inspector'.
Pete saw her from the window of the basement laboratory. He ran to find Ayo, who was waiting in the car park. "She is here!" he said. "Somebody read your complaint!"
Mr. Garrow met Ms. Odell at the door. He was smiling. He shook her hand. "Welcome to St. Elm's. Come, please. I have prepared all our maintenance files."
Ms. Odell followed him to a big meeting room. On the table, there were ten neat blue folders. Everything was clean and in order.
"All perfect, as you can see," said Mr. Garrow. Ms. Odell opened one folder. She looked at it for a long time. Then she asked, quietly, "And where is the log for the cooling tower?"
A2.proof: I have prepared all our maintenance files.
A2.q: What is Garrow trying to do?
o: Help the inspector find the truth.
Hide from the inspector.
Show only clean files so the inspector will not find the problem.
Ask the inspector for a job.
A2.hint: Garrow müfettişe dosyaları neden hazırlamış?
A2.why: Yalnızca temiz görünen dosyaları göstererek müfettişin sorunu bulmasını engellemek istiyor.

text: On Thursday afternoon a woman in a grey coat came to the front door of the hospital. She carried a leather bag and a badge that read: 'Ms. Odell, Public Health Inspector'.

B1.why: Düzenli dosyalar arasında soğutma kulesi kaydının eksik olduğunu fark ettiğini gösteriyor.

text: On Thursday afternoon a woman in a grey coat came to the front door of the hospital. She carried a leather bag and a badge that read: 'Ms. Odell, Public Health Inspector'.

He said that the cooling tower records were kept elsewhere, and he smiled again, a little too widely. Ms. Odell wrote something in her notebook.

text: On Thursday afternoon a woman in a grey coat came to the front door of the hospital. She carried a leather bag and a badge that read: 'Ms. Odell, Public Health Inspector'.
Pete saw her from the basement window and ran to find Ayo in the car park. "She's here!" he said. "Somebody read your complaint!"
Mr. Garrow met Ms. Odell at the door, smiling, and shook her hand with both of his. "Welcome to St. Elm's. Please come through. I've prepared all our maintenance files for you."

eps.title: The Missing Page
eps.recap: Ayo, Pete ve Rosa kanıt dosyasını Ms. Odell'e teslim etti. Müfettiş defterin fotoğraflarını inceledi ve Mart ayına ait sayfanın eksik olduğunu, yani en kritik uyarının kaldırılmış olabileceğini fark etti.

text: After the meeting, Ayo found Ms. Odell in the corridor. "I am Dr. Bennett," she said. "I wrote the complaint. I have evidence. Can we go somewhere private?"

They went to a small room behind the pharmacy. Ayo opened her bag. She gave Ms. Odell Pete's test, the photographs of the log, and Rosa's floor plan. Ms. Odell read everything in silence. It took forty minutes.

At the end, she put the photographs in a row on the table. "This is a very good case, Dr. Bennett," she said. "But look." She pointed at the date column. "March. April. May. Here. And here. But where is February?"
Ayo looked. She had not noticed before. In the photographs, the first page began in March. But the black book had a torn edge near the front.
"A page is missing," said Ms. Odell. "And I think it was the first one. The first warning."
A2.q: What did Ms. Odell notice?
o: The log is too long.
The photographs are blurry.
The test is expired.
The first page of the log, with the earliest warning, is missing.
A2.hint: Ms. Odell fotoğraflarda neyi fark etti?
A2.why: Defterin ilk sayfası, yani en erken uyarı eksik; sayfa yırtılmış.

text: After the meeting Ayo found Ms. Odell in the corridor. "I'm Dr. Bennett," she said. "I wrote the complaint, and I have evidence. Is there somewhere private we can talk?"

They went to a small room behind the pharmacy. Ayo opened her bag and handed over Pete's test, the photographs of the log, and Rosa's floor plan. Ms. Odell read everything in silence for forty minutes.
At the end she laid the photographs in a row. "This is a strong case, Dr. Bennett," she said. "But look here." She pointed to the date column. "March, April, May. But where is February?"
Ayo looked. She hadn't noticed before. In the photographs the first entry was in March, yet the black book had a ragged edge near the front, where something had been torn out.
"A page is missing," said Ms. Odell. "And I suspect it was the earliest and most damaging one."
B1.proof: the earliest and most damaging one
B1.q: Why is the missing page important?
o: It probably contained the first warning, which would prove the earliest knowledge of the problem.

text: After the meeting Ayo found Ms. Odell in the corridor. "I'm Dr. Bennett," she said. "I wrote the complaint, and I have evidence. Is there somewhere private we can talk?"

eps.title: Ashes in the Fireplace
eps.recap: Ms. Odell, eksik sayfayı aramak için Garrow'un odasında arama izni aldı. Garrow dışarıdayken Rosa odaya girdi ve şöminede yarı yanmış, kenarında 'Şubat' yazan bir kâğıt parçası buldu.

text: On Friday morning, Ms. Odell held a short meeting with the hospital lawyers. She asked for permission to search the manager's office. The lawyers said yes. But they asked her to wait until noon.
At eleven, Rosa was cleaning the corridor near the top floor. She saw that Mr. Garrow was walking toward the car park with his coat on. His office door was open. Nobody was inside.
Rosa's heart was beating fast. She looked left. She looked right. Then she went in.
It was a warm, quiet room with a big desk and an old stone fireplace. The fire was out. She bent down and looked into the dark space. There was a small pile of grey ash.
On top of it, there was a piece of paper. It was half burned. On the edge, she could still read two words in blue ink: 'February... low...'
A2.q: What did Rosa find?
o: A half-burned piece of paper that may be the missing page.
A birthday card.
A new log book.
A key to the cooling tower.
A2.hint: Rosa şöminenin içinde ne buldu burada?
A2.why: Yarı yanmış bir kâğıt parçası; muhtemelen eksik olan sayfa.

eps.title: Official Samples
eps.recap: Rosa'nın bulduğu yanık kâğıdın fotoğrafı Ms. Odell'e ulaştı. Müfettiş resmî numune aldı ve soğutma kulesinin hemen kapatılmasını emretti. Temizlik ekipleri çatıya çıktı.

text: Rosa did not touch the burned paper. She took photographs from three sides and ran to Ms. Odell. Ms. Odell came to the manager's office with two police officers and a man from the hospital's lawyers.
Mr. Garrow was already back. When he saw the people in the door, he opened his mouth. But he said nothing.
The police officer put the half-burned paper into a plastic bag. Ms. Odell wrote the time and the date on the bag. "This is now evidence," she said.
That afternoon, Ms. Odell went to the roof with a team in white clothes. They took water from the cooling tower in twelve small bottles. The water was green and had a bad smell.
"Close the tower," she said. "Now. Nobody may use the water on the sixth floor until I say so."

To go on holiday.

eps.title: The Contractor's Copy
eps.recap: Ms. Odell, yırtılan Şubat sayfasının fotokopisini bakım firması Aquaprime'dan buldu. Sayfada 2 Şubat tarihli uyarı vardı: 'Legionella riski, acil temizlik önerilir'. Altında Garrow'un 'bütçe yok' notu duruyordu.

text: Ms. Odell thought about the torn page. "Garrow did not write the warnings by himself," she said to Ayo. "Somebody wrote them first. And somebody made a copy, because all companies do."
She looked at the first page of the log. At the bottom, in small print, there was a company name: 'Aquaprime Water Services'.
Ms. Odell called the company. A woman answered. She was polite and a little scared. "Yes," she said. "We always keep copies of our service reports for five years. I can send it to you today."
At four in the afternoon, an email arrived. Ms. Odell printed the document and gave it to Ayo. It was dated: 2 February. The title was: 'Urgent Report'.
Ayo read the first line. 'Legionella risk. Immediate cleaning advised.' Under it, in a blue pen, was one note: 'No budget. G.'

eps.title: The Budget
eps.recap: Mr. Garrow, polisin odasında ilk kez konuştu. Yönetim kurulunun bakım bütçesini yüzde otuz kıstığını, kendisinin ise 'bir yıl daha idare edilir' diye düşündüğünü söyledi. Sorumluluk ondaydı ama yalnızca onda değildi.

text: In the afternoon, Mr. Garrow sat in a small room with Ms. Odell and a police officer. A recorder was on the table. He was not smiling any more. He looked small in his big chair.
"Tell us what happened," said Ms. Odell. Mr. Garrow looked at his hands for a long time. Then he began to talk.

"Two years ago, the hospital board cut my budget by thirty per cent," he said. "They said: save money. Every month they called me. 'Spend less, Garrow. Spend less.' I cut the cleaning of the tower. I thought, one more year. It will be fine."

"And then the warnings came?" asked Ms. Odell. "Yes," he said. "I knew. I knew every time. And every time I wrote 'postponed'. I was afraid to ask the board for more money. I was afraid to lose my job."
He took a breath. "I am responsible. But I did not decide alone."
A2.q: What does Garrow say about responsibility?
o: He says he is innocent.
He blames Ayo.
He says nobody is responsible.
He admits he is responsible, but says the board's budget cuts were also a cause.
A2.hint: Garrow sorumluluk hakkında ne söylüyor?
A2.why: Kendi sorumluluğunu kabul ediyor ama yönetim kurulunun bütçe kesintisinin de payı olduğunu söylüyor.

eps.title: Mr. Hale Goes Home
eps.recap: Tower kapatıldıktan sonra altıncı katta yeni hasta çıkmadı. Mr. Hale, aylar sonra ilk kez kendi ayaklarıyla yürüyerek taburcu oldu. Kızı Claire, Ayo'ya bir çiçek buketi getirdi ve hastane koridorunda ağladı.

text: Ten days passed. The cooling tower was empty and clean. Every day, Pete tested the water from the sixth floor. Every day, the result was the same: 'Negative'.
No new patient came with a fever. The old patients got better, one by one. The sixth floor became quiet and normal again.
On Friday morning, Mr. Hale, the first patient, put on his own coat and his own hat. He was eighty-two years old. He still had a bandage on his wrist, but he stood straight.
His daughter Claire was waiting at the door with a big bunch of yellow flowers. She gave them to Ayo. "For the doctor who listened," she said.
Mr. Hale shook Ayo's hand with both of his. "Thank you for not giving up, young lady," he said. Ayo could not speak. She only nodded, and her eyes were wet.
A2.proof: Every day, the result was the same: 'Negative'.
A2.q: What does the daily test result show?
o: The water is no longer contaminated.
The test machine is old.
Pete is bored.
The tower is full.
A2.hint: Her gün aynı sonucun çıkması neyi gösteriyor sence?
A2.why: Suyun artık kirli olmadığını gösteriyor.

B1.q: What does Claire's phrase suggest about Ayo's role?
o: That Ayo is a good singer.
That Ayo paid attention to the patients' worries when others ignored them.
That Ayo works at a radio station.
That Ayo wants flowers.
B1.hint: Claire 'dinleyen doktor' derken neyi kastediyor?
B1.why: Ayo'nun, başkalarının önemsemediği hasta ve ailelerin kaygılarını ciddiye aldığını.

text: Ten days passed. The cooling tower stood empty and clean, and every day Pete tested the water from the sixth floor. Every day the result was the same: 'Negative'.

No new patient arrived with a fever, and the old patients recovered one by one. The sixth floor became quiet and ordinary again, and the nurses, who had whispered for weeks, began to laugh in the corridors.
On Friday morning Mr. Hale, the very first patient, put on his own coat and hat. He was eighty-two years old and still wore a bandage on his wrist, but he stood straight.
His daughter Claire waited at the door with a large bunch of yellow flowers. She handed them to Ayo. "For the doctor who listened," she said.

Mr. Hale shook Ayo's hand with both of his. "Thank you for not giving up, young lady," he said. Ayo could not speak. She only nodded, her eyes wet. It occurred to her that the whole affair had hung on one small thing, the refusal to accept that five coincidences were only coincidences, and that this refusal had cost her a job, a night shift and a great many hours of sleep, and was the best thing she had ever done.
B2.proof: the refusal to accept that five coincidences were only coincidences
B2.q: What turned out to be the key to the whole affair?
o: The weather.
A lucky guess.
Ayo's refusal to dismiss the pattern as chance.
A visit from the mayor.
B2.hint: Bütün bu olayın asıl anahtarı neydi sonunda?
B2.why: Ayo'nun, beş vakayı tesadüf diye geçiştirmeyi reddetmesi.

eps.title: The Inquiry
eps.recap: Üç hafta sonra resmî soruşturma açıldı. Ayo tanık olarak ifade verdi; Rosa ve Pete de dinlendi. Soruşturma, yönetim kurulunun bakım bütçesini kısmasını ve Garrow'un uyarıları saklamasını ihmal olarak değerlendirdi; kurul başkanı istifa etti.

text: Three weeks later, there was a public inquiry. It was held in a big, grey room in the city hall. There were three judges at a long table. Many journalists sat at the back.
Ayo wore her best dark jacket. She sat in the witness chair. She put her hands on her knees to stop them shaking.
"Dr. Bennett," said the judge. "Please tell us in your own words what happened."
Ayo told the story from the beginning: the fifth patient, the sixth floor, the black book, Pete's test, Lina. It took ninety minutes. She did not hide anything, not even her own mistakes.
Pete and Rosa spoke after her. At the end, the chairman of the hospital board stood up and said, in a weak voice: "I resign."
A2.q: What was the result of the inquiry?
o: The hospital got more money.
The board chairman resigned because of the findings.
Ayo was fired.
Nothing changed.
A2.hint: Resmî soruşturmanın sonucu ne oldu sonunda?
A2.why: Kurul başkanı bulgular nedeniyle istifa etti.

text: Three weeks later a public inquiry opened in a large, grey room in the city hall. Three judges sat at a long table, and journalists filled the back rows.

"Dr. Bennett," said the presiding judge. "Please tell us in your own words what happened."
Ayo told the story from the beginning: the fifth patient, the sixth floor, the black book, Pete's test, Lina. It took ninety minutes. She hid nothing, not even her own mistakes.

Pete and Rosa spoke after her. At the end the chairman of the hospital board rose and said in a weak voice: "I resign." Rosa and Pete sat in the front row and held hands. Ayo looked at them once and felt much stronger.
B1.proof: She hid nothing, not even her own mistakes.
B1.q: What does this sentence tell us about Ayo?
o: That she is arrogant.
That she made no mistakes.
That she is honest, even about her own errors.
That she lied.
B1.hint: Ayo'nun kendi hatalarını da saklamaması ne anlama geliyor?
B1.why: Dürüst olduğunu; kendi hatalarını bile gizlemediğini gösteriyor.

text: Three weeks later a public inquiry opened in a large, grey room in the city hall. Three judges sat at a long table, and journalists filled the back rows.

Ayo told the story from the beginning: the fifth patient, the sixth floor, the black book, Pete's test, Lina. It took ninety minutes. She hid nothing, not even her own mistakes, because she had learned that an account with a missing page is the beginning of the very thing she was there to condemn.

Pete and Rosa spoke after her. At the end the chairman of the hospital board rose and said in a weak voice: "I resign." The room did not applaud. It was not that kind of victory. It was the quiet satisfaction of a mechanism that, after a very long delay, had finally done what it was built to do.
B2.proof: an account with a missing page is the beginning of the very thing she was there to condemn
B2.q: Why does Ayo refuse to hide her own mistakes?
o: Because she enjoys confessing.
Because the judges asked her to.
Because she wants to be punished.
Because an incomplete account would repeat the dishonesty she opposes.
B2.hint: Ayo kendi hatalarını neden saklamıyor?
B2.why: Eksik bir anlatım, karşı çıktığı gizleme kültürünün tekrarı olurdu.

eps.title: The New Rule
eps.recap: Hastanede yeni bir kural yazıldı: her bakım uyarısı 24 saat içinde yanıtlanacak ve iki kişi tarafından imzalanacaktı. Ayo gece nöbetine döndü. İlk sabaha karşı yeni bakım defterini açıp ilk satırı okudu.

text: Two months later, a new sign hung on the wall of the ventilation room on the sixth floor. It was printed in large black letters. It said: 'Every warning must be answered within 24 hours. Every answer must be signed by two people.'
Under the sign, there was a new book with a bright green cover. The title was simple: 'Maintenance Log: Water and Cooling'. The first page was already full of neat lines.
It was five in the morning. Ayo was back on the night shift. She walked to the ventilation room with a cup of tea in her hand. The corridor was quiet. The pipes made a soft, regular sound.
She opened the green book. The last entry was from yesterday. 'Water temperature: 62 degrees. Normal. Signed: P. Walsh and R. Díaz.'
Ayo smiled. She closed the book and put it back carefully on the shelf, where everybody could see it. Then she went to check on her patients.
A2.proof: Every warning must be answered within 24 hours.
A2.q: What is the purpose of the new rule?
o: To make the book heavier.
To reduce the number of workers.
To make sure that warnings are never ignored or hidden again.
To close the ventilation room.
A2.hint: Yeni yazılan kuralın asıl amacı nedir?
A2.why: Uyarıların bir daha görmezden gelinmemesini ve gizlenmemesini sağlamak.

B1.why: Kayıtların artık gizlenmediğini, şeffaf tutulduğunu gösteriyor.
