text: Two months later a new sign hung on the wall of the ventilation room on the sixth floor, printed in large black letters: 'Every warning must be answered within 24 hours. Every answer must be signed by two people.'
Beneath it lay a new book with a bright green cover. The title was simple: 'Maintenance Log: Water and Cooling'. Its first pages were already full of neat entries, none of them marked 'postponed'.

It was five in the morning and Ayo was back on the night shift. She walked to the ventilation room with a cup of tea in her hand. The corridor was quiet, and the pipes made a soft, regular sound, the sound of a building doing its job without secrets.
She opened the green book. The last entry was from the previous day: 'Water temperature: 62 degrees. Normal. Signed: P. Walsh and R. Díaz.'

Ayo smiled. She closed the book and set it back carefully on the shelf, where anybody could see it. The new rule had not made the hospital perfect, she knew; pipes would still age and budgets would still tighten. But it had changed the one thing that mattered: it was now impossible for a single tired person to decide, alone and in silence, that somebody else's danger could wait. Then she went to check on her patients.
C1.proof: impossible for a single tired person to decide, alone and in silence, that somebody else's danger could wait
C1.q: What is the main lesson of the new rule, according to the passage?
o: That pipes never age.
That no single person should be able to silently ignore a danger to others.
That budgets never change.
That hospitals are perfect.
C1.hint: Yeni kuralın anlattığı temel ders nedir?
C1.why: Hiç kimsenin başkalarının güvenliğini tehlikeye atan bir uyarıyı tek başına ve sessizce göz ardı edememesi.

title: Station Polaris
hero: Buzul bilimci Dr. Nika Solheim, kutup gecesinde bir buz sondajında beklenmedik bir sıcaklık ölçüyor ve verilerin kaybolduğunu fark ediyor.
intro: Aylarca güneşin doğmadığı bir kutup istasyonu. Buzul bilimci Nika Solheim, kilometrelerce kalınlıktaki buzun içine inen sondajında hiç olmaması gereken bir sıcaklık okuyor. Ardından veriler birer birer kayboluyor. Buzun altında ne var ve kim bunu saklamak istiyor? Fen ve doğa bilimleri İngilizcesiyle bir macerada Nika'ya eşlik edeceksin.
outro: Nika ve ekibi buzun altındaki sırrı ortaya çıkardı ve verilerin neden saklandığını herkese gösterdi. Otuz gün boyunca bilimsel İngilizceyle okudun, kanıtlardan sonuç çıkardın ve bir macerayı sonuna kadar götürdün. Başka bir tefrikaya geçmeye hazırsın.

eps.title: Minus Three
eps.recap: Kutup gecesi başlarken Nika, 400 metre derinlikteki sondajında buzun olması gerekenden çok daha sıcak olduğunu gördü. Ekran eksi üç dereceyi gösteriyordu; bu derinlikte buz çok daha soğuk olmalıydı.

text: The sun went down on Station Polaris for the last time that year. For the next four months, there would be no daylight. Dr. Nika Solheim did not mind. She loved the quiet.
Every morning, she went to the drill house. The drill made a long hole in the ice. At the bottom of the hole, a small machine measured the temperature.
On that Tuesday, the drill reached four hundred metres. Nika looked at the screen and waited for the number. She expected minus eighteen degrees. That is the normal temperature of ice at that depth.
The number appeared. It said: minus three.
Nika stopped breathing for a moment. Minus three was too warm. Ice at four hundred metres was never minus three. She read the screen again, and again.
A2.proof: Ice at four hundred metres was never minus three
A2.q: Why was Nika surprised by the number on the screen?
o: The drill reached the bottom of the ice too quickly.
The ice at that depth was much warmer than it should be.
The screen showed a temperature in the wrong units.
She did not expect the drill to work in the dark.
A2.hint: Nika'nın ne beklediğini ve ekranda ne gördüğünü karşılaştır.
A2.why: Nika bu derinlikte eksi on sekiz derece bekliyordu; ekranda eksi üç yazıyordu. Buz olması gerekenden çok daha sıcaktı.

text: The sun set over Station Polaris for the last time that year. For the next four months there would be no daylight at all, and the station's eleven scientists settled into the long dark. Dr. Nika Solheim did not mind. She liked the silence.

Every morning she walked to the drill house at the edge of the camp. The drill pushed a narrow hole deep into the ice, and at the bottom of the hole a small instrument measured the temperature of the ice around it. Her whole project depended on those numbers.
On that Tuesday the drill reached four hundred metres. Nika stood in front of the screen with a mug of coffee and waited. She expected minus eighteen degrees, which is normal for ice at that depth.
The number appeared. It read minus three.

She put down the mug. Minus three was far too warm. Ice does not behave like that, not at four hundred metres and not in the middle of the polar night. She read the figure again, then a third time, and the screen did not change.
B1.proof: She expected minus eighteen degrees
B1.q: What can we understand from Nika's reaction to the reading?
o: The instrument has stopped working and gives no number.
She is happy because her project is now finished.
The measurement is very different from what her scientific knowledge predicts.
The coffee has made the screen difficult to read.
B1.hint: Nika'nın beklediği değerle ekrandaki değer arasındaki farka bak.
B1.why: Nika eksi on sekiz derece bekliyordu ama eksi üç gördü; bilimsel bilgisinin öngördüğünden çok farklı bir ölçüm bu.

text: The sun set over Station Polaris for the last time that year. For the next four months there would be no daylight at all, and the station's eleven scientists prepared to settle into the long dark. Dr. Nika Solheim did not mind. She had always preferred silence to sunshine.

Every morning she walked to the drill house at the edge of the camp. The drill pushed a narrow shaft deep into the ice, and at the bottom of it a small instrument recorded the temperature of the surrounding ice. Her entire research project depended on those numbers.

On that Tuesday the drill reached four hundred metres. Nika stood in front of the screen with a mug of coffee and waited. She expected a reading of around minus eighteen degrees, which is normal for ice at that depth.
The number appeared. It read minus three.

She put down the mug very carefully. Minus three was far too warm. Ice does not behave like that, not at four hundred metres and certainly not in the middle of a polar winter. She read the figure a second time, then a third, and the screen refused to change its mind.
B2.proof: She expected a reading of around minus eighteen degrees
B2.q: Why does the author describe Nika putting down the mug 'very carefully'?
o: To suggest that the mug was broken.
To show that she wants to leave the drill house.
To explain that the coffee was too hot to drink.
To show that she is shocked and trying to stay calm.
B2.hint: Dikkatli davranmak, sürpriz karşısındaki ruh halini nasıl yansıtır?
B2.why: Nika kupayı çok dikkatle bırakıyor; bu, şaşkınlığını ve sakin kalmaya çalıştığını gösteriyor. Okuma beklentisinden çok farklı.

text: The sun set over Station Polaris for the last time that year. For the next four months there would be no daylight at all, and the station's eleven scientists prepared to settle into the long dark. Dr. Nika Solheim did not mind. She had always preferred silence to sunshine, and a glaciologist who disliked the cold was in the wrong profession.

Every morning she walked to the drill house at the edge of the camp. The drill pushed a narrow shaft deep into the ice, and at the bottom of the shaft a small instrument recorded the temperature of the surrounding ice. Her entire research programme depended on those numbers, which were meant to confirm a theory about how slowly the ice sheet moved.

On that Tuesday the drill reached four hundred metres. Nika stood in front of the screen with a mug of coffee and waited. She expected a reading of around minus eighteen degrees, which is typical for ice at that depth.
The number appeared. It read minus three.

She put the mug down very carefully, as if the table might break. Minus three was far too warm. Ice does not behave like that, not at four hundred metres and certainly not in the middle of a polar winter. She read the figure a second time, then a third, and the screen declined to change its mind.
C1.proof: Minus three was far too warm
C1.q: What does the final sentence imply about the reading?
o: That it is stable and will not disappear when checked again.
That the screen is probably broken and should be replaced.
That Nika should ignore it until morning.
That the instrument was placed in the wrong hole.
C1.hint: Ekranın 'fikrini değiştirmeyi reddetmesi' ne anlama gelir?
C1.why: Ekran üç kez bakışta da aynı değeri gösteriyor; yani okuma kararlı ve tekrar kontrolle kaybolmuyor, bu da sonucun ciddiye alınması gerektiğini gösteriyor.

eps.title: The Sensor Is Right
eps.recap: Mühendis Tomas, cihazı buz banyosunda test etti ve sensörün tam doğru ölçtüğünü gösterdi. Demek ki buzdaki sıcaklık gerçekten olması gerekenden yüksekti.

text: Nika called Tomas, the station engineer. He came to the drill house in his big yellow coat. He listened to her and then he looked at the screen. "The sensor is probably wrong," he said.
"Check it," said Nika.
Tomas pulled the instrument out of the hole. He put it in a bucket of ice and water. A bucket of ice and water is always exactly zero degrees. He waited ten minutes.
The screen said: zero point zero. Tomas checked the cable. He checked the battery. He checked the program on the computer. Everything was fine.
"Well?" asked Nika. Tomas took off his hat and scratched his head. "The sensor is right," he said. "It is working perfectly."
A2.q: What does Tomas's test show?
o: The sensor is too old to be used.
The bucket was not cold enough for the test.
The warm temperature in the ice is probably real.
Nika made a mistake with the computer.
A2.hint: Sensör sıfır derecede tam sıfırı gösterdiyse sensör hakkında ne söyleyebiliriz?
A2.why: Buz-su karışımında sensör tam sıfırı gösteriyor ve diğer her şey sağlam; yani cihaz doğru ölçüyor, sıcaklık gerçek olmalı.

text: Nika called Tomas, the station engineer, who arrived at the drill house in his big yellow coat. He listened, looked at the screen, and shrugged. "It's probably the sensor," he said. "They fail all the time in this cold."
"Then test it," said Nika.
Tomas pulled the instrument out of the shaft and placed it in a bucket of crushed ice and water, which stays at exactly zero degrees. He waited ten minutes without speaking.
The screen read: zero point zero. He checked the cable, the battery and the software, one after the other. Everything was in perfect order.

"Well?" asked Nika. Tomas took off his hat and rubbed the back of his head. "I'd love to tell you it's broken," he said. "But it isn't. The sensor is right." Outside the wind rose, and neither of them said what they were both thinking: if the sensor was right, then something under the ice was warm.
B1.proof: if the sensor was right, then something under the ice was warm
B1.q: What is the logical conclusion of Tomas's tests?
o: The cable and the battery are the cause of the error.
The sensor works only at zero degrees.
The drill went into the wrong part of the ice.
The high temperature is real and needs another explanation.
B1.hint: Sensör doğruysa ölçülen yüksek sıcaklık hakkında ne düşünmek gerekir?
B1.why: Sensör, kablo, pil ve yazılım doğru çıkıyor. Bu durumda yüksek sıcaklık gerçek ve buzun altında sıcak bir şey olmalı.

text: Nika called Tomas, the station engineer, who arrived at the drill house in his enormous yellow coat. He listened, studied the screen, and shrugged. "It's probably the sensor," he said. "They fail all the time in this cold."
"Then test it," said Nika.

Tomas hauled the instrument out of the shaft and lowered it into a bucket of crushed ice and water, a mixture that stays at precisely zero degrees. Then he stood waiting for ten minutes without a word, which for Tomas was a record.
The screen read zero point zero. He checked the cable, the battery and the software, one after the other. Everything was in perfect order.

"Well?" asked Nika. Tomas took off his hat and rubbed the back of his head. "I'd love to tell you it's broken," he said. "But it isn't. The sensor is right." Outside the wind rose against the walls, and neither of them said what they were both thinking: if the sensor was right, then something deep under the ice was warm, and nobody on the station had a theory for that.
B2.proof: if the sensor was right, then something deep under the ice was warm
B2.q: Why does Tomas test the sensor in a bucket of ice and water?
o: Because that mixture gives a known temperature to compare against.
Because the sensor needs to be cleaned before use.
Because the drill house has no other way to measure heat.
Because Nika asked him to reduce the noise.
B2.hint: Buz ve su karışımının neden bilinen bir sıcaklığı olduğunu düşün.
B2.why: Ezilmiş buz-su karışımı tam sıfır derecede kalır; Tomas sensörün bu bilinen değeri doğru gösterip göstermediğine bakarak güvenilirliğini sınıyor.

text: Nika called Tomas, the station engineer, who arrived at the drill house in his enormous yellow coat. He listened, studied the screen, and shrugged. "It's probably the sensor," he said. "They fail all the time in this cold. I've replaced a dozen of them."
"Then test it," said Nika.

Tomas hauled the instrument out of the shaft and lowered it into a bucket of crushed ice and water, a mixture that holds at precisely zero degrees. Then he stood waiting for ten minutes without a word, which, for Tomas, amounted to a personal record.
The display read zero point zero. He checked the cable, the battery and the software in turn. Every component was in perfect order, and the calibration file bore a date from only two weeks earlier.

"Well?" asked Nika. Tomas took off his hat and rubbed the back of his head. "I'd love to tell you it's broken," he said. "But it isn't. The sensor is right." Outside, the wind rose against the walls of the hut, and neither of them said what they were both thinking: if the instrument was telling the truth, then something deep beneath the ice was warm, and nobody on the station had a theory to explain it.
C1.proof: if the instrument was telling the truth
C1.q: What can be inferred about the scientists' situation at the end?
o: They have proven that the ice sheet is moving faster than expected.
They have eliminated the easy explanation and now face a real mystery.
They have agreed that the experiment should be cancelled.
They have found that the calibration file was out of date.
C1.hint: Tomas bozuk sensör açıklamasını eledikten sonra geriye ne kalıyor?
C1.why: Sensör, kablo ve kalibrasyon doğru çıkınca kolay açıklama (arıza) eleniyor; geriye buzun altında gerçekten sıcak bir şey olduğu gizemi kalıyor.

eps.title: A Missing Page
eps.recap: İstasyon müdürü Dr. Brandt, sıcaklık okumasına 'kalibrasyon hatası' dedi ve konuyu kapatmaya çalıştı. Nika, veri günlüğünden bir sayfanın temiz bir şekilde koparıldığını fark etti.

text: The next morning, Nika told Dr. Brandt, the director of the station. Dr. Brandt was a tall man with a grey beard. He listened with his eyes closed.
"It is a calibration error," he said. "Please do not tell the others. We do not want people to be afraid."
"But Tomas tested the sensor," said Nika. "It is correct."
"Then the old data will show it," said Brandt. He gave her the big paper book where the team writes every measurement. "Look yourself. You will see that I am right."
Nika opened the book and turned the pages. Then she stopped. Between two pages, there was a thin line of paper. Someone had cut out one page. It was the page from the day before the drilling started.
A2.proof: Someone had cut out one page
A2.q: Why does Nika feel doubt about Dr. Brandt?
o: He did not listen to her at all.
He has a grey beard and closes his eyes.
He refused to give her the data book.
A page of the data book is missing, and he told her not to speak.
A2.hint: Brandt'ın söylediği iki şeye ve defterdeki eksik sayfaya birlikte bak.
A2.why: Brandt konuşmamasını istedi ve 'kalibrasyon hatası' dedi; ama günlükte bir sayfa kesilmiş. Bu iki şey Nika'nın şüphesini artırıyor.

text: The next morning Nika went to see Dr. Brandt, the director of the station, a tall man with a grey beard who listened to her with his eyes closed. When she had finished, he opened them and said, "It's a calibration error."
"Tomas tested the sensor yesterday," said Nika. "It's accurate."
"Then perhaps you misread it. Please don't mention this to the others. We have eleven people here for the whole winter, and I don't want anyone to panic."
Nika frowned. "The old data will show it," Brandt added, and handed her the thick paper logbook where the team recorded every measurement. "Look for yourself."

She turned the pages one by one. Then her finger stopped. Between two pages there was a thin strip of paper, still white and clean. Someone had cut out a page, very neatly, with a sharp blade. She checked the date on the page before it. It was the day before the drilling began.
B1.proof: Someone had cut out a page, very neatly, with a sharp blade
B1.q: What is suggested by the missing page?
o: Someone may have removed data on purpose before the drilling began.
The logbook is too old to be useful.
Dr. Brandt gave her the wrong book by accident.
The team forgot to record anything that day.
B1.hint: Sayfanın bıçakla, düzgün şekilde kesilmiş olması bir kaza mıdır?
B1.why: Sayfa keskin bir bıçakla temiz biçimde kesilmiş ve tam sondajdan önceki günden; bu, verinin kasıtlı olarak çıkarılmış olabileceğini düşündürüyor.

text: The next morning Nika went to see Dr. Brandt, the director of the station, a tall man with a grey beard who listened with his eyes closed. When she had finished, he opened them and said calmly, "It's a calibration error."
"Tomas tested the sensor yesterday," said Nika. "It's accurate."
"Then perhaps the test was flawed. And please don't mention this to the others. We have eleven people here for the whole winter, and I would hate to see anyone panic over a faulty number."
Nika said nothing. "The older records will settle it," Brandt added, and handed her the thick paper logbook in which the team had written every measurement for three years. "Look for yourself."

She turned the pages one by one. Then her finger stopped. Between two pages there was a thin strip of paper, still white and clean. Someone had cut out a page, very neatly, with a sharp blade. She checked the date on the page before it. It was the day before the drilling began, and Dr. Brandt had been the only person with a key to the cabinet.
B2.proof: Dr. Brandt had been the only person with a key to the cabinet
B2.q: Why does the author mention that Brandt had the only key?
o: To explain why the cabinet was always locked at night.
To suggest that he may be the one who removed the page.
To show that he trusts Nika with the records.
To prove that the logbook was kept safe.
B2.hint: Dolabın tek anahtarının Brandt'ta olması kimi şüpheli gösterir?
B2.why: Sayfa kesilmiş ve dolaba yalnızca Brandt erişebiliyormuş. Yazar bu detayla sayfayı onun çıkarmış olabileceğini ima ediyor.

text: The next morning Nika went to see Dr. Brandt, the director of the station, a tall man with a grey beard who listened with his eyes closed, like a priest hearing a confession. When she had finished, he opened them and said, quite calmly, "It's a calibration error."
"Tomas tested the sensor yesterday," said Nika. "It's accurate."

"Then perhaps the test itself was flawed. And I'd be grateful if you didn't mention this to the others. We have eleven people here for the whole winter, and I would hate to see anyone panic over a faulty number."

Nika said nothing. "The older records will settle the matter," Brandt added, and handed her the thick paper logbook in which the team had written every measurement for three years. "Look for yourself. You'll find I'm right."

She turned the pages one by one. Then her finger stopped. Between two pages there was a thin strip of paper, still white and clean. Someone had cut out a page, very neatly, with a sharp blade. The page before it was dated the day before the drilling began, and Dr. Brandt, she remembered, was the only person on the station with a key to the cabinet in which the logbook was kept.
C1.proof: the only person on the station with a key to the cabinet
C1.q: What can be inferred about Brandt's behaviour in the passage?
o: He is trying to protect the team from a dangerous storm.
He wants Nika to take over the project.
His request for silence and his easy confidence now look suspicious.
He believes the sensor test and has apologised.
C1.hint: Brandt'ın sessiz kalma isteğini ve kesik sayfayı birlikte değerlendir.
C1.why: Brandt hem Nika'dan konuyu gizli tutmasını istiyor hem de 'haklı çıkacağını' söylüyor; sayfanın ve anahtarın ardından bu davranış şüpheli görünüyor.

eps.title: Eleven O'Clock
eps.recap: İstasyonda her gece aynı saatte ışıklar titremeye ve radyoda parazit olmaya başladı. Kit bunun rastgele hava olayı değil, düzenli bir şey olduğunu fark etti.

text: Kit was the cook of Station Polaris, and he was also the radio operator. He knew every sound in the station. On Thursday evening, he found Nika in the kitchen.
"I have a strange thing to tell you," he said. "Every night, the lights go up and down for a few seconds. It is about eleven o'clock. And at the same time, my radio makes a noise. Like a buzz."
"Maybe it is the wind," said Nika. "Or the cold."
Kit shook his head. "I wrote it down in my book. Monday, eleven o'clock. Tuesday, eleven o'clock. Wednesday, eleven o'clock. The wind is never so exact."
He opened his notebook and showed her the page. The numbers were the same every night: 23:00, 23:02, 23:01. Nika looked at him. "Then something is switched on at that time," she said.
A2.proof: The wind is never so exact.
A2.q: Why does Kit say it is not the wind?
o: The noise comes at almost the same time every night.
The wind in the station is always very weak.
The radio is broken and gives noise all day.
He does not like Nika's idea.
A2.hint: Kit'in defterindeki saatlere bak: rüzgâr böyle düzenli olur mu?
A2.why: Ses ve ışık titremesi her gece neredeyse aynı saatte; rüzgâr bu kadar düzenli olmaz, bu yüzden Kit sebebin hava olmadığını düşünüyor.

text: Kit was the cook at Station Polaris, and also its radio operator, which meant he knew every sound the station made. On Thursday evening he found Nika in the kitchen, looking worried.

"I have something strange to tell you," he said. "Every night the lights go up and down for a few seconds, at about eleven o'clock. And at exactly the same time my radio fills with a kind of buzzing."
"It could be the wind," said Nika. "Or the cold. Both are hard on the cables."
Kit shook his head. "I've been writing it in my book. Monday, eleven. Tuesday, eleven. Wednesday, eleven. The wind is never that punctual."

He opened the notebook and showed her the page. The times were almost identical: 23:00, 23:02, 23:01. Nika read them twice. "Then something is being switched on at that hour," she said slowly, "and it's drawing a lot of power."
B1.proof: The wind is never that punctual.
B1.q: What do the repeated times imply about the cause?
o: A storm is slowly moving toward the station.
Something man-made is being started at the same time every night.
The kitchen equipment is broken.
The radio is picking up a signal from another country.
B1.hint: Düzenli saatler doğal bir olaydan mı, insan eylemlerinden mi gelir?
B1.why: Her gece aynı saatte tekrarlanan ışık titremesi, o saatte birinin bir cihazı çalıştırdığını ve çok güç çektiğini düşündürüyor.

text: Kit was the cook at Station Polaris, and also its radio operator, which meant he knew every sound the station made. On Thursday evening he found Nika in the kitchen, looking more worried than usual.

"I have something strange to tell you," he said. "Every night the lights dip and flicker for a few seconds, at about eleven o'clock. And at exactly the same time my radio fills with a kind of buzzing, like a wasp in a jar."
"It could be the wind," said Nika. "Or the cold. Both are hard on the cables. This station is thirty years old, Kit."
Kit shook his head. "I've been writing it down. Monday, eleven. Tuesday, eleven. Wednesday, eleven. The wind is never that punctual."

He opened the notebook and showed her the page. The times were almost identical: 23:00, 23:02, 23:01. Nika read them twice. "Then something is being switched on at that hour," she said slowly, "and it's drawing a great deal of power. Who would run equipment at night, when everyone else is asleep?" Outside, the wind pushed against the windows, and for once it sounded like nothing but wind.
B2.proof: Who would run equipment at night, when everyone else is asleep?
B2.q: What does Nika's final question suggest?
o: That the equipment is old and should be repaired.
That Kit has forgotten to turn off the radio.
That someone may be secretly using equipment while the others sleep.
That the station needs more power in winter.
B2.hint: Gece herkes uyurken ekipman çalıştıran kişi hakkında Nika ne düşünüyor?
B2.why: Nika, herkes uyurken birinin gizlice ekipman çalıştırıyor olabileceğini ima ediyor.

text: Kit was the cook at Station Polaris, and also its radio operator, which meant he knew every sound the station made. On Thursday evening he found Nika in the kitchen, looking more worried than usual.

"I have something strange to tell you," he said. "Every night the lights dip and flicker for a few seconds, at about eleven o'clock. And at exactly the same moment my radio fills with a kind of buzzing, like a wasp trapped in a jar."
"It could be the wind," said Nika. "Or the cold. Both are hard on old cables, and these cables are older than I am."
Kit shook his head. "I've been keeping a note of it. Monday, eleven. Tuesday, eleven. Wednesday, eleven. The wind is never that punctual."

He opened the notebook and showed her the page. The times were almost identical: 23:00, 23:02, 23:01. Nika read them twice. "Then something is being switched on at that hour," she said slowly, "and it's drawing a great deal of power. Who would run heavy equipment in the middle of the night, when the whole station is asleep, unless they preferred not to be seen doing it?" Kit said nothing. He had already asked himself the same question for three nights, and he had not liked any of the answers.
C1.proof: unless they preferred not to be seen doing it
C1.q: What does the structure of Nika's last sentence suggest about her suspicion?
o: She thinks the equipment belongs to the kitchen.
She believes the sound is caused by the polar night.
She is certain that Kit is making a mistake.
She suspects a person who is deliberately hiding an activity.
C1.hint: 'Görülmemeyi tercih etmedikçe' ifadesi kimin davranışını sorguluyor?
C1.why: Nika, ağır ekipmanı gece, görülmeden çalıştıran birinin olabileceğini düşünüyor; yani bilinçli bir gizlenmeden şüpheleniyor.

eps.title: A Second Opinion
eps.recap: Nika, sondaj sensöründen bağımsız taşınabilir bir sıcaklık probuyla aynı derinlikte ölçümü tekrarladı. Sonuç yine eksi üçe yakındı; ölçüm hatası ihtimali artık çok zayıftı.

text: Nika wanted one more test. She did not trust one instrument only. In the equipment room, she found an old portable probe. It was a long thin cable with a small thermometer at the end.
On Friday, she and Tomas went to the drill house. They put the probe into the hole. Slowly, they lowered it. One hundred metres. Two hundred metres. Three hundred metres.
At four hundred metres, the cable stopped. Nika waited for ten minutes. Her hands were cold, and her heart was fast.
Then she read the number. Minus three point one.
"The same," said Tomas quietly. "A different instrument. A different cable. The same temperature." Nika sat on a box. "Then we do not have a measuring problem," she said. "We have a real problem."
A2.proof: A different instrument. A different cable. The same temperature.
A2.q: Why did Nika use a second instrument?
o: Because the first instrument was too heavy to carry.
To check that the first result was not caused by one faulty device.
Because Tomas asked her to try something new.
Because the old probe is more expensive.
A2.hint: İkinci cihaz aynı sonucu verirse ilk cihaz hakkında ne düşünürüz?
A2.why: Nika tek bir cihaza güvenmek istemedi. İki farklı cihaz aynı sıcaklığı gösterince ölçüm hatası ihtimali ortadan kalkıyor.

text: Nika wanted one more test. She did not trust a single instrument. In the equipment room she found an old portable probe, a long thin cable with a small thermometer on the end, and a handwritten label that said 'calibrated in August'.
On Friday she and Tomas carried it to the drill house and lowered it into the shaft, slowly, a few metres at a time. One hundred. Two hundred. Three hundred.
At four hundred metres the cable went slack. Nika waited ten minutes without speaking. Her hands were numb, and her heart was beating faster than the cold allowed.
Then she read the figure. Minus three point one.

"The same," said Tomas quietly. "A different instrument, a different cable, a different day. The same temperature." Nika sat down on an equipment box. "Then we don't have a measuring problem," she said. "We have a real one."
B1.proof: A different instrument, a different cable, a different day.
B1.q: What do the two matching results prove?
o: The probe needs to be recalibrated.
The ice is warmer in August than in winter.
The temperature is real and not an error of one instrument.
The shaft is too narrow for measurements.
B1.hint: Farklı cihaz, farklı kablo ve farklı gün, aynı sonuç: bu neyi kanıtlar?
B1.why: Farklı bir cihaz, kablo ve gün aynı sonucu verdiği için ölçüm hatası ihtimali ortadan kalkıyor; sıcaklık gerçek.

text: Nika wanted one more test. She did not trust a single instrument. In the equipment room she found an old portable probe, a long thin cable with a small thermometer on the end, and a handwritten label that read 'calibrated in August'.
On Friday she and Tomas carried it to the drill house and lowered it into the shaft, slowly, a few metres at a time. One hundred. Two hundred. Three hundred.
At four hundred metres the cable went slack. Nika waited ten minutes without speaking. Her hands were numb, and her heart was beating faster than the cold allowed.
Then she read the figure. Minus three point one.

"The same," said Tomas quietly. "A different instrument, a different cable, a different day. The same temperature." Nika sat down on an equipment box. "Then we don't have a measuring problem," she said. "We have a real one." She stared at the shaft, a black circle in the white floor, and for the first time she wondered not whether the ice was warm, but what was warming it.
B2.proof: what was warming it
B2.q: What shift in Nika's thinking is described at the end?
o: She decides that the experiment has failed.
She begins to believe Dr. Brandt's explanation.
She decides to stop measuring for the winter.
She moves from doubting the data to asking what causes the heat.
B2.hint: 'Buzun sıcak olup olmadığı' sorusundan 'neyin ısıttığı' sorusuna geçiş neyi gösterir?
B2.why: Nika artık verinin doğru olup olmadığını değil, buzu neyin ısıttığını soruyor; sorusu 'ölçüm hatası mı?' aşamasından 'neden?' aşamasına geçiyor.

text: Nika wanted one more test. She did not trust a single instrument, however well it had been maintained. In the equipment room she found an old portable probe, a long thin cable with a small thermometer on the end, and a handwritten label that read 'calibrated in August'.
On Friday she and Tomas carried it to the drill house and lowered it into the shaft, slowly, a few metres at a time. One hundred. Two hundred. Three hundred.
At four hundred metres the cable went slack. Nika waited ten minutes without speaking. Her hands were numb, and her heart was beating faster than the cold allowed.
Then she read the figure. Minus three point one.

"The same," said Tomas quietly. "A different instrument, a different cable, a different day. The same temperature." Nika sat down on an equipment box. "Then we don't have a measuring problem," she said. "We have a real one." She stared at the shaft, a black circle in the white floor, and understood that the question had changed. It was no longer whether the ice was warm, but what was warming it, and why a director who had read the first report had told her to forget it.
C1.proof: why a director who had read the first report had told her to forget it
C1.q: What does the last clause add to the passage?
o: It shows that Nika now connects the scientific problem with Brandt's behaviour.
It proves that the director has already solved the problem.
It suggests that Tomas is also hiding information.
It explains that the first report was lost.
C1.hint: Nika bilimsel soruyu Brandt'ın tavrıyla birleştirirken neyi fark ediyor?
C1.why: Nika artık yalnızca fiziksel nedeni değil, müdürün neden konuyu unutmasını istediğini de sorguluyor; bilimsel sorunu Brandt'ın davranışıyla ilişkilendiriyor.

eps.title: A New Lock
eps.recap: Nika, bir imza için Dr. Brandt'ın odasına gitti ve duvar kenarındaki dosya dolabına yepyeni, parlak bir kilit takıldığını gördü. İstasyondaki her şey eski ve paslıyken bu kilit çok dikkat çekiciydi.

text: On Saturday, Nika needed Dr. Brandt's signature for a new work plan. She knocked on the door of his office. Nobody answered. She waited a minute and went in.
The office was small and tidy. There was a desk, a chair, a map on the wall, and a grey metal cabinet in the corner. Nika did not usually look at furniture. But today she looked.
Everything at Station Polaris was old. The chairs were old, the tables were old and the doors were rusty. But the cabinet had a lock, and the lock was new. It was bright and clean, like a coin.
"Can I help you?" said a voice. Dr. Brandt was standing in the door. He was holding a cup of tea. He looked at her. Then he looked at the cabinet.
"I only need your signature," said Nika. She gave him the paper, and he signed it. He did not smile. When Nika left, she heard the sound of keys.
A2.q: Why is the new lock important?
o: The old lock was too rusty to open.
Brandt likes to buy new furniture.
Someone recently put something valuable in the cabinet.
All the doors in the station got new locks.
A2.hint: Her şey eski ama kilit yeni: bu fark neyi düşündürür?
A2.why: İstasyondaki her şey eski ama kilit yeni ve parlak; yakın zamanda bir şey saklamak için takılmış olabilir.

text: On Saturday Nika needed Dr. Brandt's signature on a new work plan. She knocked on his office door. Nobody answered. After a minute she let herself in to leave the paper on his desk.
The office was small and tidy: a desk, a chair, a map of the ice sheet on the wall, and a grey metal cabinet in the corner. Nika did not usually look at furniture. Today she did.

Everything at Station Polaris was old. The chairs were scratched, the tables were stained, and the door handles were rusty. But the cabinet had a lock, and the lock was new. It was bright and clean, like a freshly minted coin.
"Can I help you?" Dr. Brandt was standing in the doorway with a cup of tea. He looked at Nika, and then, for a fraction of a second, at the cabinet.
"I only need your signature," she said. He signed without reading the plan. He did not smile. As she walked down the corridor, Nika heard the quiet, careful sound of a key turning behind her.
B1.proof: the lock was new
B1.q: What does the sound of the key at the end suggest?
o: Brandt is leaving the station.
Someone else is entering the office.
The cabinet is being repaired.
Brandt is checking that the cabinet is safely locked.
B1.hint: Nika ayrıldıktan hemen sonra anahtar sesi duyulması neyi gösterir?
B1.why: Nika çıkar çıkmaz anahtar sesi geliyor; Brandt dolabın kilitli olduğundan emin olmaya çalışıyor, yani içindekini saklıyor.

text: On Saturday Nika needed Dr. Brandt's signature on a new work plan. She knocked on his office door, and nobody answered. After a minute she let herself in to leave the paper on his desk.
The office was small and tidy: a desk, a chair, a map of the ice sheet on the wall, and a grey metal cabinet in the corner. Nika did not usually notice furniture. Today she did.

Everything at Station Polaris was old. The chairs were scratched, the tables stained, the door handles rusted by years of ice. But the cabinet had a lock, and the lock was new. It was bright and clean, like a freshly minted coin, and it looked as out of place as a diamond on a farmer's hand.
"Can I help you?" Dr. Brandt stood in the doorway with a cup of tea. He looked at Nika and then, for a fraction of a second, at the cabinet.

"I only need your signature," she said. He signed without reading the plan. He did not smile. As she walked down the corridor, Nika heard the quiet, careful sound of a key turning behind her, and she understood that a man does not buy a new lock to protect old paper.
B2.proof: a man does not buy a new lock to protect old paper
B2.q: What conclusion does Nika draw?
o: That the cabinet contains something recent and important that Brandt wants hidden.
That the cabinet contains only old documents.
That Brandt is afraid of thieves from outside the station.
That the lock was a gift from the headquarters.
B2.hint: 'Eski kâğıtları korumak için yeni kilit alınmaz' sözünün sonucu ne?
B2.why: Nika, Brandt'ın yeni bir kilidin eski kâğıtlar için alınmayacağını düşünüyor; dolapta yeni ve önemli bir şey olduğunu sezdiriyor.

text: On Saturday Nika needed Dr. Brandt's signature on a new work plan. She knocked on his office door, and nobody answered. After a minute she let herself in to leave the paper on his desk.
The office was small and tidy: a desk, a chair, a map of the ice sheet on the wall, and a grey metal cabinet in the corner. Nika did not usually notice furniture. Today she did.

Everything at Station Polaris was old. The chairs were scratched, the tables stained, the door handles rusted by years of ice. But the cabinet had a lock, and the lock was new. It was bright and clean, like a freshly minted coin, and it looked as out of place as a diamond on a farmer's hand.
"Can I help you?" Dr. Brandt stood in the doorway with a cup of tea. He looked at Nika and then, for no more than a fraction of a second, at the cabinet.

"I only need your signature," she said. He signed without reading the plan, which was uncharacteristic, and he did not smile, which was not. As she walked down the corridor, Nika heard the quiet, careful sound of a key turning behind her. She understood then that a man does not buy a new lock to protect old paper, and that the only person in the station with the authority to buy one was the one standing behind that door.
C1.proof: the only person in the station with the authority to buy one
C1.q: What does the last sentence imply about who put the lock on the cabinet?
o: That it was installed by the previous director years ago.
That it was almost certainly Brandt himself, who controls the station's purchases.
That it was installed by Tomas for safety.
That nobody knows who installed it.
C1.hint: Kilidi satın alma yetkisi olan tek kişi kimdir?
C1.why: Yalnızca istasyon müdürü Brandt'ın böyle bir kilidi alma yetkisi var; Nika kilidi onun taktığını ima ediyor.

eps.title: A Perfectly Flat Line
eps.recap: Nika, sondaj kayıtlarını ana bilgisayarda incelerken 360–420 metre arasındaki değerlerin tamamen düz bir çizgiye dönüştüğünü fark etti. Doğada böyle mükemmel düzgünlük olmazdı; veriler değiştirilmiş görünüyordu.

text: On Sunday, Nika sat at the main computer in the station. She wanted to see all the temperature data from the drill. She opened the files and made a graph.
The line on the graph went down slowly, as it should. At one hundred metres, it was cold. At two hundred, it was colder. At three hundred, it was very cold. Then something strange happened.
Between three hundred and sixty and four hundred and twenty metres, the line became completely flat. It was a perfectly straight line, at minus eighteen degrees.
Nika looked at the numbers. Every number was exactly the same: minus eighteen point zero. Nature never makes numbers like that. There are always small changes.
"These are not real," she whispered. "Somebody wrote these numbers. Somebody changed the data."
A2.proof: Nature never makes numbers like that.
A2.q: Why does Nika think the data were changed?
o: The computer was too slow to make the graph.
The graph was drawn in the wrong colour.
The temperatures were too cold.
Natural measurements are never perfectly identical.
A2.hint: Gerçek ölçümlerde sayıların küçük farklar göstermesi gerekir; burada ne var?
A2.why: Bütün değerler tam olarak eksi on sekiz; doğal ölçümler asla bu kadar aynı olmaz, bu yüzden Nika verilerin değiştirildiğini düşünüyor.

text: On Sunday Nika sat down at the main computer in the station. She wanted to look at all the temperature data from the drill, so she opened the files and plotted a graph.
The line sloped downward gently, as it should. At one hundred metres it was cold. At two hundred it was colder. At three hundred it was colder still. Then something strange happened.

Between three hundred and sixty and four hundred and twenty metres, the line became completely flat. It was a perfectly straight line at minus eighteen degrees, exactly what she had expected to see on Tuesday.

Nika opened the table of numbers. Every value in that range was identical: minus eighteen point zero. Nature never produces numbers like that. Real measurements wobble a little, even in the most stable ice.
"These aren't measurements," she whispered. "Somebody has typed them in. Somebody has replaced the real data with the numbers I expected to find."
B1.proof: Real measurements wobble a little, even in the most stable ice.
B1.q: What does the flat line reveal?
o: The real data were replaced with invented, expected values.
The ice is very stable at that depth.
The sensor stopped working at 360 metres.
The computer cannot show more than one line.
B1.hint: Mükemmel şekilde düz çizgi ve aynı değerler neyi gösterir?
B1.why: Gerçek ölçümler biraz dalgalanır; tamamen aynı değerler birinin gerçek verileri beklenen sayılarla değiştirdiğini gösteriyor.

text: On Sunday Nika sat down at the main computer in the station. She wanted to look at all the temperature data from the drill, so she opened the files and plotted a graph, expecting the usual smooth, gentle curve.
The line sloped downward as it should. At one hundred metres it was cold. At two hundred it was colder. At three hundred it was colder still. Then something strange happened.

Between three hundred and sixty and four hundred and twenty metres, the line became completely flat. It was a perfectly straight line at minus eighteen degrees, exactly the figure she had expected to see on Tuesday.

Nika opened the table of numbers. Every value in that range was identical: minus eighteen point zero. Nature never produces numbers like that. Real measurements wobble a little, even in the most stable ice, because instruments, ice and rock are never perfectly still.

"These aren't measurements," she whispered. "Somebody has typed them in. Somebody has replaced the real data with the numbers I was supposed to find." She looked over her shoulder, and the empty room suddenly felt full of people.
B2.proof: the numbers I was supposed to find
B2.q: What does Nika's last sentence imply about the person who changed the data?
o: That the person is a visitor from another station.
That the person knew what result the scientists were expecting.
That the computer wrote the numbers itself.
That Nika wrote the numbers by mistake.
B2.hint: Birinin 'bulmam gereken sayılar' yazması onun neyi bildiğini gösterir?
B2.why: Veriyi değiştiren kişi, bilim insanlarının hangi sonucu beklediğini biliyordu; yani proje hakkında bilgisi olan biri.

text: On Sunday Nika sat down at the main computer in the station. She wanted to examine all the temperature data from the drill, so she opened the files and plotted a graph, expecting the usual smooth, gentle curve of ice growing colder with depth.
The line sloped downward as it should. At one hundred metres it was cold. At two hundred it was colder. At three hundred it was colder still. Then something strange happened.

Between three hundred and sixty and four hundred and twenty metres, the line became completely flat. It was a perfectly straight line at minus eighteen degrees, exactly the figure she had expected to see on Tuesday, and exactly the figure that the textbooks would have predicted.

Nika opened the table of numbers. Every value in that range was identical: minus eighteen point zero. Nature never produces numbers like that. Real measurements wobble a little, even in the most stable ice, because instruments, ice and rock are never perfectly still.

"These aren't measurements," she whispered. "Somebody has typed them in. Somebody has replaced the real data with the numbers I was supposed to find, which means that somebody knew, before I did, what I was going to find." She looked over her shoulder, and the empty room suddenly felt full of people.
C1.proof: somebody knew, before I did, what I was going to find
C1.q: What troubling conclusion does Nika reach?
o: That she made a mistake with her own calculations.
That the textbooks are wrong about ice.
That another person understood the true result earlier than she did.
That the computer is older than the station.
C1.hint: Birinin onun bulacağı sonucu 'kendisinden önce' bilmesi ne anlama gelir?
C1.why: Nika, birinin gerçek sonucu kendisinden önce bildiğini ve bu yüzden gerçek verileri beklenen sayılarla değiştirdiğini fark ediyor.

eps.title: Three Empty Disks
eps.recap: Tomas yedek diskleri kontrol etti ve üçünün de silinmiş olduğunu gördü. Disklerin biçimlendirme tarihi, ışıkların ilk titrediği geceyle aynıydı.

text: On Monday, Nika told Tomas about the flat line. Tomas was quiet for a moment. "Then we need the backup disks," he said. "We keep the old data on three hard disks. They are in the engine room."
They went to the engine room. It was warm and smelled of oil. In a metal box, there were three small black disks. Each disk had a label: A, B and C.
Tomas connected disk A to his laptop. He waited. The screen said: 'Empty'. He tried disk B. Empty. He tried disk C. Empty.
"All three," he said. "Nobody does that by accident." He opened a small window with information. "Look at this. These disks were erased on the twelfth. At eleven o'clock at night."
Nika took out her notebook. She looked at Kit's page of dates. "The twelfth," she said. "That is the first night the lights went down."
A2.proof: These disks were erased on the twelfth. At eleven o'clock at night.
A2.q: What is important about the date on the disks?
o: It is the same night as the first power problem.
It is the day Nika arrived at the station.
It is the day the storm started.
It is the birthday of the engineer.
A2.hint: Disklerin silindiği gece ile Kit'in not ettiği ilk gece arasındaki ilişkiyi bul.
A2.why: Diskler on ikisinde gece on birde silinmiş; bu, ışıkların ilk titrediği geceyle aynı. Yani iki olay birbiriyle bağlantılı.

Nika took out her notebook and found Kit's page of dates. "The twelfth," she said slowly. "That was the first night the lights flickered. The same hour."
B1.proof: That was the first night the lights flickered. The same hour.

o: The disks were damaged by the cold.

B1.why: Silme saati ve elektrik dalgalanması aynı; ikisini de aynı kişinin ya da aynı işlemin yaptığı düşünülebilir.

"He's still deleting something."
C1.proof: He's still deleting something
C1.q: What does Tomas conclude from the nightly power use?
o: That the disks are slowly repairing themselves.
That the generator needs more fuel.
That the station will lose power tomorrow.
That the person is still erasing or changing data every night.
C1.hint: Her gece saat on birde devam eden güç çekimi neye işaret eder?
C1.why: Elektrik dalgalanmaları her gece sürdüğüne göre, Tomas birinin hâlâ bir şeyleri sildiğini ya da değiştirdiğini düşünüyor.

eps.title: Kit Saw Something
eps.recap: Kit, Dr. Brandt'ın geceleri elinde bir kutuyla jeneratör kulübesine gittiğini gördüğünü söyledi. Ancak korkuyordu ve yalnızca aşçı olduğunu hatırlatıyordu.

text: On Tuesday evening, Kit asked Nika to come to the kitchen. He closed the door and he turned the radio down. His hands were not still.
"I have to tell you something," he said. "But please do not say that I told you. I am only the cook."
"You are not only the cook," said Nika. "You are my friend." Kit smiled for a short moment. Then he looked serious again.
"Three nights ago, I could not sleep," he said. "I went to the window. I saw Dr. Brandt outside in the snow. It was very late. He was carrying a grey case. He walked to the generator hut."
"And did he come back?" asked Nika. "Yes," said Kit. "After one hour. And the next night he did the same. And the next one."
A2.proof: I saw Dr. Brandt outside in the snow
A2.q: What does Kit's story suggest about Dr. Brandt?
o: He likes to take walks in the snow.
He does something secret at night in the generator hut.
He is looking for his lost keys.
He is repairing the kitchen.
A2.hint: Brandt'ın gece, kutuyla ve her gece aynı yere gitmesi neyi gösteriyor?
A2.why: Brandt her gece elinde bir kutuyla jeneratör kulübesine gidiyor; bu, orada gizli bir iş yaptığını düşündürüyor.

text: On Tuesday evening Kit asked Nika to come to the kitchen. He closed the door and turned the radio down. His hands were restless on the counter.
"I need to tell you something," he said. "But please don't say it came from me. I'm only the cook."

"Three nights ago I couldn't sleep, so I stood at my window. Dr. Brandt was outside in the snow, very late. He was carrying a grey case, and he walked straight to the generator hut."

"Did he come back?" asked Nika. "After an hour. And the next night he did exactly the same. And the one after that." Nika thought of the flickering lights, which happened every night at eleven, in the hour when Dr. Brandt was supposedly asleep.
B1.proof: supposedly asleep
B1.q: How do the new details connect with earlier events?
o: Brandt is sleeping while the generator is working.
Kit has been complaining about the cold.
Brandt's nightly visits match the time of the power problems.
The power problems stopped when Brandt went outside.
B1.hint: Brandt'ın geceleri çıkması ile elektrik dalgalanmalarının saatini karşılaştır.
B1.why: Brandt her gece aynı saatlerde dışarı çıkıyor ve elektrik dalgalanmaları da aynı saatte oluyor; iki olay birbiriyle örtüşüyor.

text: On Tuesday evening Kit asked Nika to come to the kitchen. He closed the door and turned the radio down. His hands were restless on the counter, rearranging spoons that were already tidy.
"I need to tell you something," he said. "But please don't say it came from me. I'm only the cook."
"You're not only the cook," said Nika. "You're my friend." Kit smiled for a moment, then grew serious again.

"Three nights ago I couldn't sleep, so I stood at my window. Dr. Brandt was outside in the snow, very late. He was carrying a grey case, and he walked straight to the generator hut. I told myself it was none of my business."

"Did he come back?" asked Nika. "After an hour. And the next night he did exactly the same. And the one after that." Nika thought of the lights flickering every night at eleven, in the hour when the station's director was supposedly asleep. Neither of them spoke. In a small station in the dark, there are few things more frightening than a regular habit.
B2.proof: there are few things more frightening than a regular habit
B2.q: Why does the narrator say a 'regular habit' can be frightening?
o: Because habits are always dangerous in winter.
Because Kit is afraid of the dark.
Because the director sleeps too little.
Because repeated secret behaviour suggests a deliberate plan.
B2.hint: Düzenli tekrarlanan gizli bir davranış neyi düşündürür?
B2.why: Her gece tekrarlanan gizli davranış, bunun tesadüf değil planlı olduğunu düşündürüyor; korkutucu olan da bu.

text: On Tuesday evening Kit asked Nika to come to the kitchen. He closed the door and turned the radio down. His hands were restless on the counter, rearranging spoons that were already tidy.
"I need to tell you something," he said. "But please don't say it came from me. I'm only the cook."
"You're not only the cook," said Nika. "You're the one person here who notices everything." Kit smiled for a moment, then grew serious again.

"Three nights ago I couldn't sleep, so I stood at my window. Dr. Brandt was outside in the snow, very late. He was carrying a grey case, and he walked straight to the generator hut. I told myself it was none of my business. I've been telling myself that for three nights."

"Did he come back?" asked Nika. "After an hour. And the next night he did exactly the same. And the one after that." Nika thought of the lights flickering every night at eleven, in the hour when the station's director was supposedly asleep. Neither of them spoke. In a small station in the middle of the polar night, she reflected, there are few things more frightening than a regular habit, because a habit means a plan, and a plan means that someone has already decided what the rest of us are not allowed to know.
C1.proof: a habit means a plan
C1.q: What reasoning does Nika use in the last sentence?
o: She reasons that repeated secret acts show a planned intention to hide something.
She believes Brandt is just following the weather.
She thinks Kit is lying about what he saw.
She believes the generator is making the noise.
C1.hint: Düzenli alışkanlıktan plana, plandan gizlenen bilgiye uzanan akıl yürütmeyi izle.
C1.why: Nika, tekrarlanan gizli davranışın bir plana işaret ettiğini ve birinin bir şeyi bilinçli olarak sakladığını düşünüyor.

eps.title: The Storm Closes In
eps.recap: Büyük bir fırtına istasyonu vurdu ve kimse dışarı çıkamaz hâle geldi. Dr. Brandt, tüm dış mesajların kendi onayından geçmesini emretti.

text: On Wednesday, the wind came. It started slowly. By the evening, it was a monster. It screamed round the buildings and threw hard snow against the windows. The sky was black.

Dr. Brandt called everyone to the main room. He stood in front of them. "Listen carefully," he said. "This is a very big storm. Nobody goes outside. Nobody. The doors will be closed until it stops. Maybe three days. Maybe a week."
People looked at each other. They were afraid, but they understood. A person can die very fast in such wind.
"One more thing," said Dr. Brandt. "The radio is only for emergencies. If anybody wants to send a message to the outside, he must show it to me first. I will read it. Then Kit can send it."
Nika felt something cold in her stomach. "Why must you read every message?" she asked. "To avoid panic," said Dr. Brandt, and he smiled.
A2.proof: he must show it to me first
A2.q: What does Brandt's new rule do?
o: It saves energy for the generator.
It helps Kit to rest at night.
It gives him control of what the station tells the outside world.
It prevents people from going outside.
A2.hint: Her mesajı Brandt'ın önceden okuması neyi sağlar?
A2.why: Dışarıya giden her mesaj önce Brandt'ın onayından geçiyor; bu, istasyondan çıkan bilgiyi kontrol etmesini sağlıyor.

text: On Wednesday the wind arrived. It began slowly, but by evening it was a monster, screaming round the buildings and hurling hard snow against the windows. The sky had turned black at noon, and now even the lights outside were swallowed by the white.

Dr. Brandt called everyone to the main room. "Listen carefully," he said. "This is a very serious storm. Nobody goes outside, not for any reason. The doors stay closed until it ends. That could be three days. It could be a week."
People exchanged glances. They were afraid, but they understood. In wind like this, a man can lose his way ten metres from the door and never be found.
"One more thing," said Dr. Brandt. "The radio is for emergencies only. If anyone wishes to send a message outside the station, he must show it to me first. I will read it, and then Kit will send it."

Nika felt something cold settle in her stomach. "Why must you read every message?" she asked. "To avoid unnecessary panic," said Dr. Brandt, and he smiled in a way that made her think of the new lock on his cabinet.
B1.proof: he smiled in a way that made her think of the new lock on his cabinet
B1.q: What is Nika suggesting by connecting Brandt's smile with the lock?
o: That Brandt is happy to see her.
That Brandt wants to repair the cabinet.
That Brandt is afraid of the storm.
That Brandt's rule is another way of keeping information hidden.
B1.hint: Brandt'ın gülümsemesini kilitle ilişkilendiren Nika neyi ima ediyor?
B1.why: Nika, mesajları denetleme kuralını dolaptaki yeni kilit gibi bilgiyi saklamaya yönelik bir önlem olarak görüyor.

B2.why: Fırtına kimsenin istasyondan çıkmasına ya da dışarıyla serbestçe iletişim kurmasına izin vermiyor; bu, saklayacak şeyi olan Brandt'a avantaj sağlıyor.

eps.title: Red Crystals
eps.recap: Nika, buz örneklerini mikroskopta inceledi ve içinde buza ait olmayan küçük, kızıl-gri mineral kristalleri buldu. Bunlar ancak ısıtılmış kayadan gelebilirdi.

text: During the storm, Nika worked in the small laboratory. She had twelve pieces of ice from the drill. Each piece was long and clear like glass. She cut a thin slice from each one and put it under the microscope.
The first slice was beautiful and clean. The second one was clean too. The third, the fourth, the fifth. Then she looked at slice number nine.
Inside the ice, there were tiny crystals. They were red and grey, and they were very small, smaller than grains of sand. Nika looked at them for a long time.

She knew the minerals in ice. Dust from the sky gives one kind of mineral. Dust from mountains gives another kind. But these crystals were different. She had seen crystals like these only once before, in a museum, in a piece of volcanic rock.
"These do not come from ice," she said quietly. "They come from rock. And the rock was very, very hot."
A2.proof: They come from rock. And the rock was very, very hot.
A2.q: What does Nika learn from the crystals?
o: The ice was made from sand.
The microscope is dirty.
The ice came from the museum.
Heated rock may be close to the place where the ice was drilled.
A2.hint: Kristaller buzdan değil kayadan geliyor ve kaya çok sıcakmış: bu ne anlama gelir?
A2.why: Kristaller ısıtılmış kayadan geliyor; yani sondaj noktasının yakınında sıcak bir kaya, bir ısı kaynağı olabilir.

text: During the storm Nika worked in the small laboratory with twelve cylinders of ice from the drill. Each was long and clear like glass. She cut a thin slice from each one and placed it under the microscope.
The first slice was clean and beautiful. So was the second, the third, the fourth, the fifth. Then she looked at slice number nine.
Inside the ice lay tiny crystals, red and grey, smaller than grains of sand. Nika studied them for a long time without moving.

She knew the minerals normally found in ice. Dust from the atmosphere carries one kind, dust from mountains another. These crystals were different. She had seen crystals like them only once before, in a museum, in a piece of volcanic rock.
"These don't come from the ice," she said quietly. "They come from rock. And that rock was once extremely hot."
B1.proof: that rock was once extremely hot.
B1.q: Why are the crystals important for the investigation?
o: They suggest a heat source below the ice that could explain the temperature.
They prove that the ice is very old.
They show that the ice contains salt.
They are the reason the data disappeared.
B1.hint: Isıtılmış kayadan gelen kristaller sıcaklık okumasına nasıl bağlanır?
B1.why: Kristaller ısınmış kayadan geliyor; bu, buzun altında sıcaklığı yükselten bir ısı kaynağı olabileceğini düşündürüyor.

text: During the storm Nika worked in the small laboratory with twelve cylinders of ice from the drill. Each was long and clear like glass. She cut a thin slice from each one and placed it under the microscope, labelling the images in her careful handwriting.
The first slice was clean and beautiful. So was the second, the third, the fourth, the fifth. Then she looked at slice number nine.
Inside the ice lay tiny crystals, red and grey, smaller than grains of sand. Nika studied them for a long time without moving, while outside the wind tried to tear the roof off.

She knew the minerals normally found in ice. Dust from the atmosphere carries one kind, dust from mountains another. These crystals were different. She had seen crystals like them only once before, in a museum, in a piece of volcanic rock.

"These don't come from the ice," she said quietly. "They come from rock. And that rock was once extremely hot." She thought of the minus three degrees at four hundred metres, and for the first time she allowed herself to put the two facts side by side.
B2.proof: she allowed herself to put the two facts side by side
B2.q: What does Nika do at the end of the passage?
o: She decides to stop the experiment.
She links the crystals with the unexpected warm temperature.
She compares two kinds of ice.
She sends the crystals to the museum.
B2.hint: İki gerçeği 'yan yana koymak' ne anlama gelir?
B2.why: Nika kristallerle sıcaklık ölçümünü ilişkilendiriyor: ikisini birlikte düşünerek buzun altında bir ısı kaynağı olabileceği sonucuna varıyor.

The first slice was clean and beautiful. So was the second, the third, the fourth, the fifth. Then she looked at slice number nine.
Inside the ice lay tiny crystals, red and grey, smaller than grains of sand. Nika studied them for a long time without moving, while outside the wind tried to tear the roof off.

She knew the minerals normally found in ice. Dust from the atmosphere carries one kind, dust from mountains another. These crystals were different. She had seen crystals like them only once before, in a museum, in a piece of volcanic rock.

C1.q: Why does Nika hide her theory at the back of her notebook?
o: Because her notebook has no space left.

C1.why: Teorisi o kadar olağandışı ki, Nika onu henüz kimseyle paylaşmaya hazır değil ve kayıt altına bile çekingenlikle alıyor.

eps.title: Core C-12
eps.recap: Nika, kristaller bulduğu örneğin etiketinde 'C-12, 450 m' yazdığını fark etti. Resmî kayıtlar ise sondajın 400 metrede bittiğini gösteriyordu; yani birisi daha derine inmişti.

text: Nika wanted to know exactly where the red crystals came from. She went back to the ice slice number nine. She looked at the small paper label in the tube. It was written in a pen, in fine letters. She read it slowly.
The label said: 'Core C-12. Depth: 450 m.'
Nika read it three times. Then she took her own work diary. She turned to the page for the drilling. There, in her own handwriting, was the last depth of the drill: four hundred metres. Not more.
"Four hundred," she said. "The drill stopped at four hundred. But this piece of ice is from four hundred and fifty."
She called Tomas. He came and looked at the label. "I did not drill to four hundred and fifty," he said. "Nobody in my team did." They looked at each other. "Then who did?" asked Nika.
A2.proof: The drill stopped at four hundred.
A2.q: What is surprising about the label?
o: It shows a depth that the official drilling never reached.
It is written in a different language.
It shows the wrong date.
It belongs to another station.
A2.hint: Etiketteki derinlik ile resmî kayıtlardaki derinliği karşılaştır.
A2.why: Etikette 450 m yazıyor ama sondaj resmî olarak 400 metrede durmuş; yani birisi kayıt dışı daha derine inmiş.

text: Nika wanted to know exactly where the red crystals had come from. She returned to ice slice number nine and looked at the small paper label tucked into the tube. It was written in pen, in fine, careful letters.
The label said: 'Core C-12. Depth: 450 m.'

Nika read it three times. Then she opened her own work diary and turned to the page for the drilling. There, in her own handwriting, was the final depth reached by the drill: four hundred metres. Not one metre more. She had checked it herself, and Tomas had signed beneath it.
"Four hundred," she said. "The drill stopped at four hundred. But this piece of ice comes from four hundred and fifty."
She called Tomas, who came and read the label. "I never drilled to four hundred and fifty," he said. "Nobody on my team did." They looked at each other across the bench. "Then who did?" asked Nika.
B1.proof: Nobody on my team did.
B1.q: What can we conclude from the label and the diary?
o: The drill has a mistake in its measurements.
Someone drilled deeper than the official records show.
Nika wrote the wrong number in her diary.
Tomas drilled secretly at night.
B1.hint: Etiket ile günlük birbiriyle çelişiyor; bu çelişki neyi ortaya çıkarıyor?
B1.why: Resmî kayıt 400 m ama örnek 450 m; ekibi dışındaki biri daha derine sondaj yapmış olmalı.

text: Nika wanted to know exactly where the red crystals had come from. She returned to ice slice number nine and looked at the small paper label tucked into the tube. It was written in pen, in fine, careful letters that she did not recognise.
The label said: 'Core C-12. Depth: 450 m.'

Nika read it three times. Then she opened her own work diary and turned to the page for the drilling. There, in her own handwriting, was the final depth reached by the official drill: four hundred metres. Not one metre more. She had checked it herself, and Tomas had signed beneath it.

She called Tomas, who came and read the label. "I never drilled to four hundred and fifty," he said. "Nobody on my team did." They looked at each other across the bench. "Then who did?" asked Nika. Neither answered, but both were thinking of a grey case, a generator hut and eleven o'clock at night.
B2.proof: a grey case, a generator hut and eleven o'clock at night
B2.q: What do the final images suggest?
o: That the drill is stored in the generator hut.
That Kit is guilty of the secret drilling.
That they suspect the secret drilling was done by Brandt at night.
That the ice was carried in a grey case.
B2.hint: Gri kutu, jeneratör kulübesi ve gece saat on bir: hangi karakterle bağlantılı?
B2.why: Gri kutu, jeneratör kulübesi ve gece on bir Kit'in anlattığı Brandt'ın gizli faaliyetini çağrıştırıyor; ikisi de gizli sondajı onun yapmış olabileceğini düşünüyor.

text: Nika wanted to know exactly where the red crystals had come from. She returned to ice slice number nine and looked at the small paper label tucked into the tube. It was written in pen, in fine, careful letters that she did not recognise.
The label said: 'Core C-12. Depth: 450 m.'

Nika read it three times. Then she opened her own work diary and turned to the page for the drilling. There, in her own handwriting, was the final depth reached by the official drill: four hundred metres. Not one metre more.
"Four hundred," she said. "The drill stopped at four hundred. But this piece of ice comes from four hundred and fifty."

She called Tomas, who came and read the label. "I never drilled to four hundred and fifty," he said. "Nobody on my team did." They looked at each other across the bench. "Then who did?" asked Nika. Neither answered, but both were thinking of a grey case, a generator hut and eleven o'clock at night. Somebody had been drilling in the dark, below the depth that the records admitted to, and had then removed every trace of it, except for a single label, written by a man who had not thought that anyone would ever read it.
C1.proof: written by a man who had not thought that anyone would ever read it
C1.q: What is the most important inference from the last sentence?
o: That the label was written by Tomas.
That the label was printed by a machine.
That the ice cores were thrown away.
That the person hid the evidence well but overlooked one small detail.
C1.hint: Her izi sildiği halde unuttuğu tek ayrıntı ne?
C1.why: Kişi tüm izleri silmiş ama bir etiketi gözden kaçırmış; yani delil olarak küçük bir ayrıntı kalmış.

eps.title: A Mirror Under the Ice
eps.recap: Nika, istasyondaki radarla buzun altını taradı ve 450 metre civarında düz, parlak bir yüzey gördü. Bu yüzey, radar dalgalarını ayna gibi yansıtıyordu.

text: The storm was quiet at last. Nika went to the radar room. It was small and warm. Tomas was already there with two cups of tea.
"Let us scan the ice under the station," said Nika. Tomas pressed a button. The machine began to hum. On the screen, there were many grey lines. They showed the layers of the ice.
At the bottom, there was a thick bright line. It was flat and very straight. It did not look like rock. Rock is rough. This line was smooth.
"It is like a mirror," whispered Tomas. "The radar hits it and comes back very strong."
Nika looked at the number on the screen: 450 metres. "Brandt said the ice here is solid to the bottom," she said. "This is not solid."
A2.q: What does the bright flat line on the radar suggest?
o: The radar is broken and shows nothing.
There is something smooth under the ice that is not normal rock.
The ice is very thin there.
The station is built on a mirror.
A2.hint: Radar çizgisinin düz ve parlak olması kayanın ne olmadığını gösteriyor?
A2.why: Pürüzsüz ve parlak bir yansıma, kaya gibi pürüzlü bir şeyin değil, buzun altındaki farklı ve düz bir yüzeyin işareti.

text: The storm had finally gone quiet. Nika went to the radar room, a small, warm space where Tomas was already waiting with two cups of tea.
"Let's scan the ice beneath the station," said Nika. Tomas pressed a button and the machine began to hum. The screen filled with grey lines, each one a layer of ice.
At the bottom, one thick bright line appeared. It was flat and perfectly straight. Rock is rough and the radar usually returns a messy signal from it, but this line was smooth.
"It looks like a mirror," whispered Tomas. "The signal hits it and comes straight back, very strong."

Nika checked the depth: 450 metres. "Dr. Brandt told us the ice here is solid all the way down," she said. "This is not solid." Nika wrote the number in her notebook and underlined it, because she did not trust her memory tonight.
B1.proof: Rock is rough
B1.q: Why is the smooth bright line important?
o: It proves the radar works perfectly in storms.
It shows that the ice is made of glass.
It is unlike rock, so something else must lie beneath the ice.
It means Tomas drew it by hand.
B1.hint: Kayanın pürüzlü olduğunu bilmek, düz çizgiyi nasıl yorumlatır?
B1.why: Kaya pürüzlüdür ve dağınık yansıma verir; düz parlak çizgi, altta kaya dışında başka bir şey olduğunu gösterir.

text: The storm had finally gone quiet. Nika went to the radar room, a small, warm space where Tomas was already waiting with two cups of tea that had long since gone lukewarm.
"Let's scan the ice beneath the station," said Nika. Tomas pressed a button and the machine began to hum. The screen filled with grey lines, each one a layer of ice laid down over thousands of years.

At the bottom, one thick bright line appeared. It was flat and perfectly straight. Rock is rough, and the radar usually returns a messy signal from it, but this line was smooth, the way a calm surface of water is smooth.
"It looks like a mirror," whispered Tomas. "The signal hits it and comes straight back, very strong."

Nika checked the depth: 450 metres. That was fifty metres deeper than the point where the core had been labelled 'official'. "Dr. Brandt told us the ice here is solid all the way down," she said. "This is not solid." Her heart was beating so loudly that she was sure Tomas could hear it, and the little room felt much too small.
B2.proof: the way a calm surface of water is smooth
B2.q: What is Nika beginning to suspect?
o: That the ice is melting at the surface.
That the radar picked up the storm.
That Tomas is lying to her.
That liquid water may lie beneath the ice.
B2.hint: Yazar düz yüzeyi neye benzetiyor?
B2.why: Sakin bir su yüzeyine benzetiyor; yani Nika buzun altında sıvı su olabileceğinden şüpheleniyor.

text: The storm had finally gone quiet. Nika went to the radar room, a small, warm space where Tomas was already waiting with two cups of tea that had long since gone lukewarm.

"Let's scan the ice beneath the station," said Nika. Tomas pressed a button and the machine began to hum. The screen filled with grey lines, each one a layer of ice laid down over thousands of years, like the pages of a very slow diary.

At the bottom, one thick bright line appeared. It was flat and perfectly straight. Rock is rough, and the radar usually returns a messy signal from it, but this line was smooth, the way a calm surface of water is smooth, and it reflected the signal with an almost insulting clarity.
"It looks like a mirror," whispered Tomas. "The signal hits it and comes straight back, very strong."

Nika checked the depth: 450 metres. That was fifty metres deeper than the point where the core had been labelled 'official'. "Dr. Brandt told us the ice here is solid all the way down," she said. "This is not solid." Neither of them dared to say the word that was forming in both their minds, because once it was said aloud, it could not be unsaid.
C1.proof: once it was said aloud, it could not be unsaid
C1.q: Why do Nika and Tomas avoid saying the word?
o: Because naming the discovery would make it real and carry serious consequences.
Because they have forgotten the word.
Because the radio room is forbidden for talking.
Because the word is not in English.
C1.hint: Neden kimse o kelimeyi ağzına almıyor?
C1.why: Keşfi (bir göl) adlandırmak onu gerçek kılar ve ciddi sonuçları olur; bu yüzden ikisi de söylemekten çekiniyor.

eps.title: The Arithmetic of Water
eps.recap: Tomas radar yansımasının gücünü hesapladı. Sonuç, yüzeyin sert kayadan değil, sıvı sudan geldiğini gösteriyordu. Buzun altında bir göl olabilirdi.

text: Tomas worked all night. He sat in front of his computer with a pencil behind his ear. He put numbers into a long table. Nika sat beside him and watched.
"Every material sends back a different amount of the radar signal," he explained. "Ice sends back a little. Rock sends back more. But water sends back almost everything."
At five in the morning, he stopped. He wrote one number on a piece of paper. Then he wrote another number below it. They were almost the same.
"The first number is the signal from our bright line," he said. "The second number is the signal from a lake in Greenland. Nika, they are the same."
Nika covered her mouth with her hand. "A lake," she said. "Under four hundred and fifty metres of ice."
A2.q: What did Tomas find with his numbers?
o: The signal is too weak to understand.
The radar has a mistake in its software.
The signal matches the one from a lake, so there may be a lake under the ice.
The ice contains no water at all.
A2.hint: Tomas'ın iki sayısının neredeyse aynı olması neyi gösteriyor?
A2.why: Parlak çizginin sinyali bilinen bir gölünkiyle aynı; yani buzun altında bir göl olabilir.

text: Tomas worked all night. He sat in front of his computer with a pencil behind his ear and typed numbers into a long table while Nika sat beside him and watched.
"Every material sends back a different amount of the radar signal," he explained. "Ice returns a little. Rock returns more. But water returns almost everything."
At five in the morning he stopped, wrote one number on a scrap of paper, and wrote a second number beneath it. They were almost identical.
"The first is the signal from our bright line," he said. "The second is the signal from a known lake under the Greenland ice. Nika, they match."

Nika covered her mouth with her hand. "A lake," she said. "Under four hundred and fifty metres of ice." Then she smiled, tired and amazed, and Tomas laughed quietly, as if somebody might be listening through the wall.
B1.proof: they match
B1.q: What conclusion can be drawn from the two matching numbers?
o: That Greenland and Antarctica are connected.
That Tomas copied the numbers.
That the station is in Greenland.
That the reflecting surface behaves like liquid water, not rock.
B1.hint: İki sinyalin eşleşmesinden hangi sonuç çıkar?
B1.why: Yüzey, kaya gibi değil sıvı su gibi davranıyor; Grönland'daki bilinen gölle benzerlik bunu destekliyor.

text: Tomas worked all night. He sat in front of his computer with a pencil behind his ear and typed numbers into a long table while Nika sat beside him and watched, drinking coffee she did not taste.

"Every material sends back a different amount of the radar signal," he explained. "Ice returns a little. Rock returns more. But water returns almost everything, because it is so smooth and so different from what lies above it."
At five in the morning he stopped, wrote one number on a scrap of paper, and wrote a second number beneath it. They were almost identical.
"The first is the signal from our bright line," he said. "The second is the signal from a known lake under the Greenland ice. Nika, they match."

Nika covered her mouth with her hand. "A lake," she said. "Under four hundred and fifty metres of ice." It was exactly the kind of discovery that changes a career, she thought, and exactly the kind that someone might want to keep quiet. Tomas just nodded and began to check the numbers a second time.
B2.proof: exactly the kind that someone might want to keep quiet
B2.q: Who might Nika be thinking of at the end?
o: Dr. Brandt, who has been hiding data.
The cook, Kit, who makes dinner.
The radar machine.
A reporter outside.
B2.hint: Nika sessiz kalmak isteyebilecek kimseyi düşünüyor olabilir?
B2.why: Nika, verileri saklayan Dr. Brandt'ı düşünüyor; bulgu bir kariyeri değiştirebilir ama biri bunu gizli tutmak isteyebilir.

text: Tomas worked all night. He sat in front of his computer with a pencil behind his ear and typed numbers into a long table while Nika sat beside him and watched, drinking coffee she did not taste.

"Every material sends back a different amount of the radar signal," he explained. "Ice returns a little. Rock returns more. But water returns almost everything, because it is so smooth and so different from what lies above it."
At five in the morning he stopped, wrote one number on a scrap of paper, and wrote a second number beneath it. They were almost identical.
"The first is the signal from our bright line," he said. "The second is the signal from a known lake under the Greenland ice. Nika, they match."

Nika covered her mouth with her hand. "A lake," she said. "Under four hundred and fifty metres of ice." It was exactly the kind of discovery that changes a career, she thought, and exactly the kind that someone might want to keep quiet if it threatened the programme that paid for it. Science was supposed to follow the numbers wherever they led. Whether the people who funded it would do the same was an entirely different question.
C1.proof: Whether the people who funded it would do the same was an entirely different question.
C1.q: What tension does the passage end on?
o: Between day and night.
Between following the scientific evidence and protecting funding.
Between Nika and Tomas.
Between ice and rock.
C1.hint: Bilimin sayıları takip etmesi ile finansörlerin tepkisi arasında nasıl bir gerilim var?
C1.why: Bilim kanıtı takip eder ama projeyi finanse edenler aynı şekilde davranmayabilir; gerilim doğruluk ile fon arasında.

eps.title: Heat From Below
eps.recap: Nika ve Tomas, buzun altındaki suyun neden donmadığını açıkladı: yerin derinliklerinden gelen ısı. Daha önce okunan -3 derecelik anormal sıcaklık da bu ısının izi olmalıydı.
