text: "But why is the water not frozen?" asked Kit. She was holding a big wooden spoon and a pot of soup. Nika and Tomas looked at her. It was a good question.
Tomas drew a picture on the white board. He drew the ice on the top. He drew the lake under it. Under the lake, he drew a red circle.
"Deep in the earth, there is very hot rock," he said. "In some places, the heat comes up slowly. It warms the ground. It warms the water above it."
"Geothermal heat," said Nika. "That is why the ice at 400 metres was minus three, not minus eighteen. The heat from below makes it warmer."
Kit put down the spoon. "So the sensor was right all the time," she said. "And Dr. Brandt was wrong."
A2.q: Why is the water under the ice not frozen?
o: Salt in the water melts the ice.
The station heater is too strong.
Kit's soup is too hot.
Heat from the hot rock deep under the ground warms it.
A2.hint: Gölün donmaması hangi ısıyla açıklanıyor?
A2.why: Yerin derinliklerindeki sıcak kayadan yukarı çıkan ısı suyu donmaktan koruyor.

text: "But why isn't the water frozen?" asked Kit. She stood in the doorway holding a wooden spoon and a pot of soup. Nika and Tomas looked at her. It was a very good question.
Tomas drew on the white board: the ice on top, the lake beneath it, and under the lake a red circle.
"Deep in the earth there is very hot rock," he said. "In some places the heat rises slowly through the crust. It warms the ground, and it warms the water that sits on top of it."
"Geothermal heat," said Nika. "That's why the ice at 400 metres read minus three instead of minus eighteen. The warmth from below was leaking upwards."
Kit put down the spoon. "So the sensor was right all along," she said slowly. "And Dr. Brandt was wrong about the calibration." Tomas smiled and nodded.
B1.proof: The warmth from below was leaking upwards.
B1.q: How does the new theory explain the strange temperature?
o: Warmth rising from below made the ice warmer than expected.
The sensor was badly calibrated.
The weather outside got warmer.
The core was taken from a different place.
B1.hint: -3 derecelik sıcaklık hangi yeni açıklamayla uyuşuyor?
B1.why: Aşağıdan yukarı sızan sıcaklık buzu beklenenden daha sıcak yapmış; sensör hatalı değil.

text: "But why isn't the water frozen?" asked Kit. She stood in the doorway holding a wooden spoon and a pot of soup. Nika and Tomas looked at her. It was a very good question, and neither of them had asked it yet.
Tomas drew on the white board: the ice on top, the lake beneath it, and under the lake a red circle.

"Deep in the earth there is very hot rock," he said. "In some places the heat rises slowly through the crust. It warms the ground, and it warms the water that sits on top of it. Under thick ice, the water cannot lose its heat easily, so it stays liquid, like a pot with a lid on it."
"Geothermal heat," said Nika. "That's why the ice at 400 metres read minus three instead of minus eighteen. The warmth from below was leaking upwards."

Kit put down the spoon. "So the sensor was right all along," she said slowly. "And Dr. Brandt was wrong about the calibration." Nika did not answer. She was wondering whether he had been wrong, or merely very convenient.
B2.proof: wrong, or merely very convenient
B2.q: What is Nika wondering about Dr. Brandt?
o: Whether he likes soup.
Whether he made a mistake or lied on purpose.
Whether he can fix the radar.
Whether he will visit Kit.
B2.hint: 'Yanlış mı yoksa sadece işine mi geliyor' sorusu neyi sorguluyor?
B2.why: Nika, Brandt'ın gerçekten hata mı yaptığını yoksa bilerek mi yanlış söylediğini merak ediyor.

text: "But why isn't the water frozen?" asked Kit. She stood in the doorway holding a wooden spoon and a pot of soup. Nika and Tomas looked at her. It was a very good question, and neither of them had asked it yet.
Tomas drew on the white board: the ice on top, the lake beneath it, and under the lake a red circle.

"Deep in the earth there is very hot rock," he said. "In some places the heat rises slowly through the crust. It warms the ground, and it warms the water that sits on top of it. Under thick ice, the water cannot lose its heat easily, so it stays liquid, like a pot with a lid on it."

"Geothermal heat," said Nika. "That's why the ice at 400 metres read minus three instead of minus eighteen. The warmth from below was leaking upwards. The sensor never lied; it was the only honest instrument on this base."

Kit put down the spoon. "So the sensor was right all along," she said slowly. "And Dr. Brandt was wrong about the calibration." Nika did not answer. She was wondering whether he had been wrong, or merely very convenient, and whether a man who erases three backup disks can ever be described as having simply made a mistake.
C1.proof: whether a man who erases three backup disks can ever be described as having simply made a mistake
C1.q: What does Nika's last thought imply?
o: That backup disks are always faulty.
That Brandt is a good technician.
That deleting backups points to deliberate concealment rather than an error.
That mistakes are impossible.
C1.hint: Üç yedek diski silmek bir hata olarak açıklanabilir mi?
C1.why: Üç yedeğin silinmesi tesadüf olamaz; Nika bunun bilinçli bir gizleme olduğunu düşünüyor.

eps.title: Stop the Work
eps.recap: Nika bulgularını Dr. Brandt'a götürdü. Brandt sakin bir sesle her şeyin bir yanlış anlama olduğunu söyledi ve sondaj çalışmasının derhal durdurulmasını emretti.

text: On Sunday morning, Nika walked into Dr. Brandt's office with the radar pictures. Tomas stood behind her. Her hands were cold, but her voice was strong.
She put the pictures on his desk and explained everything. The bright line. The numbers. The warm ice. The lake.
Dr. Brandt listened. He did not interrupt. His face did not change. When she finished, he took off his glasses and cleaned them slowly.
"This is very interesting, Nika," he said. "But it is only a mistake in your machine. We cannot build a theory on a mistake. I want all drilling to stop today. All of it."
"But why?" asked Tomas. "Because I am the director," said Dr. Brandt, "and I said so."
A2.proof: I want all drilling to stop today.
A2.q: Why is Brandt's reaction strange?
o: A scientist should be curious about new data, but he wants to stop the work.
He is too happy about the discovery.
He shouts and breaks the radar.
He asks to join the drilling.
A2.hint: Brandt'ın tepkisi bir bilim insanından beklenenden nasıl farklı?
A2.why: Yeni bir bulgu karşısında merak etmesi gerekirken sondajı durdurmak istiyor; bu garip ve şüpheli.

text: On Sunday morning Nika walked into Dr. Brandt's office carrying the radar pictures, with Tomas behind her. Her hands were cold but her voice was steady.
She laid the pictures on his desk and explained everything: the bright line, the numbers, the warm ice, the lake.
Dr. Brandt listened without interrupting. His face did not change. When she finished he took off his glasses and cleaned them slowly with a corner of his sweater.
"This is very interesting, Nika," he said. "But it's almost certainly an error in your equipment. One cannot build a theory on an error. I want all drilling to stop today. All of it."

"Why?" asked Tomas. "Because I am the director," said Dr. Brandt, "and I have said so." Nika said nothing, but she looked at the pictures on the desk, and Tomas took her arm and led her out of the room.
B1.proof: Because I am the director
B1.q: What does Brandt's answer show?
o: That he follows the rules of the base.
That he gives an order without a scientific reason.
That he agrees with Tomas.
That he is afraid of the cold.
B1.hint: Brandt neden sondajın durdurulmasını istediğini açıklıyor mu?
B1.why: Hayır; bilimsel bir gerekçe vermek yerine yalnızca müdür olduğunu söylüyor, yani otoritesini kullanıyor.

text: On Sunday morning Nika walked into Dr. Brandt's office carrying the radar pictures, with Tomas behind her. Her hands were cold but her voice was steady, and she had rehearsed every sentence the night before.
She laid the pictures on his desk and explained everything: the bright line, the numbers, the warm ice, the lake.

Dr. Brandt listened without interrupting. His face did not change at all, which struck her as strange, because a man hearing about a possible discovery under his own station should show at least a flicker of excitement. When she finished he took off his glasses and cleaned them slowly with a corner of his sweater.
"This is very interesting, Nika," he said. "But it's almost certainly an error in your equipment. One cannot build a theory on an error. I want all drilling to stop today. All of it."
"Why?" asked Tomas. "Because I am the director," said Dr. Brandt, "and I have said so." Outside in the corridor Tomas whispered that he had never seen the director so nervous, and Nika agreed.
B2.proof: a man hearing about a possible discovery under his own station should show at least a flicker of excitement
B2.q: What does Nika notice about Brandt?
o: That he is very excited and happy.
That he does not understand English.
That he shows no excitement, which suggests he already knew.
That he is angry at Tomas.
B2.hint: Brandt'ın yüzünün hiç değişmemesi neden dikkat çekici?
B2.why: Böyle bir keşif haberine hiç heyecan göstermemesi, konuyu zaten bildiğini düşündürüyor.

text: On Sunday morning Nika walked into Dr. Brandt's office carrying the radar pictures, with Tomas behind her. Her hands were cold but her voice was steady, and she had rehearsed every sentence the night before.
She laid the pictures on his desk and explained everything: the bright line, the numbers, the warm ice, the lake.

Dr. Brandt listened without interrupting. His face did not change at all, which struck her as strange, because a man hearing about a possible discovery under his own station should show at least a flicker of excitement. When she finished he took off his glasses and cleaned them slowly with a corner of his sweater, a gesture she had noticed whenever he needed a moment to choose his words.
"This is very interesting, Nika," he said. "But it's almost certainly an error in your equipment. One cannot build a theory on an error. I want all drilling to stop today. All of it."

"Why?" asked Tomas. "Because I am the director," said Dr. Brandt, "and I have said so." It was not an argument. It was the sound of a man who has run out of arguments and is falling back on his title, and Nika, for the first time, was certain that he was afraid.
C1.proof: the sound of a man who has run out of arguments
C1.q: What does Nika conclude from his final reply?
o: That he is the best scientist on the base.
That he will help them tomorrow.
That he never says anything important.
That he has no real reason and is afraid.
C1.hint: Brandt'ın 'çünkü ben müdürüm' demesi neyin işareti?
C1.why: Argümanı kalmayan birinin unvanına sığınması; Nika bunun korkunun işareti olduğunu anlıyor.

eps.title: A Second Hole
eps.recap: Brandt sondajı yasaklayınca Nika, Tomas ve Kit gizlice ikinci bir sondaj noktası belirlediler: istasyonun yaklaşık iki kilometre doğusunda, radarda aynı parlak yüzeyin başladığı yer.

text: That night, Nika, Tomas and Kit sat together in the kitchen. The lights were off. Only one small lamp was on. They talked very quietly.
"We cannot stop," said Nika. "If we are right, this is a very big discovery. We need a sample of the water. Only a sample can prove it."

Tomas opened a map. "The radar shows the bright surface starts here," he said. He put his finger on a point two kilometres east of the station. "It is far from the main building. Brandt cannot see it from his window."
"The small drill and the sledge are in the garage," said Kit. "I have the key." She smiled for the first time in days.
They shook hands in the dark. Outside, the wind was starting to blow again.
A2.proof: Brandt cannot see it from his window.
A2.q: Why do they choose a point far from the main building?
o: They want to be closer to the kitchen.
They want to work in secret so Dr. Brandt does not stop them.
They like walking in the snow.
The ice is softer there.
A2.hint: İkinci sondaj noktası neden istasyondan uzak seçildi?
A2.why: Brandt'ın pencereden görmemesi için; ekip gizlice çalışmak istiyor.

text: That night Nika, Tomas and Kit sat together in the kitchen with the lights off and a single small lamp burning. They spoke in whispers.
"We can't stop," said Nika. "If we're right, this is an enormous discovery, and only a water sample can prove it."

Tomas unrolled a map. "The radar shows the bright surface beginning here," he said, touching a point two kilometres east of the station. "It's far from the main building. Brandt can't see it from his window, and he never goes that way."
"The small drill and the sledge are in the garage," said Kit. "I have the key." She smiled for the first time in days.
They shook hands in the dark. Outside, the wind was beginning to rise again. Nika looked at her friends and felt that, for the first time in weeks, they were a real team.
B1.proof: only a water sample can prove it
B1.q: What do they need to prove the lake exists?
o: A permission letter from Brandt.
A new radar machine.
A real sample of water from beneath the ice.
A map from the library.
B1.hint: Göl hakkında kesin kanıtı ne sağlar?
B1.why: Yalnızca buzun altından alınacak gerçek bir su örneği teoriyi kanıtlayabilir.

text: That night Nika, Tomas and Kit sat together in the kitchen with the lights off and a single small lamp burning. They spoke in whispers, like children planning a prank, though the stakes were of a very different kind.
"We can't stop," said Nika. "If we're right, this is an enormous discovery, and only a water sample can prove it. Radar pictures are an opinion. Water is a fact."

Tomas unrolled a map. "The radar shows the bright surface beginning here," he said, touching a point two kilometres east of the station. "It's far from the main building. Brandt can't see it from his window, and he never goes that way. The ice there is slightly thinner, too."
"The small drill and the sledge are in the garage," said Kit. "I have the key." She smiled for the first time in days.

They shook hands in the dark. Outside, the wind was beginning to rise again, and none of them dared to mention that a second storm was forecast for Wednesday. Nika wrote down the coordinates on her hand, so that nobody could find a paper.
B2.proof: Radar pictures are an opinion. Water is a fact.
B2.q: What distinction does Nika make?
o: That radar is always wrong.
That water is more expensive than radar.
That facts never need proof.
That indirect measurements are interpretations while a physical sample is direct proof.
B2.hint: 'Radar resimleri bir görüştür, su bir gerçektir' sözü ne demek istiyor?
B2.why: Dolaylı ölçümler yoruma açıktır; fiziksel bir numune ise doğrudan kanıttır.

text: That night Nika, Tomas and Kit sat together in the kitchen with the lights off and a single small lamp burning. They spoke in whispers, like children planning a prank, though the stakes were of a very different kind.
"We can't stop," said Nika. "If we're right, this is an enormous discovery, and only a water sample can prove it. Radar pictures are an opinion. Water is a fact."

Tomas unrolled a map. "The radar shows the bright surface beginning here," he said, touching a point two kilometres east of the station. "It's far from the main building. Brandt can't see it from his window, and he never goes that way. The ice there is slightly thinner, too, which makes the drilling quicker."

"The small drill and the sledge are in the garage," said Kit. "I have the key." She smiled for the first time in days. It occurred to Nika that of the four people on the base who were not the director, three had now decided to disobey him, and that this was how quiet rebellions usually begin: not with a speech, but with a key.
They shook hands in the dark. Outside, the wind was beginning to rise again, and none of them dared to mention that a second storm was forecast for Wednesday.
C1.proof: this was how quiet rebellions usually begin: not with a speech, but with a key
C1.q: What point does the narrator make about the group's decision?
o: That small practical steps, not grand words, start a real act of defiance.
That Kit makes speeches.
That the key is magical.
That the director gave them the key.
C1.hint: 'Sessiz isyanlar bir konuşmayla değil, bir anahtarla başlar' ifadesi ne anlatıyor?
C1.why: Gerçek bir itaatsizlik büyük sözlerle değil, küçük ve pratik adımlarla başlar; burada anahtar o adımı temsil ediyor.

eps.title: Not Before the Meeting
eps.recap: Kit, radyo odasında Brandt'ın merkeze gönderdiği kısa mesajı yakaladı: 'Fon toplantısından önce hiçbir şey çıkmamalı.' Mesaj, Brandt'ın bulguyu bilerek gizlediğini gösteriyordu.

text: On Monday night, Kit went to the radio room to clean the table. She always did this at nine o'clock. Nobody was there. The big radio was quiet.
Then the machine made a small sound. A message was coming out of the printer. Kit looked at it. She did not want to read it. But she read it.
The message was from Dr. Brandt to the headquarters. It was short. It said: 'Nothing must come out before the funding meeting. Keep all results inside the station. B.'
Kit read it again. Her hand began to shake. 'Nothing must come out.' It was exactly what Nika was afraid of.
She folded the paper and put it in her pocket. Then she ran to find Nika.
A2.proof: Nothing must come out before the funding meeting.
A2.q: What does the message prove?
o: Brandt wants to celebrate the discovery.
Brandt is asking for more food.
Brandt wants to hide the results from the outside world on purpose.
Brandt is writing to his family.
A2.hint: Mesajın içeriği Brandt hakkında neyi kanıtlıyor?
A2.why: Brandt, fon toplantısına kadar sonuçların dışarı çıkmamasını istiyor; yani verileri bilerek saklıyor.

text: On Monday night Kit went to the radio room to clean the table, as she did every evening at nine. Nobody was there, and the big radio was silent.
Then the printer gave a small click and a message began to slide out. Kit glanced at it. She did not want to read it, but she read it anyway.
It was from Dr. Brandt to headquarters, and it was short: 'Nothing must come out before the funding meeting. Keep all results inside the station. B.'
She read it again, and her hand began to shake. 'Nothing must come out.' It was exactly what Nika had been afraid of.

She folded the paper, slipped it into her pocket, and ran to find Nika. She ran down the long corridor, past the kitchen and the laboratory, until she saw a thin line of light under Nika's door and knocked quickly three times.
B1.proof: Keep all results inside the station.
B1.q: Why is the funding meeting mentioned?
o: Brandt wants to invite everyone to a party.
The meeting is about the weather.
The meeting is only for cooks.
Brandt fears that the discovery could affect the money for the project.
B1.hint: Brandt neden 'fon toplantısını' özellikle anıyor?
B1.why: Brandt, keşfin proje için gelen paraya zarar verebileceğinden korkuyor; bu yüzden sonuçları toplantıya kadar gizlemek istiyor.

text: On Monday night Kit went to the radio room to clean the table, as she did every evening at nine. Nobody was there, and the big radio was silent, like an animal asleep.

Then the printer gave a small click and a message began to slide out. Kit glanced at it. She did not want to read it, but she read it anyway, because curiosity is stronger than discretion in a place where nothing else ever happens.
It was from Dr. Brandt to headquarters, and it was short: 'Nothing must come out before the funding meeting. Keep all results inside the station. B.'
She read it again, and her hand began to shake. 'Nothing must come out.' It was exactly what Nika had been afraid of: not a mistake, not a calibration problem, but a decision.

She folded the paper, slipped it into her pocket, and ran to find Nika. She ran down the long corridor, past the kitchen and the laboratory, until she saw a thin line of light under Nika's door and knocked quickly, three times, before anyone else could appear.
B2.proof: not a mistake, not a calibration problem, but a decision
B2.q: What does Kit realise from the message?
o: That Brandt's silence was intentional and planned.
That Brandt made a small technical error.
That the printer is broken.
That headquarters wrote the message.
B2.hint: Kit mesajdan hangi sonuca varıyor?
B2.why: Brandt'ın sessizliği bir hata değil, bilinçli bir karar; bunu mesajın içeriği gösteriyor.

text: On Monday night Kit went to the radio room to clean the table, as she did every evening at nine. Nobody was there, and the big radio was silent, like an animal asleep.

Then the printer gave a small click and a message began to slide out. Kit glanced at it. She did not want to read it, but she read it anyway, because curiosity is stronger than discretion in a place where nothing else ever happens.

It was from Dr. Brandt to headquarters, and it was short: 'Nothing must come out before the funding meeting. Keep all results inside the station. B.' The word 'results' was underlined twice, and beneath it, in a different ink, someone at headquarters had replied: 'Understood.'

She read it again, and her hand began to shake. 'Nothing must come out.' It was exactly what Nika had been afraid of: not a mistake, not a calibration problem, but a decision. And it appeared that Brandt was not alone in having made it.
She folded the paper, slipped it into her pocket, and ran to find Nika, her boots loud on the metal floor. It was a short message, but to Kit it seemed to weigh as much as the whole station.
C1.proof: someone at headquarters had replied: 'Understood.'
C1.q: What new problem does the reply 'Understood' raise?
o: That headquarters wants to help Nika.
That someone at headquarters may also be involved in hiding the results.
That the printer writes replies by itself.
That Kit wrote the answer.
C1.hint: Merkezden gelen 'Anlaşıldı' cevabı ne ima ediyor?
C1.why: Merkezdeki birinin de saklama kararından haberdar olduğunu, yani sorunun yalnızca Brandt ile sınırlı olmayabileceğini ima ediyor.

eps.title: The Sent Folder
eps.recap: Kit, radyo odasındaki eski kayıtlarda Brandt'ın aylardır merkeze gönderdiği e-postaları buldu. E-postalar, sıcaklık verilerinin 'uygunsuz' olduğunu ve rapora alınmaması gerektiğini söylüyordu.

text: On Tuesday, Kit stayed in the radio room after dinner. The storm was loud outside. She opened the old computer. It was slow, and its screen was yellow.
She found a folder with a strange name: 'Sent, Director'. It had more than a hundred messages. Kit began to read them from the bottom.

The first one was from October. 'Dear headquarters. The temperature in the deep core is higher than expected. I do not think we should include it in the report.' The second one was from November. 'Please do not ask the team about the radar results.'
Message after message, the sentences were the same. Hide this number. Remove this graph. Do not tell the team.
Kit counted. There were fifty-three messages. She printed twelve of them. Her hand was cold when she took the paper from the printer.
A2.q: What do the old emails show?
o: Brandt sent birthday greetings.
Brandt asked for more food.
Brandt wrote a story.
Brandt hid unusual data from the team and the report for months.
A2.hint: Eski e-postalar Brandt hakkında ne gösteriyor?
A2.why: Brandt aylarca olağandışı verileri ekipten ve rapordan saklamış.

text: On Tuesday Kit stayed in the radio room after dinner while the storm roared outside. She switched on the old computer, which was slow and had a yellowish screen.
She found a folder with a strange name: 'Sent, Director'. It held more than a hundred messages, and Kit began reading from the bottom.

The first was from October. 'Dear headquarters. The temperature in the deep core is higher than expected. I do not think we should include it in the report.' The next was from November: 'Please do not ask the team about the radar results.'
Message after message the instructions were the same. Hide this number. Remove this graph. Do not tell the team.
Kit counted fifty-three messages and printed twelve of them. Her hand was cold as she took the pages from the printer. She put the pages in her jacket and zipped it up.
B1.proof: I do not think we should include it in the report.
B1.q: What was Brandt's aim in the October message?
o: To keep the unexpected temperature out of the official report.
To ask headquarters for new equipment.
To report an accident.
To invite headquarters to visit.
B1.hint: Brandt Ekim mesajında neyi amaçlıyor?
B1.why: Beklenmedik sıcaklık verisinin resmî rapora girmemesini istiyor.

text: On Tuesday Kit stayed in the radio room after dinner while the storm roared outside. She switched on the old computer, which was slow and had a yellowish screen that made everything look like an old photograph.
She found a folder with a strange name: 'Sent, Director'. It held more than a hundred messages, and Kit began reading from the bottom, as one reads the history of a quarrel.

The first was from October. 'Dear headquarters. The temperature in the deep core is higher than expected. I do not think we should include it in the report.' The next was from November: 'Please do not ask the team about the radar results.'
Message after message the instructions were the same. Hide this number. Remove this graph. Do not tell the team.

Kit counted fifty-three messages and printed twelve of them. Her hand was cold as she took the pages from the printer. What shocked her was not the secrecy itself, but the tone: courteous, tidy, almost bureaucratic, the language of a man who had convinced himself that he was merely managing a difficulty.
B2.proof: the language of a man who had convinced himself that he was merely managing a difficulty
B2.q: What does Kit notice about the tone of the emails?
o: That they are angry and rude.
That they are polite and calm, as if Brandt believed he was doing nothing wrong.
That they are written in code.
That they are in a foreign language.
B2.hint: Kit e-postaların üslubunda neyi fark ediyor?
B2.why: Üslup kibar ve sakin; Brandt yaptığında yanlış bir şey görmüyormuş gibi.

text: On Tuesday Kit stayed in the radio room after dinner while the storm roared outside. She switched on the old computer, which was slow and had a yellowish screen that made everything look like an old photograph.
She found a folder with a strange name: 'Sent, Director'. It held more than a hundred messages, and Kit began reading from the bottom, as one reads the history of a quarrel.

The first was from October. 'Dear headquarters. The temperature in the deep core is higher than expected. I do not think we should include it in the report.' The next was from November: 'Please do not ask the team about the radar results.'
Message after message the instructions were the same. Hide this number. Remove this graph. Do not tell the team.

Kit counted fifty-three messages and printed twelve of them. Her hand was cold as she took the pages from the printer. What shocked her was not the secrecy itself, but the tone: courteous, tidy, almost bureaucratic, the language of a man who had convinced himself that he was merely managing a difficulty. Fifty-three small decisions, none of them dramatic, had added up to a disaster of silence. She zipped the pages inside her jacket.
C1.proof: Fifty-three small decisions, none of them dramatic, had added up to a disaster of silence.
C1.q: What point does the narrator make?
o: That fifty-three is a lucky number.
That the emails were dramatic.
That many small, quiet choices together created a serious cover-up.
That the disaster was a storm.
C1.hint: Elli üç küçük karar birlikte neye dönüşmüş?
C1.why: Tek tek dramatik olmayan birçok küçük karar, birlikte ciddi bir gizleme oluşturmuş.

eps.title: The Director Speaks
eps.recap: Nika, Tomas ve Kit çıktıları Brandt'ın önüne koydu. Brandt uzun süre sustu, sonra bulgunun açıklanmasının projeyi bitireceğinden korktuğunu itiraf etti: fon kesilirse istasyon kapanacaktı.

text: On Wednesday morning, Nika, Tomas and Kit went to Dr. Brandt's office. Kit put twelve papers on the desk. Nobody spoke. The wind hit the windows.
Brandt looked at the first paper. Then the second. He looked up. His face was grey and tired. For the first time, he looked old.
"Yes," he said, quietly. "It is true. I hid the data."

He took off his glasses. "For twenty years, I worked for this station. Every year the money gets smaller. I thought: if we tell them about the warm ice, they will send new teams and close our project. I thought they would call it a failure."
He looked at Nika. "I was afraid. I am still afraid. If this base closes, forty people lose their jobs."
A2.q: Why did Brandt hide the data?
o: He was afraid the project would lose its money and the station would close.
He wanted to win a prize.
He wanted to leave the base.
He did not know about the data.
A2.hint: Brandt veriyi neden sakladığını söylüyor?
A2.why: Bulgunun projenin parasını keseceğinden ve istasyonun kapanacağından korkmuş.

text: On Wednesday morning Nika, Tomas and Kit walked into Dr. Brandt's office. Kit laid twelve printed pages on the desk. Nobody spoke, and the wind beat against the windows.
Brandt looked at the first page, then the second. When he raised his head his face was grey and tired. For the first time he looked old.
"Yes," he said quietly. "It's true. I hid the data."

He took off his glasses. "For twenty years I have worked for this station. Every year the budget shrinks. I thought that if we reported warm ice, headquarters would send new people and shut our project down. I thought they would call it a failure."
He looked at Nika. "I was afraid, and I still am. If this base closes, forty people lose their jobs." Nika said nothing. She only nodded, because she understood how hard it had been to say.
B1.proof: forty people lose their jobs
B1.q: What responsibility does Brandt feel?
o: Concern for his own garden.
Concern for the staff and the survival of the station.
Concern for the weather.
Concern for a prize.
B1.hint: Brandt veriyi saklarken hangi sorumluluğu hissediyor?
B1.why: İstasyonun devamı ve kırk kişinin işi için kaygı duyuyor.

text: On Wednesday morning Nika, Tomas and Kit walked into Dr. Brandt's office. Kit laid twelve printed pages on the desk. Nobody spoke, and the wind beat against the windows like an impatient visitor.
Brandt looked at the first page, then the second. When he raised his head his face was grey and tired. For the first time he looked old.
"Yes," he said quietly. "It's true. I hid the data."

He took off his glasses. "For twenty years I have worked for this station. Every year the budget shrinks. I thought that if we reported warm ice, headquarters would send new people and shut our project down. I thought they would call it a failure, not a discovery."

He looked at Nika. "I was afraid, and I still am. If this base closes, forty people lose their jobs. I told myself that I was protecting them. Perhaps I was only protecting myself." Nika said nothing at first. She only nodded, because she understood how hard those words had been to say, and Tomas looked at the floor, and Kit's eyes were wet.
B2.proof: Perhaps I was only protecting myself.
B2.q: What does Brandt's last sentence show?
o: That he is proud of himself.
That he blames Nika.
That he is beginning to doubt his own justification.
That he is joking.
B2.hint: Brandt son cümlesinde ne itiraf ediyor?
B2.why: Kendi gerekçesinden şüphe etmeye başlıyor; belki yalnızca kendini koruyordu.

text: On Wednesday morning Nika, Tomas and Kit walked into Dr. Brandt's office. Kit laid twelve printed pages on the desk. Nobody spoke, and the wind beat against the windows like an impatient visitor.
Brandt looked at the first page, then the second. When he raised his head his face was grey and tired. For the first time he looked old.
"Yes," he said quietly. "It's true. I hid the data."

He took off his glasses. "For twenty years I have worked for this station. Every year the budget shrinks. I thought that if we reported warm ice, headquarters would send new people and shut our project down. I thought they would call it a failure, not a discovery."

He looked at Nika. "I was afraid, and I still am. If this base closes, forty people lose their jobs. I told myself that I was protecting them. Perhaps I was only protecting myself." It was the most honest sentence Nika had ever heard from him, and she realised, with a strange reluctance, that she did not hate him. Fear had made him dishonest; it had not made him wicked, and the difference mattered to what they would do next. Tomas and Kit stood beside her without a word.
C1.proof: Fear had made him dishonest; it had not made him wicked
C1.q: How does Nika now view Brandt?
o: As a hero.
As a stranger.
As a joke.
As a frightened man who acted wrongly, not as a purely evil person.
C1.hint: Nika, Brandt'a artık nasıl bakıyor?
C1.why: Korkudan dolayı yanlış yapan ama kötü niyetli olmayan biri olarak görüyor.

eps.title: More Than a Lake
eps.recap: Nika, Brandt'a bulgunun projeyi bitirmeyeceğini, aksine onu kurtarabileceğini anlattı: buzun altındaki göl, yıllardır aranan bir keşif olabilirdi. Brandt ilk kez umutla başını kaldırdı.

text: Nika sat down in front of Dr. Brandt. She was not angry now. She spoke slowly.

"Dr. Brandt, you are afraid that this discovery will close the station. I think the opposite. A lake under four hundred and fifty metres of ice, kept warm by the earth, is a very rare thing. Scientists have looked for places like this for many years."

"Because water that has been closed away for a long time can contain very old life. Tiny living things that have never seen the sun. It may tell us how life lives in hard places, even on other planets."
Brandt listened. His hands were on his knees. "Do you think the money will not stop?" he asked.
"I think it will grow," said Nika. "A new discovery makes people want to give money. A hidden discovery makes them angry."
A2.proof: A hidden discovery makes them angry.
A2.q: What is Nika's main argument?
o: The station should close.
Sharing the discovery will help the project, while hiding it will cause problems.
Brandt should leave.
Water is boring.
A2.hint: Nika Brandt'ı hangi gerekçeyle ikna etmeye çalışıyor?
A2.why: Keşfi paylaşmanın projeye yardımcı olacağını, saklamanın ise sorun çıkaracağını savunuyor.

text: Nika sat down opposite Dr. Brandt. She was no longer angry, and she spoke slowly.

"Dr. Brandt, you're afraid this discovery will close the station. I believe the opposite. A lake beneath four hundred and fifty metres of ice, kept warm by the Earth itself, is extremely rare. Scientists have searched for places like this for decades."

"Because water sealed away for a very long time can contain ancient life: tiny organisms that have never seen the sun. It could teach us how life survives in the harshest places, even on other planets."
Brandt listened, his hands on his knees. "And you think the money won't stop?" he asked.
"I think it will grow," said Nika. "A new discovery makes people want to give. A hidden discovery makes them furious." Tomas nodded and said that he would help to write the report that very night.
B1.proof: A new discovery makes people want to give.
B1.q: Why does Nika think the funding will grow?
o: Because Brandt will pay for it.
Because the weather will improve.
Because an important discovery attracts interest and support.
Because the lake is deep.
B1.hint: Nika fonların neden artacağını düşünüyor?
B1.why: Önemli bir keşif ilgi ve destek çeker.

text: Nika sat down opposite Dr. Brandt. She was no longer angry, and she spoke slowly, choosing every word as one chooses footholds on a steep slope.

"Dr. Brandt, you're afraid this discovery will close the station. I believe the opposite. A lake beneath four hundred and fifty metres of ice, kept warm by the Earth itself, is extremely rare. Scientists have searched for places like this for decades."

"Because water sealed away for a very long time can contain ancient life: tiny organisms that have never seen the sun. It could teach us how life survives in the harshest places, even on other planets."
Brandt listened, his hands on his knees. "And you think the money won't stop?" he asked.

"I think it will grow," said Nika. "A new discovery makes people want to give. A hidden discovery, once it is found out, makes them furious, and this one will be found out, because the ice is not going to keep our secret." Tomas nodded and said that he would help to write the report that very night, and Kit promised hot tea for everybody.
B2.proof: the ice is not going to keep our secret
B2.q: What does Nika imply in the final sentence?
o: That ice can speak.
That the secret is safe.
That the station is made of ice.
That the truth will come out sooner or later, so it is better to tell it themselves.
B2.hint: 'Buz bizim sırrımızı saklamayacak' ne anlama geliyor?
B2.why: Gerçek er ya da geç ortaya çıkacak; bu yüzden kendilerinin açıklaması daha iyi.

text: Nika sat down opposite Dr. Brandt. She was no longer angry, and she spoke slowly, choosing every word as one chooses footholds on a steep slope.

"Dr. Brandt, you're afraid this discovery will close the station. I believe the opposite. A lake beneath four hundred and fifty metres of ice, kept warm by the Earth itself, is extremely rare. Scientists have searched for places like this for decades."

"Because water sealed away for a very long time can contain ancient life: tiny organisms that have never seen the sun. It could teach us how life survives in the harshest places, even on other planets. Funding committees do not close the base that stands on top of such a thing; they build a bigger one."
Brandt listened, his hands on his knees. "And you think the money won't stop?" he asked.

"I think it will grow," said Nika. "A new discovery makes people want to give. A hidden discovery, once it is found out, makes them furious, and this one will be found out, because the ice is not going to keep our secret." For a long moment the director said nothing. Then, very slowly, as if the muscles had forgotten how, he began to smile.
C1.proof: as if the muscles had forgotten how
C1.q: What does Brandt's slow smile suggest?
o: That he feels hope for the first time in a long while.
That he is mocking Nika.
That he is in pain.
That he is about to cry from anger.
C1.hint: Brandt'ın yavaşça gülümsemesi neyi gösteriyor?
C1.why: Uzun zamandır ilk kez umut hissettiğini gösteriyor.

eps.title: Water at Last
eps.recap: Kit'in verdiği anahtarla ekip gizli kalmaya gerek kalmadan ikinci sondaja gitti. Brandt da onlara katıldı. İki kilometre doğuda alınan su örneğinde mikroskop altında küçük canlı izleri göründü.

text: On Thursday, the wind was weaker. Nika, Tomas, Kit and Dr. Brandt put on thick red coats. They took the small drill and the sledge from the garage. This time they did not hide.
They walked two kilometres east in the snow. The sky was dark blue. Their lamps made small yellow circles on the ice.
At the marked point, Tomas started the drill. It went down slowly. The noise was loud. After three hours, the drill stopped. Dark water came up in the hole.
Nika filled a small bottle. She held it close to her chest to keep it warm. They went back to the station as fast as they could.
In the laboratory, she put one drop under the microscope. She looked for a long time. Then she said, in a very small voice: "They are moving."
A2.q: What does Nika see under the microscope?
o: A broken drill.
Sand and stones.
Tiny living organisms in the water from under the ice.
Her own face.
A2.hint: Nika mikroskopta ne görüyor burada?
A2.why: Buzun altından çıkan suda hareket eden küçük canlılar görüyor.

text: On Thursday the wind had weakened. Nika, Tomas, Kit and Dr. Brandt pulled on thick red coats and took the small drill and the sledge from the garage. This time they were not hiding.
They walked two kilometres east through the snow beneath a dark-blue sky, their lamps making small yellow circles on the ice.
At the marked point Tomas started the drill. It went down slowly and noisily. After three hours it stopped, and dark water welled up in the hole.
Nika filled a small bottle and held it against her chest to keep it from freezing. They hurried back to the station.

In the laboratory she put a single drop under the microscope and looked for a long time. Then she said, in a very small voice: "They're moving." They carried it carefully, and Kit made hot tea for everyone.
B1.proof: They're moving.
B1.q: What is the significance of this moment?
o: It shows that the drop is boiling.
It proves that the microscope is broken.
It shows that Nika is dizzy.
It suggests that living organisms exist in the lake under the ice.
B1.hint: 'Hareket ediyorlar' sözünün önemi nedir?
B1.why: Buzun altındaki gölde canlı organizmalar olabileceğini düşündürüyor.

text: On Thursday the wind had weakened. Nika, Tomas, Kit and Dr. Brandt pulled on thick red coats and took the small drill and the sledge from the garage. This time they were not hiding, and the strange freedom of it made the walk feel almost like a holiday.
They walked two kilometres east through the snow beneath a dark-blue sky, their lamps making small yellow circles on the ice.
At the marked point Tomas started the drill. It went down slowly and noisily. After three hours it stopped, and dark water welled up in the hole.
Nika filled a small bottle and held it against her chest to keep it from freezing. They hurried back to the station.

In the laboratory she put a single drop under the microscope and looked for a long time. Then she said, in a very small voice: "They're moving." Nobody in the room breathed. They were the first human beings to look at the inhabitants of a world that had been sealed away since long before there were any humans to look.
B2.proof: a world that had been sealed away since long before there were any humans to look
B2.q: What does the last sentence emphasise?
o: The historic importance of seeing life from an isolated, ancient environment.
That the room was cold.
That the humans were old.
That the world was sold.
B2.hint: Son cümle hangi önemi vurguluyor?
B2.why: Uzun süre izole kalmış, çok eski bir ortamdaki yaşamı ilk kez görmenin tarihî önemini vurguluyor.

text: On Thursday the wind had weakened. Nika, Tomas, Kit and Dr. Brandt pulled on thick red coats and took the small drill and the sledge from the garage. This time they were not hiding, and the strange freedom of it made the walk feel almost like a holiday.
They walked two kilometres east through the snow beneath a dark-blue sky, their lamps making small yellow circles on the ice.
At the marked point Tomas started the drill. It went down slowly and noisily. After three hours it stopped, and dark water welled up in the hole.
Nika filled a small bottle and held it against her chest to keep it from freezing. They hurried back to the station.

In the laboratory she put a single drop under the microscope and looked for a long time. Then she said, in a very small voice: "They're moving." Nobody in the room breathed. They were the first human beings to look at the inhabitants of a world that had been sealed away since long before there were any humans to look. Brandt took off his glasses and wiped his eyes with his sleeve, and Nika did not pretend not to see it, because some things are too large for tact.
C1.proof: some things are too large for tact
C1.q: What does Brandt's reaction show?
o: That he is allergic to dust.
That the discovery has moved him deeply.
That he is bored.
That he wants to leave.
C1.hint: Brandt'ın gözlerini silmesi neyi gösteriyor burada?
C1.why: Bu keşif Brandt'ı derinden etkilemiş ve duygulandırmış.

eps.title: The Generator Stops
eps.recap: İkinci fırtına tam zamanında geldi. Gece yarısı ana jeneratör durdu, ısıtma kesildi ve istasyonun içindeki sıcaklık hızla düşmeye başladı. Yedek jeneratör ise bir türlü çalışmıyordu.

text: The second storm came on Friday. It was stronger than the first. The wind screamed. The station shook like a toy.
At midnight, all lights went out. There was a loud silence. Then somebody said, in the dark, "The generator."
Tomas ran to the hut with a torch. He opened the panel. The big engine was silent. He pressed the button again and again. Nothing.
"Try the spare one," shouted Nika. Tomas tried. The spare engine made a sad cough and stopped.
Inside the station, the temperature was already falling. On the wall thermometer, the red line went down: 14, 12, 10. Outside, it was minus forty-five.
A2.q: Why is the generator failure dangerous?
o: The lights are too bright.
The radio is too loud.
The food will be too hot.
Without heating, people could freeze in the extreme cold.
A2.hint: Jeneratörün durması neden bu kadar tehlikeli?
A2.why: Isıtma durunca dışarıdaki aşırı soğuk yüzünden içerisi donacak ve insanlar tehlikeye girecek.

text: The second storm arrived on Friday, stronger than the first. The wind screamed and the station shook like a toy.
At midnight all the lights went out. For a moment there was only a loud silence, and then somebody said in the dark, "The generator."
Tomas ran to the generator hut with a torch and opened the panel. The big engine was dead. He pressed the starter again and again. Nothing happened.
"Try the spare!" shouted Nika. Tomas tried it. The spare engine gave a sad cough and fell silent.

Inside the station the temperature was already dropping. On the wall thermometer the red line sank: 14, 12, 10. Outside it was minus forty-five. Nika grabbed her coat and the big torch and ran toward the hut. Kit started to collect blankets from every bedroom, and Brandt went to wake the others in the cold dark corridor.
B1.proof: The spare engine gave a sad cough and fell silent.
B1.q: What is the situation after the spare engine fails?
o: They have no source of power or heat, and the cold is increasing.
They have more power than before.
They are on holiday.
They can go outside safely.
B1.hint: Yedek motor da durunca durum nasıl?
B1.why: Elektrik ve ısı kaynağı kalmadı ve soğuk giderek artıyor.

text: The second storm arrived on Friday, stronger than the first. The wind screamed and the station shook like a toy in the hands of an angry child.
At midnight all the lights went out. For a moment there was only a loud silence, and then somebody said in the dark, "The generator."

Tomas ran to the generator hut with a torch and opened the panel. The big engine was dead. He pressed the starter again and again. Nothing happened. The fuel gauge showed that the tank was full, so the fault was not a simple lack of fuel.
"Try the spare!" shouted Nika. Tomas tried it. The spare engine gave a sad cough and fell silent.

Inside the station the temperature was already dropping. On the wall thermometer the red line sank: 14, 12, 10. Outside it was minus forty-five, and the wind was strong enough to knock a man off his feet. Nika grabbed her coat and the big torch and ran toward the hut. Kit started to collect blankets from every bedroom, and Brandt went to wake the others in the cold dark corridor, shouting that nobody should leave the building.
B2.proof: the fault was not a simple lack of fuel
B2.q: What can be inferred from the full fuel tank?
o: That the engine does not need fuel.
That the engine stopped for a reason other than empty fuel.
That the tank is broken.
That Tomas filled it recently.
B2.hint: Yakıt deposunun dolu olması ne gösteriyor?
B2.why: Motorun yakıt bittiği için değil, başka bir nedenle durduğunu gösteriyor.

text: The second storm arrived on Friday, stronger than the first. The wind screamed and the station shook like a toy in the hands of an angry child.
At midnight all the lights went out. For a moment there was only a loud silence, and then somebody said in the dark, "The generator."

Tomas ran to the generator hut with a torch and opened the panel. The big engine was dead. He pressed the starter again and again. Nothing happened. The fuel gauge showed that the tank was full, so the fault was not a simple lack of fuel.

"Try the spare!" shouted Nika. Tomas tried it. The spare engine gave a sad cough and fell silent. Two engines, each of which had passed inspection a month before, had failed within the same minute. Tomas, who did not believe in coincidences, put down his torch and began to think very carefully.

Inside the station the temperature was already dropping. On the wall thermometer the red line sank: 14, 12, 10. Outside it was minus forty-five, and the wind was strong enough to knock a man off his feet. Nika grabbed her coat and ran toward the hut, while Kit started to collect blankets from every bedroom and Brandt woke the others in the cold dark corridor.
C1.proof: Tomas, who did not believe in coincidences
C1.q: What does Tomas begin to suspect?
o: That the engines are too new.
That the inspection was a mistake.
That both engines may have been tampered with.
That the wind is lucky.
C1.hint: İki motorun aynı dakikada bozulması Tomas'a ne düşündürüyor?
C1.why: Tomas, iki motorun da aynı anda bozulmasının tesadüf olmadığını, kasıtlı müdahale olabileceğini düşünüyor.

eps.title: A Part Too Clean
eps.recap: Tomas, jeneratörün yakıt pompası kapağının yeni cilalanmış gibi parladığını fark etti; diğer parçaların hepsi yağ ve kirle kaplıydı. Bu parçanın yakın zamanda söküldüğü anlaşılıyordu.

text: Tomas lay on the cold floor of the generator hut. He held his torch in his teeth and looked inside the big engine. It was a mess of black oil and old dirt.
Everything was dark. Everything was dirty. But in the middle, there was one small metal part. It was shining like a new coin. It was the cover of the fuel pump.
Tomas touched it with his glove. There was no dirt. There was no oil. Four screws held it. The screws were bright and new.
"Nika," he called. "Come here. Look at this." Nika came and knelt next to him. "Nobody cleans only one part of an engine," said Tomas quietly. "Somebody took it off and put it back. Very recently."
Behind them, the door opened. Cold wind came in. Brandt stood in the door. He looked at the shining metal, and he did not move.
A2.proof: It was shining like a new coin.
A2.q: What does the clean part suggest?
o: Somebody removed and replaced it recently, so the engine was tampered with.
The engine is brand new.
The part is made of gold.
The hut was cleaned yesterday.
A2.hint: Parlayan bu parça neyi düşündürüyor bize?
A2.why: Biri parçayı yakın zamanda söküp yeniden takmış; motora müdahale edilmiş.

text: Tomas lay on the freezing floor of the generator hut with his torch between his teeth, looking inside the big engine. It was a mess of black oil and old grime.
Everything was dark and dirty, except for one small metal part that shone like a new coin: the cover of the fuel pump.
He touched it with his glove. There was no dirt and no oil on it. Four screws held it in place, and the screws were bright and unscratched.
"Nika," he called. "Come and look at this." She knelt beside him. "Nobody cleans just one part of an engine," said Tomas quietly. "Somebody took it off and put it back on. Very recently."
Behind them the door opened and cold wind poured in. Brandt stood in the doorway. He looked at the shining metal, and he did not move.
B1.proof: Nobody cleans just one part of an engine
B1.q: Why is the shining pump cover suspicious?
o: Because it is too dirty.
Because only that part is clean, showing that someone handled it recently.
Because it is made of plastic.
Because it is the biggest part.
B1.hint: Tek bir parçanın temiz olması neden şüpheli?
B1.why: Sadece o parça temiz; yakın zamanda biri ona dokunmuş.

text: Tomas lay on the freezing floor of the generator hut with his torch between his teeth, looking inside the big engine. It was a mess of black oil and old grime, the accumulated history of twenty winters.
Everything was dark and dirty, except for one small metal part that shone like a new coin: the cover of the fuel pump.
He touched it with his glove. There was no dirt and no oil on it. Four screws held it in place, and the screws were bright and unscratched.

"Nika," he called. "Come and look at this." She knelt beside him. "Nobody cleans just one part of an engine," said Tomas quietly. "Somebody took it off and put it back on. Very recently. And they were careful enough to wipe it, but not careful enough to wipe the rest of the room."

Behind them the door opened and cold wind poured in. Brandt stood in the doorway. He looked at the shining metal, and he did not move. He said nothing yet. He said nothing yet, and the torch light trembled in his hand.
B2.proof: not careful enough to wipe the rest of the room
B2.q: What does Tomas's remark reveal?
o: That the room is dirty everywhere.
That Tomas dislikes cleaning.
That the person who tampered with the part was careful but left a visible clue.
That the screws are old.
B2.hint: Tomas'ın 'odanın geri kalanını silmeyi unutmuş' demesi neyi gösteriyor?
B2.why: Parçaya müdahale eden kişi özenli davranmış ama temiz parlayan tek bir parça kendisini ele vermiş.

text: Tomas lay on the freezing floor of the generator hut with his torch between his teeth, looking inside the big engine. It was a mess of black oil and old grime, the accumulated history of twenty winters.
Everything was dark and dirty, except for one small metal part that shone like a new coin: the cover of the fuel pump.
He touched it with his glove. There was no dirt and no oil on it. Four screws held it in place, and the screws were bright and unscratched.

"Nika," he called. "Come and look at this." She knelt beside him. "Nobody cleans just one part of an engine," said Tomas quietly. "Somebody took it off and put it back on. Very recently. And they were careful enough to wipe it, but not careful enough to wipe the rest of the room."

Behind them the door opened and cold wind poured in. Brandt stood in the doorway. He looked at the shining metal, and he did not move. Nika looked at him, and for a moment the whole story seemed to balance on that one silent figure: the man who had hidden the data, the man who had wept at the microscope, and now the man who might have switched off the heat of forty people. Which of the three, she wondered, was the real Brandt?
C1.proof: Which of the three, she wondered, was the real Brandt?
C1.q: What question does Nika ask herself?
o: Whether Brandt is hungry.
Whether Brandt owns the generator.
Whether Tomas is Brandt's brother.
Whether Brandt is a liar, a repentant scientist, or a dangerous saboteur.
C1.hint: Nika, Brandt hakkında kendine hangi soruyu soruyor?
C1.why: Brandt'ın yalancı mı, pişman bir bilim insanı mı yoksa tehlikeli bir sabotajcı mı olduğunu merak ediyor.

eps.title: Brandt's Hands
eps.recap: Brandt, parçanın kendisinin söküp geri taktığını itiraf etti: ilk fırtınadan sonra radarın çalışmasını durdurmak istemişti. Sonra kendi ellerini jeneratörün içine uzattı ve ekibin gözleri önünde onu onardı.

text: Dr. Brandt stood in the door of the generator hut. The wind blew snow around his boots. Nobody spoke. Then he took one step forward.

"I took the cover off," he said. "Three days ago. I wanted to stop the radar. I thought, if the power goes off for one night, they cannot scan. I did not think about the storm. I did not think about the cold."
Nika looked at him. She was very angry, but she held it inside. There was no time. The thermometer in the station was now at six degrees.
"Can you fix it?" she asked. "Yes," said Brandt. "I must."

He took off his gloves. He lay down on the frozen floor. His fingers went inside the engine. Everyone watched. After twenty minutes, the engine coughed, and then it began to roar. The lights in the hut came on.
A2.q: What does Brandt confess?
o: He broke the radar by accident.
He removed the part himself to stop the radar, and now he fixes it.
He did not touch the engine.
He found the part on the floor.
A2.hint: Brandt ekibe tam olarak ne itiraf ediyor?
A2.why: Radarı durdurmak için parçayı kendisinin söktüğünü ve şimdi onarmaya çalıştığını.

text: Dr. Brandt stood in the doorway of the generator hut while the wind blew snow around his boots. Nobody spoke. Then he took one step forward.
"I took the cover off," he said. "Three days ago. I wanted to stop the radar. I thought that if the power failed for one night, you couldn't scan. I didn't think about the storm, or the cold."
Nika looked at him. She was furious, but she held it in, because there was no time. The thermometer inside the station now read six degrees.
"Can you fix it?" she asked. "Yes," said Brandt. "I have to."

He took off his gloves and lay down on the frozen floor, reaching into the engine. Everyone watched. After twenty minutes the engine coughed, spluttered, and then began to roar. The lights in the hut came on. The wind outside slowly began to calm down.
B1.proof: I didn't think about the storm, or the cold.
B1.q: What does this confession reveal about Brandt's earlier actions?
o: That he planned to freeze the team.
That he loves storms.
That he acted impulsively without thinking about the dangerous consequences.
That he forgot the engine.
B1.hint: Brandt'ın itirafı önceki hareketleri hakkında ne gösteriyor?
B1.why: Sonuçlarını düşünmeden, bir anlık korkuyla hareket ettiğini gösteriyor.

text: Dr. Brandt stood in the doorway of the generator hut while the wind blew snow around his boots. Nobody spoke. Then he took one step forward.

"I took the cover off," he said. "Three days ago. I wanted to stop the radar. I thought that if the power failed for one night, you couldn't scan. I didn't think about the storm, or the cold. That is the truth, and I'm ashamed of it."
Nika looked at him. She was furious, but she held it in, because there was no time for fury. The thermometer inside the station now read six degrees.
"Can you fix it?" she asked. "Yes," said Brandt. "I have to."

He took off his gloves and lay down on the frozen floor, reaching into the engine. Everyone watched. After twenty minutes the engine coughed, spluttered, and then began to roar. The lights in the hut came on, and with them, absurdly, a small cheer, which stopped almost as soon as it started. They were saved by the man who had endangered them, and nobody quite knew what to feel.
B2.proof: They were saved by the man who had endangered them
B2.q: What mixed feelings does the passage describe?
o: Pure joy.
Pure anger.
Boredom.
Relief at being saved combined with confusion about the person who saved them.
B2.hint: Ekip neden karışık duygular yaşıyor?
B2.why: Onları tehlikeye atan kişi aynı zamanda kurtardı; rahatlama ile kafa karışıklığı bir arada.

text: Dr. Brandt stood in the doorway of the generator hut while the wind blew snow around his boots. Nobody spoke. Then he took one step forward.

"I took the cover off," he said. "Three days ago. I wanted to stop the radar. I thought that if the power failed for one night, you couldn't scan. I didn't think about the storm, or the cold. That is the truth, and I'm ashamed of it."
Nika looked at him. She was furious, but she held it in, because there was no time for fury. The thermometer inside the station now read six degrees.
"Can you fix it?" she asked. "Yes," said Brandt. "I have to."

He took off his gloves and lay down on the frozen floor, reaching into the engine. Everyone watched. After twenty minutes the engine coughed, spluttered, and then began to roar. The lights in the hut came on, and with them, absurdly, a small cheer, which stopped almost as soon as it started. They were saved by the man who had endangered them, and nobody quite knew what to feel. Kit, who had said nothing all night, handed him a cup of hot tea. "You're an idiot," she said gently. "But you're our idiot." It was, Nika thought, a better verdict than any court could have given.
C1.proof: It was, Nika thought, a better verdict than any court could have given.
C1.q: What does Nika think of Kit's remark?
o: That it expresses both blame and forgiveness in a humane way.
That it is cruel.
That it is legally binding.
That it is meaningless.
C1.hint: Nika Kit'in sözünü neden 'bir mahkemeden daha iyi' buluyor?
C1.why: Söz hem suçlamayı hem bağışlamayı insani bir biçimde dile getiriyor.

eps.title: The Grey Case
eps.recap: Brandt, ekibi jeneratör kulübesinin arka köşesine götürdü ve gri bir kutuyu gösterdi. İçinde, silindiğini sandıkları tüm sondaj verilerinin kopyası olan üç disk vardı. Verileri hiç yok etmemiş, saklamıştı.

text: When the generator was working, the team was tired but happy. Tomas wanted to sleep. But Brandt said, "Wait. I want to show you something."
He took them to the back of the hut. Behind some old barrels, there was a grey metal case. It was the case that Kit had seen him carrying every night. He opened it with a small key.
Inside, there were three black discs. They were wrapped in soft cloth. On each, there was a label: 'Core. Radar. Temperature.'
"These are the original data," he said. "I did not destroy them. I could not. I am a scientist. I only moved them here, so nobody would find them."
Tomas took one disc and held it in both hands, like a baby. "Then it was never lost," he said, and he laughed, and then he wiped his eyes.
A2.q: Why is the grey case important?
o: It contains food.
It contains spare parts.
It contains the original data that everyone believed was lost.
It contains Brandt's clothes.
A2.hint: Bu gri kutu hikâyede neden önemli?
A2.why: Herkesin kaybolduğunu sandığı orijinal verileri içeriyor.

text: When the generator was running again the team was tired but happy. Tomas wanted to sleep, but Brandt said, "Wait. I want to show you something."
He led them to the back of the hut. Behind some old barrels stood a grey metal case, the one Kit had seen him carrying every night. He opened it with a small key.
Inside lay three black discs wrapped in soft cloth, each labelled: 'Core. Radar. Temperature.'
"These are the original data," he said. "I didn't destroy them. I couldn't. I'm a scientist. I only moved them here so that nobody would find them."

Tomas lifted one disc in both hands like a baby. "So it was never lost," he said, laughing, and then wiped his eyes. Kit asked whether the discs were safe, and Brandt said that they had never been safer than in the cold of the hut. Nika took the case in both arms and carried it back to the station herself.
B1.proof: I couldn't. I'm a scientist.
B1.q: What does Brandt's explanation reveal about his character?
o: That he hates science.
That he is a thief.
That he forgot the discs.
That despite his actions, he could not bring himself to destroy scientific data.
B1.hint: Brandt'ın 'ben bir bilim insanıyım' demesi onun hakkında ne gösteriyor?
B1.why: Yaptıklarına rağmen bilimsel veriyi yok etmeye gönlünün el vermediğini gösteriyor.

text: When the generator was running again the team was tired but happy. Tomas wanted to sleep, but Brandt said, "Wait. I want to show you something."
He led them to the back of the hut. Behind some old barrels stood a grey metal case, the one Kit had seen him carrying every night. He opened it with a small key.
Inside lay three black discs wrapped in soft cloth, each labelled: 'Core. Radar. Temperature.'

"These are the original data," he said. "I didn't destroy them. I couldn't. I'm a scientist. I only moved them here so that nobody would find them. Every night I came to check that they were still safe, like a man visiting a sick friend."

Tomas lifted one disc in both hands like a baby. "So it was never lost," he said, laughing, and then wiped his eyes. Kit asked whether the discs were safe, and Brandt said that they had never been safer than in the cold of the hut. Nika took the case in both arms and carried it back to the station herself, walking slowly through the snow as if it contained something alive.
B2.proof: like a man visiting a sick friend
B2.q: What does the comparison show about Brandt's attitude to the data?
o: That he cared for the data deeply even while hiding it.
That he disliked the data.
That he was ill.
That he sold the data.
B2.hint: Brandt'ın her gece kutuyu kontrol etmesi neyi gösteriyor?
B2.why: Veriyi saklarken bile ona derin bir özen gösterdiğini gösteriyor.

text: When the generator was running again the team was tired but happy. Tomas wanted to sleep, but Brandt said, "Wait. I want to show you something."
He led them to the back of the hut. Behind some old barrels stood a grey metal case, the one Kit had seen him carrying every night. He opened it with a small key.
Inside lay three black discs wrapped in soft cloth, each labelled: 'Core. Radar. Temperature.'

"These are the original data," he said. "I didn't destroy them. I couldn't. I'm a scientist. I only moved them here so that nobody would find them. Every night I came to check that they were still safe, like a man visiting a sick friend."

Tomas lifted one disc in both hands like a baby. "So it was never lost," he said, laughing, and then wiped his eyes. It was a strange moral landscape, Nika reflected: a man who had concealed the truth for months had also, with equal diligence, protected it from destruction. He had been a thief of attention but never of substance, and she suspected that this was the only reason the story could still end well. Nika carried the case back to the station herself, walking slowly through the snow.
C1.proof: a thief of attention but never of substance
C1.q: What distinction does Nika make about Brandt?
o: That he stole money.
That he hid the discovery from people but did not destroy the actual data.
That he was a champion.
That he was a judge.
C1.hint: Nika, Brandt'ın davranışında hangi ayrımı yapıyor?
C1.why: Keşfi insanlardan gizlemiş ama verinin kendisini yok etmemiş.

eps.title: Independent Eyes
eps.recap: Merkez, Nika'nın gönderdiği verileri, kendilerinden bağımsız üç bilim insanına doğrulattı. Üçü de aynı sonuca vardı: Buzun altında gerçekten büyük bir göl vardı ve su örneğindeki canlı izleri sahteydi diyecek hiçbir nedenleri yoktu.

text: After the storm, the radio worked again. Nika sent all the data to headquarters: the radar images, the temperature tables, the photographs under the microscope. She wrote one long email. Brandt read it before she sent it. He nodded. He did not change a word.
Two weeks passed. Every day, the team waited for an answer. Kit made soup. Tomas drew pictures. Nobody could sleep well.
Then, on a Tuesday, a message came. It was from the director of the polar research institute. It was short.
'We sent your data to three independent scientists in three different countries. They did not know each other. They all say the same: the lake is real. The signs of life are real. Congratulations.'
Nika read the message aloud. Tomas jumped. Kit screamed. Brandt sat down on the floor and put his face in his hands.
A2.proof: They all say the same: the lake is real.
A2.q: Why is it important that three independent scientists agree?
o: It shows that they are friends.
It shows that the data is long.
It shows that they are tired.
It shows that the discovery is reliable, not just the opinion of one team.
A2.hint: Üç bağımsız bilim insanının aynı sonuca varması neden önemli?
A2.why: Keşfin tek bir ekibin görüşü değil, güvenilir ve doğrulanmış olduğunu gösterir.

text: After the storm the radio worked again. Nika sent all the data to headquarters: the radar images, the temperature tables, the microscope photographs, together with a long email. Brandt read it before she sent it. He nodded and did not change a word.
Two weeks passed, and every day the team waited for an answer. Kit made soup, Tomas drew sketches, and nobody slept well.
Then, one Tuesday, a message came from the director of the polar research institute. It was short.

'We sent your data to three independent scientists in three different countries. They did not know each other. They all say the same: the lake is real, and the signs of life are real. Congratulations.'
Nika read the message aloud. Tomas jumped, Kit screamed, and Brandt sat down on the floor and put his face in his hands.
B1.proof: He nodded and did not change a word.
B1.q: What does Brandt's reaction to the email show?
o: That he now supports honest reporting of the results.
That he did not read it.
That he wants to rewrite it.
That he is angry.
B1.hint: Brandt'ın e-postayı değiştirmemesi ne anlama geliyor?
B1.why: Sonuçların dürüstçe raporlanmasını artık desteklediğini gösteriyor.

Independent confirmation is the cold bath of science: it either destroys a discovery or turns it into knowledge. This one had survived, and so, in a way, had the people who made it.
B2.proof: Independent confirmation is the cold bath of science
B2.q: What role does independent confirmation play, according to the passage?
o: It makes discoveries warm.
It tests a discovery and either rejects it or establishes it as knowledge.
It is unnecessary.
It is a kind of soup.
B2.hint: Bağımsız doğrulama bilimde nasıl bir işlev görüyor?
B2.why: Bir keşfi sınar ve ya çürütür ya da bilgi haline getirir.

Nika thought of the fifty-three hidden messages and realised that the best answer to concealment is not accusation but verification, since a truth that three strangers can confirm needs no defender.
C1.proof: a truth that three strangers can confirm needs no defender
C1.q: What lesson does Nika draw?

That accusations are better.
That verifiable evidence is the best response to secrecy.
That messages should be hidden.

C1.why: Suçlamak değil, doğrulanabilir kanıt; üç yabancının doğrulayabildiği gerçek savunucuya ihtiyaç duymaz.

eps.title: The Announcement
eps.recap: Bir ay sonra enstitü, buzun altındaki gölün keşfini basına duyurdu. Haber bütün dünyada yayıldı. Fon artırıldı, istasyonu kapatma planı geri çekildi ve yeni bir bilim ekibi atandı.

text: One month later, on a cold bright morning, the Polar Research Institute held a press conference. A big hall in the capital city was full of journalists and cameras.
The director stood on the stage. Behind her, there was a giant picture of Antarctica. In the middle of the ice, she had put a blue circle.

"Ladies and gentlemen," she said. "Today I am proud to announce the discovery of a new lake under four hundred and fifty metres of ice. It is kept warm by the heat of the Earth. It may contain life that has been hidden for thousands of years."
In the polar station, Nika, Tomas, Kit and Brandt watched the broadcast on one small screen. Kit held the wooden spoon like a microphone.
That evening, a second message arrived: the money for the station would triple. No station would close. Fourteen new scientists would come in the summer.
A2.q: What was the result of the announcement?
o: The project received more money and the station stayed open.
The station was closed.
The lake disappeared.
Brandt won a prize.
A2.hint: Basın duyurusunun sonucu ne oldu sonunda?
A2.why: Proje daha fazla fon aldı ve istasyon açık kaldı.

text: One month later, on a cold bright morning, the Polar Research Institute held a press conference. A large hall in the capital was crowded with journalists and cameras.
The director stood on the stage with a giant picture of Antarctica behind her, and in the middle of the ice a blue circle.

"Ladies and gentlemen," she said. "Today I am proud to announce the discovery of a new lake beneath four hundred and fifty metres of ice, kept warm by the heat of the Earth. It may contain life that has been hidden for thousands of years."

At the polar station, Nika, Tomas, Kit and Brandt watched the broadcast on one small screen. Kit held her wooden spoon like a microphone. When the director thanked 'the team at Station Polaris', Brandt's lips moved silently, and Nika realised he was counting the people she had named, to see whether he was among them.

That evening a second message arrived: funding for the station would triple. Nothing would close, and fourteen new scientists would arrive in the summer. The thing that Brandt had feared for twenty years had turned out to be the very thing that saved him, and Nika could not decide whether this was an irony or a lesson. Perhaps, she thought, it was both, and the only person who could tell the difference was the one who had paid for it.
C1.proof: the only person who could tell the difference was the one who had paid for it
C1.q: What does Nika conclude about the meaning of events?
o: That the outcome was a coincidence.
That nobody paid anything.
That it is a joke.
That the outcome is both ironic and instructive, and only Brandt knows its cost.
C1.hint: Nika olayların anlamı hakkında nasıl bir sonuca varıyor?
C1.why: Sonuç hem ironik hem öğretici; bedelini yalnızca Brandt tam olarak biliyor.

eps.title: The Director Steps Down
eps.recap: Brandt, istasyon müdürlüğünden kendi isteğiyle ayrıldı ama bilim ekibinde kalmayı kabul etti. Yeni müdür olarak Nika önerildi. Kit, veda yemeğinde 'Bu masada yalan yok' diye bir kural koydu.

text: On Sunday, Dr. Brandt called a meeting in the kitchen. All four of them sat around the big table. Kit had cooked a lot of food, but nobody was eating.

"I have written a letter to headquarters," he said. "I have resigned as director of the station. I did something wrong, and I cannot lead you. But I would like to stay, if you agree, as a member of the science team. I want to work on the lake. I want to learn."
The room was silent. Nika looked at Tomas. Tomas looked at Kit. Kit put down her spoon.
"I vote yes," she said. "But I have a new rule for this kitchen. No lies at this table. Not even small ones."
"Agreed," said Brandt. And for the first time in months, he laughed.
A2.q: What decision does Brandt make?
o: He leaves the station forever.
He resigns as director but stays as a member of the science team.
He becomes the cook.
He refuses to say anything.
A2.hint: Brandt nasıl bir karar alıyor?
A2.why: Müdürlükten istifa ediyor ama bilim ekibinde kalıyor.

text: On Sunday Dr. Brandt called a meeting in the kitchen. All four of them sat around the big table. Kit had cooked a great deal of food, but nobody was eating.

"I've written to headquarters," he said. "I've resigned as director of the station. I did something wrong, and I can't lead you. But if you agree, I'd like to stay as a member of the science team. I want to work on the lake. I want to learn."
The room was silent. Nika looked at Tomas, Tomas looked at Kit, and Kit put down her spoon.
"I vote yes," she said. "But I have a new rule for this kitchen. No lies at this table. Not even small ones."
"Agreed," said Brandt. And for the first time in months, he laughed. Tomas poured everybody a cup of tea, and nobody left the table for a long time.
B1.proof: I did something wrong, and I can't lead you.
B1.q: Why does Brandt resign?
o: He is tired of the cold.
He is offered a better job.
He accepts responsibility for his wrongdoing and believes he should not lead.
He wants to become a cook.
B1.hint: Brandt müdürlükten neden istifa ediyor burada?
B1.why: Yaptığı yanlışın sorumluluğunu kabul ediyor ve liderlik etmemesi gerektiğini düşünüyor.

text: On Sunday Dr. Brandt called a meeting in the kitchen. All four of them sat around the big table. Kit had cooked a great deal of food, but nobody was eating.

"I've written to headquarters," he said. "I've resigned as director of the station. I did something wrong, and I can't lead you. But if you agree, I'd like to stay as a member of the science team. I want to work on the lake. I want to learn. I have spent twenty years managing science, and I have almost forgotten what it is to do it."
The room was silent. Nika looked at Tomas, Tomas looked at Kit, and Kit put down her spoon.
"I vote yes," she said. "But I have a new rule for this kitchen. No lies at this table. Not even small ones."

"Agreed," said Brandt. And for the first time in months, he laughed. Tomas poured everybody a cup of tea, and nobody left the table for a long time. Outside, the wind had finally dropped, and for the first time in weeks the station was completely quiet.
B2.proof: I have almost forgotten what it is to do it.
B2.q: What does Brandt's remark show about his reasons for staying?
o: That he wants more money.
That he dislikes science.
That he wants to boss people.
That he wants to return to real scientific work after years of administration.
B2.hint: Brandt neden ekipte kalmak istiyor?
B2.why: Yıllarca yöneticilik yaptıktan sonra yeniden gerçek bilimsel çalışmaya dönmek istiyor.

text: On Sunday Dr. Brandt called a meeting in the kitchen. All four of them sat around the big table. Kit had cooked a great deal of food, but nobody was eating.

"I've written to headquarters," he said. "I've resigned as director of the station. I did something wrong, and I can't lead you. But if you agree, I'd like to stay as a member of the science team. I want to work on the lake. I want to learn. I have spent twenty years managing science, and I have almost forgotten what it is to do it."
The room was silent. Nika looked at Tomas, Tomas looked at Kit, and Kit put down her spoon.
"I vote yes," she said. "But I have a new rule for this kitchen. No lies at this table. Not even small ones."

"Agreed," said Brandt. And for the first time in months, he laughed. Nika, who had been proposed as the new director, watched him with a feeling she could not quite name. It was not forgiveness, exactly, because forgiveness implies that the matter is closed. It was closer to an understanding: that a person is larger than the worst thing he has done, and that the best way to honour a discovery is to build, around it, a team in which nobody needs to hide.
C1.proof: a person is larger than the worst thing he has done
C1.q: What kind of feeling does Nika have towards Brandt?
o: A mature understanding rather than complete forgiveness.
Pure hatred.
Perfect trust.
Indifference.
C1.hint: Nika, Brandt'a karşı nasıl bir duygu hissediyor?
C1.why: Tam bir af değil, bir insanın yaptığı en kötü şeyden büyük olduğunu kabul eden olgun bir anlayış.

eps.title: Daylight
eps.recap: Aylar sonra kutup gündüzü doğdu. Nika, istasyonun penceresinden ilk güneşi izledi ve defterine yeni bir soru yazdı: 'Gölde yaşayanlar bizden önce ne biliyordu?' Ardından yeni sondajın planını yapmaya başladı.

text: After four long months of darkness, the sun came back. Nika stood at the window of the station in her warm sweater. The sky was pink and gold. A thin line of light moved slowly over the white ice. It was the first sunrise of the year.
Behind her, the station was waking up. She could hear Kit singing in the kitchen. She could hear Tomas laughing at something. She could hear Brandt's slow steps in the corridor.
Nika sat at her desk. She opened a new notebook. She wrote the date. Then she wrote one big question on the first page:
'What did the life in the lake know before we came?'
She looked at the sentence for a long time and smiled. Outside, the light was getting stronger. A new year of work was beginning.
A2.proof: What did the life in the lake know before we came?
A2.q: What does Nika's new question show?
o: That she wants to leave science.
That she is sad.
That the discovery has opened new curiosity and further research.
That she forgot the lake.
A2.hint: Nika'nın yeni sorusu neyi gösteriyor?
A2.why: Keşfin yeni bir merak ve yeni araştırmalar doğurduğunu gösteriyor.

text: After four long months of darkness the sun came back. Nika stood at the station window in her warm sweater. The sky was pink and gold, and a thin line of light moved slowly across the white ice. It was the first sunrise of the year.
Behind her the station was waking up. She could hear Kit singing in the kitchen, Tomas laughing at something, and Brandt's slow footsteps in the corridor.
