eps.title: The Black Notebook
eps.recap: Noah, laboratuvarın en eski dolabında kendi ham veri defterini buldu. Defterin her sayfası tarihli ve imzalıydı ve analizin adım adım nasıl yapıldığını gösteriyordu.

text: On Wednesday night, the laboratory was empty. Noah and Mei opened an old grey cupboard in the corner. Inside there were many old notebooks. On the third shelf, Noah saw a black one with his initials: N.K.
"This is my raw data notebook," he said. "In the lab, we write everything by hand. Every day. Every number. And we sign every page."
He opened it. The pages were full of small numbers and drawings. At the top of each page, there was a date. At the bottom, there was his signature.
Mei turned the pages. "Look," she said. "Here is the day you found tau-star. March the ninth. And here is a note from Professor Alder: 'Well done, Noah. Check again.' She signed it too."
Noah felt tears in his eyes. "Nobody can erase this," he said. "It is paper."
A2.q: Why is the notebook important?
o: It is a book of poems.
It is Mei's homework.
It is empty.
It is dated and signed evidence that Noah found the result.
A2.hint: Siyah defter neden önemli bir kanıt?
A2.why: Tarihli ve imzalı sayfalar sonucu Noah'ın bulduğunu gösteriyor ve silinemiyor.

text: On Wednesday night the laboratory was empty. Noah and Mei opened an old grey cupboard in the corner, full of old notebooks. On the third shelf Noah found a black one with his initials on the cover: N.K.
"This is my raw data notebook," he said. "In this lab we write everything by hand, every day, every number. And we sign every page."
He opened it. The pages were crowded with small numbers and sketches, each dated at the top and signed at the bottom.
Mei turned the pages. "Look," she said. "Here's the day you found tau-star. The ninth of March. And here's a note from Professor Alder: 'Well done, Noah. Check again.' She signed that, too."
Noah felt tears in his eyes. "Nobody can delete this," he said. "It's paper." Mei took a photograph of every page with her phone, one after another, and Noah held the notebook flat under the lamp.
B1.proof: Nobody can delete this
B1.q: Why does Noah say it cannot be deleted?
o: Because it is a physical paper record, not a digital file.
Because it is locked in a safe.
Because it is too heavy.
Because it is a secret.
B1.hint: Noah neden 'bunu kimse silemez' diyor?
B1.why: Çünkü defter fiziksel bir kâğıt kayıt; dijital dosyalar gibi silinemez.

text: On Wednesday night the laboratory was empty. Noah and Mei opened an old grey cupboard in the corner, full of old notebooks that smelled of dust and coffee. On the third shelf Noah found a black one with his initials on the cover: N.K.

"This is my raw data notebook," he said. "In this lab we write everything by hand, every day, every number. And we sign every page. Professor Alder insists on it. I used to complain about the rule. I won't any more."
He opened it. The pages were crowded with small numbers and sketches, each dated at the top and signed at the bottom.
Mei turned the pages. "Look," she said. "Here's the day you found tau-star. The ninth of March. And here's a note from Professor Alder: 'Well done, Noah. Check again.' She signed that, too."

Noah felt tears in his eyes. "Nobody can delete this," he said. "It's paper. Whoever erased the servers forgot that science was done on paper for three hundred years before it was ever done on a disk."
B2.proof: science was done on paper for three hundred years
B2.q: What irony does Noah point out?
o: That paper is more expensive than servers.
That the thief deleted the digital files but ignored the paper records.
That scientists dislike notebooks.
That servers are older than paper.
B2.hint: Noah hangi ironiyi dile getiriyor?
B2.why: Hırsız dijital kayıtları silmiş ama kâğıt defterleri unutmuş.

text: On Wednesday night the laboratory was empty. Noah and Mei opened an old grey cupboard in the corner, full of old notebooks that smelled of dust and coffee. On the third shelf Noah found a black one with his initials on the cover: N.K.

"This is my raw data notebook," he said. "In this lab we write everything by hand, every day, every number. And we sign every page. Professor Alder insists on it. I used to complain about the rule. I won't any more."

He opened it. The pages were crowded with small numbers and sketches, each dated at the top and signed at the bottom, in the neat, slightly nervous handwriting of a young man who did not yet know that he was making history.
Mei turned the pages. "Look," she said. "Here's the day you found tau-star. The ninth of March. And here's a note from Professor Alder: 'Well done, Noah. Check again.' She signed that, too."

Noah felt tears in his eyes. "Nobody can delete this," he said. "It's paper. Whoever erased the servers forgot that science was done on paper for three hundred years before it was ever done on a disk. And the one thing a clever thief cannot do is travel back to March and sign a page."
C1.proof: the one thing a clever thief cannot do is travel back to March and sign a page
C1.q: What is Noah's point about the dated pages?
o: That Noah can travel in time.
That March is a lucky month.
That the dates and signatures cannot be forged afterwards.
That signatures are unimportant.
C1.hint: Tarihli ve imzalı sayfalar geriye dönük olarak neden taklit edilemez?
C1.why: Mart ayında atılmış tarih ve imza sonradan sahte olarak eklenemez; defter bu yüzden güçlü bir kanıt.

eps.title: Who Did the Analysis
eps.recap: Noah ve Mei defteri sayfa sayfa incelediler. Analizi baştan sona Noah'ın yaptığı, Voss'un ise yalnızca iki kez laboratuvara geldiği ve yöntemi sorduğu ortaya çıktı.

text: On Thursday, Noah and Mei sat at the long table. They put the black notebook in the middle. Mei took a yellow pen. She began to mark every page.
"Who made the table of results?" she asked. "You," said Noah. "Who ran the new method?" "You." "Who made the graph on page forty?" "Me."

Mei turned to the last pages. She read the visitors' notes. Dr. Voss came to the laboratory only two times. On the first day, he wrote: 'Visited. Interesting. Asked about the method.' On the second day, he wrote: 'Visited. Asked for final tables.'
"That is all," said Mei. "Two visits. Two questions. He did not make a single number."
Noah looked at the notebook. For the first time in a week, he felt strong.
A2.q: What does the notebook show about Dr. Voss?
o: He only visited twice and asked questions; he did not do any analysis.
He did most of the work.
He wrote the whole paper.
He never came to the laboratory.
A2.hint: Defter Voss'un katkısı hakkında ne söylüyor?
A2.why: Voss yalnızca iki kez gelmiş ve soru sormuş; hiçbir analiz yapmamış.

text: On Thursday Noah and Mei sat at the long table with the black notebook between them. Mei took a yellow highlighter and began to mark every page.
"Who produced the results table?" she asked. "I did," said Noah. "Who ran the new method?" "I did." "Who drew the graph on page forty?" "Me."

Mei turned to the last pages, where the visitors' notes were kept. Dr. Voss had come to the laboratory only twice. The first time he had written: 'Visited. Interesting. Asked about the method.' The second time: 'Visited. Asked for final tables.'
"That's all," said Mei. "Two visits, two questions. He never produced a single number."

Noah looked at the notebook, and for the first time in a week he felt strong. He closed the notebook gently and put it back into his bag, and Mei promised that she would not let it out of her sight until the end of the conference.
B1.proof: He never produced a single number.
B1.q: What does Mei conclude?
o: That Voss is the real author.
That Voss made no scientific contribution to the analysis.
That Noah did not work.
That Mei wrote the paper.
B1.hint: Mei defteri inceledikten sonra hangi sonuca varıyor?
B1.why: Voss'un analize bilimsel bir katkısı yok; yalnızca soru sormuş.

text: On Thursday Noah and Mei sat at the long table with the black notebook between them. Mei took a yellow highlighter and began to mark every page, methodically, as an auditor goes through a set of accounts.
"Who produced the results table?" she asked. "I did," said Noah. "Who ran the new method?" "I did." "Who drew the graph on page forty?" "Me."

Mei turned to the last pages, where the visitors' notes were kept. Dr. Voss had come to the laboratory only twice. The first time he had written: 'Visited. Interesting. Asked about the method.' The second time: 'Visited. Asked for final tables.'
"That's all," said Mei. "Two visits, two questions. He never produced a single number, and he never corrected one."

Noah looked at the notebook, and for the first time in a week he felt strong. The claim that Voss could make, if he ever dared to make it, was that he had contributed ideas. But the notebook showed that his only idea had been to ask for the results when they were finished.
B2.proof: his only idea had been to ask for the results when they were finished
B2.q: What is the point of the final sentence?
o: That Voss had many ideas.
That the results were not finished.
That Voss's only 'contribution' was to request the finished results.
That Noah had no ideas.
B2.hint: Voss'un tek 'fikri' ne olmuş?
B2.why: Voss'un tek katkısı, sonuçlar bittiğinde onları istemek olmuş.

text: On Thursday Noah and Mei sat at the long table with the black notebook between them. Mei took a yellow highlighter and began to mark every page, methodically, as an auditor goes through a set of accounts.
"Who produced the results table?" she asked. "I did," said Noah. "Who ran the new method?" "I did." "Who drew the graph on page forty?" "Me."

Mei turned to the last pages, where the visitors' notes were kept. Dr. Voss had come to the laboratory only twice. The first time he had written: 'Visited. Interesting. Asked about the method.' The second time: 'Visited. Asked for final tables.'
"That's all," said Mei. "Two visits, two questions. He never produced a single number, and he never corrected one."

Noah looked at the notebook, and for the first time in a week he felt strong. The claim that Voss could make, if he ever dared to make it, was that he had contributed ideas. But the notebook showed that his only idea had been to ask for the results when they were finished. Authorship, Noah reflected, is not a matter of who sits in the largest office. It is a matter of who was in the room when the number first appeared on the page, and the page had his handwriting on it, and nobody else's.
C1.proof: Authorship, Noah reflected, is not a matter of who sits in the largest office.
C1.q: What principle does Noah express?
o: That the largest office belongs to the author.
That authorship should be decided by vote.
That the page was written by the director.
That authorship depends on who actually did the work, not on rank.
C1.hint: Noah yazarlık hakkında hangi ilkeyi dile getiriyor?
C1.why: Yazarlık makamla değil, işi gerçekten kimin yaptığıyla belirlenir.

eps.title: A Careless Cleaner
eps.recap: Noah ve Mei gece geç saatte Voss'un odasının yanından geçerken kapının aralık olduğunu gördüler. İçeride, masanın üzerinde laboratuvarın kendi disklerinin kopyalarına benzeyen üç USB bellek vardı.

text: It was nearly ten o'clock at night. Noah and Mei were going home. They walked along the long corridor of the administration building. It was empty. Only one light was on.
Mei stopped. "Noah," she whispered. "Look." At the end of the corridor, the door of Dr. Voss's office was open. Only a few centimetres. A thin line of light came out.
They went closer. Nobody was inside. On the desk, in the light of the lamp, there were three small black USB sticks. Each one had a white label.
Mei read the labels. 'Polymer, Raw.' 'Polymer, Tables.' 'Polymer, Figures.' Noah put his hand over his mouth.
A cleaning lady came from the other side of the corridor, pushing a cart. "Oh, he forgot to lock again," she said and smiled. "He always does when he is in a hurry."
A2.q: What do the USB sticks probably contain?
o: Music for the party.
Copies of Noah's polymer data, so Voss kept the data.
Photographs of the university.
Blank storage.
A2.hint: USB belleklerin etiketleri neyi düşündürüyor?
A2.why: Etiketlerde 'Polymer' yazıyor; Noah'ın verilerinin kopyalarını Voss'un sakladığını düşündürüyor.

text: It was nearly ten o'clock at night, and Noah and Mei were going home. They walked down the long corridor of the administration building. It was empty, and only one light was on.
Mei stopped. "Noah," she whispered. "Look." At the end of the corridor the door of Dr. Voss's office stood open by a few centimetres, and a thin line of light spilled out.
They moved closer. Nobody was inside. On the desk, in the circle of lamplight, lay three small black USB sticks, each with a white label.
Mei read them. 'Polymer, Raw.' 'Polymer, Tables.' 'Polymer, Figures.' Noah put his hand over his mouth.

A cleaning lady came pushing her cart from the other end of the corridor. "Oh, he's forgotten to lock up again," she said, smiling. "He always does when he's in a hurry." They walked out into the cold night air in silence.
B1.proof: Polymer, Raw.
B1.q: Why do the labels matter?
o: They are the names of music albums.
They show that Voss studies chemistry.
They match the data that was deleted from the laboratory.
They are just decorations.
B1.hint: Bu etiketler neden bu kadar önemli sayılıyor?
B1.why: Etiketler laboratuvardan silinen verilerle eşleşiyor; kopyalar Voss'un elinde olabilir.

text: It was nearly ten o'clock at night, and Noah and Mei were going home. They walked down the long corridor of the administration building. It was empty, and only one light was on, as though the building itself had decided to let them see.
Mei stopped. "Noah," she whispered. "Look." At the end of the corridor the door of Dr. Voss's office stood open by a few centimetres, and a thin line of light spilled out.
They moved closer. Nobody was inside. On the desk, in the circle of lamplight, lay three small black USB sticks, each with a white label.

Mei read them. 'Polymer, Raw.' 'Polymer, Tables.' 'Polymer, Figures.' Noah put his hand over his mouth. Those were not the names of his folders on the laboratory server, but the names of the three layers that had disappeared from it.

A cleaning lady came pushing her cart from the other end of the corridor. "Oh, he's forgotten to lock up again," she said, smiling. "He always does when he's in a hurry." They walked out into the cold night air in silence, both of them thinking the same thing.
B2.proof: the names of the three layers that had disappeared from it
B2.q: What do the three labels correspond to?
o: The three floors of the building.
The three days of the week.
The three students in the lab.
The three kinds of data that were deleted from the server.
B2.hint: Üç etiket neyin üç katmanına karşılık geliyor?
B2.why: Laboratuvar sunucusundan kaybolan üç tür veriye: ham veri, tablolar ve şekiller.

text: It was nearly ten o'clock at night, and Noah and Mei were going home. They walked down the long corridor of the administration building. It was empty, and only one light was on, as though the building itself had decided to let them see.
Mei stopped. "Noah," she whispered. "Look." At the end of the corridor the door of Dr. Voss's office stood open by a few centimetres, and a thin line of light spilled out.
They moved closer. Nobody was inside. On the desk, in the circle of lamplight, lay three small black USB sticks, each with a white label.

Mei read them. 'Polymer, Raw.' 'Polymer, Tables.' 'Polymer, Figures.' Noah put his hand over his mouth. Those were not the names of his folders on the laboratory server, but the names of the three layers that had disappeared from it, in the same order, written by someone who had been accustomed to thinking of the work as his own.

A cleaning lady came pushing her cart from the other end of the corridor. "Oh, he's forgotten to lock up again," she said, smiling. "He always does when he's in a hurry." Noah looked at Mei. They both knew that they could not take the sticks, because stolen evidence would be useless in any hearing. But they could, and did, photograph every label.
C1.proof: stolen evidence would be useless in any hearing
C1.q: Why do they photograph the labels instead of taking the sticks?
o: Because evidence taken illegally could not be used and could harm them.
Because the sticks were too heavy.
Because the cleaning lady asked them to.
Because the sticks were empty.
C1.hint: Neden USB'leri almayıp yalnızca etiketleri fotoğraflıyorlar?
C1.why: Yasa dışı yoldan alınan delil geçersiz olur ve onlara zarar verebilir; bu yüzden yalnızca fotoğraflıyorlar.

eps.title: The Programme Has Changed
eps.recap: Noah, konferansın yeni programını gördü: açılış konuşmasını Prof. Alder yerine Dr. Voss yapacaktı ve konu başlığı 'Polimer Filmlerde Hafıza Etkileri' idi. Konferansa yalnızca bir gün vardı.

text: On Friday, the email with the new conference programme arrived. Noah opened it in the library. He read the first page quickly. Then he stopped.
The Opening Lecture was on Saturday at nine in the morning. It was the most important talk of the conference. For many years, Professor Alder gave it. But this year, the name was different.
'Opening Lecture: Memory Effects in Polymer Films. Speaker: Dr. Henrik Voss.'
Noah read the line three times. He could not believe his eyes. It was the title of the stolen paper. It was the title of his work.
He called Mei. "The conference is tomorrow," he said. His voice was thin. "And Dr. Voss will give my paper to the whole world."
A2.q: What is the new problem?
o: The conference was cancelled.
Professor Alder won a prize.
Voss will present Noah's stolen work at the most important talk tomorrow.
Noah forgot to attend.
A2.hint: Yeni programda hangi sorun ortaya çıkıyor?
A2.why: Voss, Noah'ın çalışmasını ertesi gün açılış konuşmasında kendi adına sunacak.

text: On Friday the email with the new conference programme arrived. Noah opened it in the library and skimmed the first page. Then he stopped.
The Opening Lecture was scheduled for Saturday at nine in the morning, the most important talk of the whole conference. For years Professor Alder had given it. This year the name was different.
'Opening Lecture: Memory Effects in Polymer Films. Speaker: Dr. Henrik Voss.'
Noah read the line three times, hardly believing his eyes. It was the title of the stolen paper. It was the title of his work.

He called Mei. "The conference is tomorrow," he said, his voice thin. "And Dr. Voss is about to present my paper to the entire world." Mei said she would be at the library in ten minutes, and that Noah should not tell anyone else yet, not even the professor, until they had a plan.
B1.proof: It was the title of his work.
B1.q: Why is the change in the programme alarming?
o: Because the programme is late.
Because Saturday is a holiday.
Because Mei is sick.
Because the title belongs to Noah's research, and Voss will present it as his own.
B1.hint: Programdaki değişiklik neden alarm verici?
B1.why: Başlık Noah'ın araştırmasına ait ve Voss onu kendi çalışmasıymış gibi sunacak.

text: On Friday the email with the new conference programme arrived. Noah opened it in the library and skimmed the first page. Then he stopped, as if somebody had called his name from behind.
The Opening Lecture was scheduled for Saturday at nine in the morning, the most important talk of the whole conference. For years Professor Alder had given it. This year the name was different.
'Opening Lecture: Memory Effects in Polymer Films. Speaker: Dr. Henrik Voss.'
Noah read the line three times, hardly believing his eyes. It was the title of the stolen paper. It was the title of his work, announced to a thousand scientists under another man's name.

He called Mei. "The conference is tomorrow," he said, his voice thin. "And Dr. Voss is about to present my paper to the entire world. We have less than twenty-four hours." Mei said she would be at the library in ten minutes, and that Noah should not tell anyone else yet, not even the professor, until they had a plan, because a leaked plan is only a warning.
B2.proof: less than twenty-four hours
B2.q: What does the last sentence emphasise?
o: That time is nearly gone and they must act immediately.
That the conference is boring.
That Mei is late.
That Noah has plenty of time.
B2.hint: Son cümle hangi aciliyeti vurguluyor?
B2.why: Zaman neredeyse kalmadı; Noah ve Mei bir günden kısa sürede harekete geçmek zorunda.

text: On Friday the email with the new conference programme arrived. Noah opened it in the library and skimmed the first page. Then he stopped, as if somebody had called his name from behind.
The Opening Lecture was scheduled for Saturday at nine in the morning, the most important talk of the whole conference. For years Professor Alder had given it. This year the name was different.
'Opening Lecture: Memory Effects in Polymer Films. Speaker: Dr. Henrik Voss.'

Noah read the line three times, hardly believing his eyes. It was the title of the stolen paper. It was the title of his work, announced to a thousand scientists under another man's name. The audacity of it was almost admirable: Voss was not hiding the theft, but celebrating it in public, on the one stage where nobody would dare to interrupt him.

He called Mei. "The conference is tomorrow," he said, his voice thin. "And Dr. Voss is about to present my paper to the entire world. We have less than twenty-four hours." Mei said she would be at the library within ten minutes, and that nobody else should be told until they had a plan, because a leaked plan is only a warning to the person it is aimed at.
C1.proof: on the one stage where nobody would dare to interrupt him
C1.q: What does the narrator suggest about Voss's strategy?
o: That he wants to be interrupted.
That he is acting boldly in public because a prestigious stage discourages challenge.
That he is afraid of the audience.
That he forgot his speech.
C1.hint: Voss neden hırsızlığı gizlemek yerine açıkça sahneye çıkarıyor?
C1.why: Prestijli bir sahnede kimsenin ona itiraz etmeye cesaret edemeyeceğini düşünüyor; cüretkâr bir strateji bu.

eps.title: Tell the Professor
eps.recap: Cuma gecesi Noah ve Mei, Prof. Alder'in evine gitti. Bütün kanıtları sırayla anlattılar: v3 dosyası, kurumsal hesap, takma ad, güvenlik kaydı, defter ve USB'ler. Alder uzun süre hiçbir şey söylemedi.

text: On Friday night, at nine o'clock, Noah and Mei knocked on Professor Alder's door. She opened it in her blue dressing gown. She looked tired. "Is something wrong?" she asked.
"Yes, Professor," said Noah. "We need to tell you something. It will take an hour."

They sat in her small living room. Noah put the black notebook on the table. Mei opened her laptop. One by one, they told her everything. The deleted file. The journal. The code FAC-ADM-02. The word 'tau-star'. The guard and the chocolates. The USB sticks with white labels.
Professor Alder listened with her hands in her lap. She did not interrupt. When they finished, the room was very quiet. The clock on the wall made a small sound: tick, tick, tick.
"I need to think," she said at last. "Please, wait outside. Just for a few minutes."
A2.q: How does Professor Alder react to the story?
o: She laughs at them.
She calls the police at once.
She falls asleep.
She listens carefully and needs time to think.
A2.hint: Prof. Alder öğrencilerin anlattıklarına nasıl tepki veriyor?
A2.why: Dikkatle dinliyor ve düşünmek için zamana ihtiyaç duyuyor.

o: That she is a very calm person with nothing to say.

That she is planning a party.

B2.why: Sessiz kalmak ya çok sakin olmak ya da çok incinmiş olmak demektir; Noah hocasının derinden yaralanmış olabileceğinden korkuyor.

eps.title: My Own Student
eps.recap: Prof. Alder geri çağırdığında yüzü solgundu. Voss'un yıllar önce kendi öğrencisi olduğunu, ona hep güvendiğini ve bunun doğru olabileceğine inanmak istemediğini söyledi. Noah'tan kesin bir kanıt istedi.

text: After ten minutes, Professor Alder opened the door again. Her face was white. She asked them to come in and sit. She did not offer tea, which she always did.

"I must tell you something about Henrik Voss," she said. "Twenty-five years ago, he was my student. A bright young man. Very polite. Very eager. I helped him with his first paper. I wrote him many letters. I thought of him almost as a son."
She stopped. Her voice was thin. "I find it very hard to believe this. I know you are honest, Noah. I know you did the work. But Henrik... I cannot imagine it."
Noah felt sad for her. "Professor, we have only told you what we found."
"I know," she said. "But in science, we need more than a feeling. I need one piece of proof that no one can argue with. Show me, and I will believe it."
A2.q: Why is it hard for Professor Alder to believe the story?
o: Voss was her student and she trusted him like a son.
Voss is her enemy.
She does not know Voss.
She thinks Noah is lying.
A2.hint: Prof. Alder'in inanması neden zor?
A2.why: Voss yıllar önce onun öğrencisiydi ve ona oğlu gibi güveniyordu.

text: After ten minutes Professor Alder opened the door again. Her face was white. She invited them to sit, and she did not offer tea, which she always did.

o: A photograph of Voss.
Solid, undeniable proof, not suspicion.
An apology.
A new experiment.
B1.hint: Prof. Alder nasıl bir kanıt istiyor?

text: After ten minutes Professor Alder opened the door again. Her face was white. She invited them to sit, and she did not offer tea, which she always did, even to the plumber.

"I know," she said. "But in science a feeling isn't enough. I need one piece of proof that nobody can argue with. Show me that, and I will believe it." Noah looked at her hands, which were trembling a little in her lap.
B2.proof: it's that I'm afraid you are right
B2.q: What is Professor Alder's real fear?
o: That Noah is wrong.
That the notebook is lost.
That the painful accusation against her former student may be true.
That she will miss the conference.
B2.hint: Prof. Alder asıl neden korkuyor?
B2.why: Eski öğrencisine yöneltilen acı suçlamanın doğru olmasından korkuyor.

As a sign she distrusts him.

C1.why: Bunu güvensizlik değil, bilimsel dürüstlük olarak görüyor.

eps.title: Logs at Midnight
eps.recap: Gece yarısı Mei, laboratuvar sunucusunun yönetici günlüklerini istedi. Üniversitenin BT sorumlusu Mr. Okoye, gizli kalmak şartıyla sunucuya bakmayı kabul etti; kayıtlar, silme komutunun Voss'un hesabıyla verildiğini gösterdi.

text: At midnight, Mei called a friend who worked in the university's computer office. His name was Mr. Okoye. He was a quiet man with big headphones. He came to the laboratory in his slippers.
"I will do this only because it is Professor Alder," he said. "And you must not tell anyone I helped."
He sat in front of the main server and typed for twenty minutes. Numbers and letters ran down the black screen. Noah, Mei and Professor Alder, who had come with them, watched without a sound.
Suddenly, Mr. Okoye stopped. "Here," he said. "The delete command. Third of December, 3:12 a.m."
He pointed at a line. It had a user name. The name was: 'hvoss'. "This command was typed by the account of Dr. Henrik Voss."
A2.q: What does the server log show?
o: Professor Alder deleted her own file.
Dr. Voss's account gave the command to delete the files.
The server broke by itself.
Noah deleted the file by mistake.
A2.hint: Sunucu kaydı silme komutu hakkında ne gösteriyor?
A2.why: Silme komutu Dr. Voss'un hesabıyla verilmiş.

text: At midnight Mei called a friend who worked in the university's computer office, a quiet man named Mr. Okoye who wore big headphones. He arrived at the laboratory in his slippers.
"I'm only doing this because it's Professor Alder," he said. "And you must never tell anyone I helped."
He sat at the main server and typed for twenty minutes while numbers and letters raced down the black screen. Noah, Mei and Professor Alder, who had come with them, watched in silence.
Suddenly Mr. Okoye stopped. "Here," he said. "The delete command. Third of December, 3:12 a.m."

He pointed at a line containing a user name: 'hvoss'. "This command was issued by the account of Dr. Henrik Voss." Professor Alder put her hand on Noah's shoulder, and nobody said a word for a while. Mr. Okoye saved a copy of the log on a small disk and gave it to Mei with a serious nod before he went home.
B1.proof: Third of December, 3:12 a.m.
B1.q: Why does the time of the command matter?
o: It is the time of the conference.
It is when Voss was born.
It matches the exact minute when the files were deleted.
It is lunchtime.
B1.hint: Komutun verildiği zaman neden bu kadar önemli?
B1.why: Dosyanın silindiği dakikayla birebir örtüşüyor.

text: At midnight Mei called a friend who worked in the university's computer office, a quiet man named Mr. Okoye who wore big headphones. He arrived at the laboratory in his slippers, as though he had been waiting for this call for years.

He pointed at a line containing a user name: 'hvoss'. "This command was issued by the account of Dr. Henrik Voss. And look at the origin: it came from ADMIN-07, the machine in the administration building." The two clues that had seemed to point in different directions, the shared account and the personal one, now joined into a single line. Mr. Okoye saved a copy of the log on a small disk and gave it to Mei with a serious nod.
B2.proof: joined into a single line
B2.q: What happens to the earlier clues?
o: They disappear.
They contradict each other.
They point to Mei.
They are connected into one clear chain leading to Voss.
B2.hint: Önceki ipuçları sonunda nasıl birleşiyor?
B2.why: ADMIN-07 ve Voss'un hesabı tek bir zincir oluşturup Voss'u gösteriyor.

The two clues that had seemed to point in different directions, the shared account and the personal one, now joined into a single line. "Thank you, Mr. Okoye," she said. "That is proof."

eps.title: The Ethics Chair
eps.recap: Prof. Alder, sabaha karşı Etik Kurul Başkanı Prof. Lindqvist'i telefonla uyandırdı. Lindqvist önce şaşırdı, sonra ciddi bir sesle toplantıyı konferanstan bir saat önce yapmayı kabul etti.

text: At four in the morning, Professor Alder picked up the telephone. Noah and Mei sat at the kitchen table and listened. She dialled a number she knew by heart.
After seven rings, a sleepy voice answered. "Lindqvist." He was the chairman of the university's Ethics Committee.
"Anders, it is Margaret Alder," she said. "I am sorry to wake you. I have a very serious matter. It concerns a case of stolen research. It concerns the university's deputy dean."
Nobody spoke on the other end for a long time. Then, in a different voice, clear and awake, the chairman said: "Tell me everything, Margaret. Slowly."
She talked for twenty minutes. At the end, Professor Lindqvist said: "I will call the committee. We meet at eight. One hour before the conference."
A2.q: What is the result of the phone call?
o: The conference will be cancelled.
Voss will be arrested at once.
The Ethics Committee will meet before the conference to hear the case.
Nothing will happen.
A2.hint: Telefon görüşmesinin sonucu ne oldu?
A2.why: Etik kurul, konferanstan bir saat önce toplanıp konuyu dinleyecek.

text: At four in the morning Professor Alder picked up the telephone while Noah and Mei sat at her kitchen table, listening. She dialled a number she knew by heart.

"Anders, it's Margaret Alder," she said. "I'm sorry to wake you. I have a very serious matter concerning stolen research. It involves the deputy dean of the university."
For a long time nobody spoke at the other end. Then, in a different voice, clear and fully awake, the chairman said: "Tell me everything, Margaret. Slowly."

She talked for twenty minutes. At the end Professor Lindqvist said: "I'll call the committee. We'll meet at eight, one hour before the conference." She put the phone down and looked at Noah and Mei. "Now we wait for the morning," she said. "And we pray that the roads are empty."
B1.proof: Tell me everything, Margaret. Slowly.
B1.q: How does the chairman's tone change during the call?
o: From angry to happy.
From formal to funny.
It does not change.
From sleepy to alert and serious as he realises the importance.
B1.hint: Başkanın tonu görüşme boyunca nasıl değişiyor?
B1.why: Uykulu sesten, konunun önemini anladıkça uyanık ve ciddi bir sese geçiyor.

text: At four in the morning Professor Alder picked up the telephone while Noah and Mei sat at her kitchen table, listening. She dialled a number she knew by heart, though she had called it only twice in twenty years.

o: Because Voss's subordinates might warn him or interfere.

B2.why: Voss'un astlarının ona haber verebileceğinden veya işe karışabileceğinden endişe ediyor.

text: At four in the morning Professor Alder picked up the telephone while Noah and Mei sat at her kitchen table, listening. She dialled a number she knew by heart, though she had called it only twice in twenty years.

eps.title: One Hour Before
eps.recap: Sabah sekizde Etik Kurul gizlice toplandı. Prof. Alder defteri, günlükleri ve fotoğrafları gösterdi. Kurul üyeleri soru sordu. Başkan karar için yirmi dakika istedi ve konferans salonuna girmeden önce kimsenin Voss'a haber vermemesini emretti.

text: At eight o'clock on Saturday, the Ethics Committee met in a small room on the third floor of the library. There were five members around a long table. Noah and Mei waited in the corridor. Professor Alder went in alone.
She put the black notebook on the table. Then she put down the printed server log and the photographs of the USB sticks. She spoke for fifteen minutes. Her voice was calm and clear.

The committee members asked questions. One was a woman with white hair. She asked about the dates. Another was a young man with glasses. He asked about the signatures. Professor Alder answered every question.
At eight forty, the chairman closed the file. "We need twenty minutes to decide," he said. "Until then, nobody may speak to Dr. Voss about this. Nobody."
In the corridor, Noah looked at his watch. It was eight forty-two. The conference started at nine.
A2.proof: nobody may speak to Dr. Voss about this
A2.q: Why must nobody speak to Dr. Voss?
o: Because Voss is on holiday.
Because Voss is deaf.
Because he is sleeping.
So that he cannot prepare, hide evidence or run away.
A2.hint: Kimse neden Voss ile bu konuda konuşmamalı?
A2.why: Hazırlık yapmasını, kanıtları gizlemesini veya kaçmasını önlemek için.

text: At eight o'clock on Saturday the Ethics Committee met in a small room on the third floor of the library. Five members sat around a long table. Noah and Mei waited in the corridor, and Professor Alder went in alone.
She laid the black notebook on the table, along with the printed server log and the photographs of the USB sticks. She spoke for fifteen minutes in a calm, clear voice.

eps.title: The Opening Lecture
eps.recap: Saat dokuzda büyük salon doldu. Dr. Voss sahneye çıktı, gülümsedi ve ilk slaytı gösterdi: 'Polimer Filmlerde Hafıza Etkileri — Dr. H. Voss'. Noah salonun arka sırasından, Etik Kurul kararı hâlâ gelmeden, bunu izledi.

text: At nine o'clock, the big hall was full. There were a thousand people in red seats. The air smelled of coffee and new paper. Noah and Mei stood at the back, next to the door.
The lights went down. A tall man in a dark suit walked onto the stage. He had a warm smile. He carried a small remote control in his hand. It was Dr. Voss.
"Good morning, colleagues," he said into the microphone. His voice was deep and friendly. "I am delighted to open this year's conference with new and exciting results."
He pressed the button. A giant picture appeared behind him. It showed a title in white letters: 'Memory Effects in Polymer Films'. Under the title, there was one name: 'Dr. H. Voss'.
Noah's hands were cold. The committee had not come out yet. And on the stage, the man began to speak about his numbers.
A2.proof: Under the title, there was one name

o: Voss presents Noah's work with only his own name on it.

Voss thanks Noah.
Voss cancels the lecture.
A2.hint: Sahnede şu anda tam olarak ne oluyor?
A2.why: Voss, Noah'ın çalışmasını yalnızca kendi adıyla sunuyor.

eps.title: A Question from the Second Row
eps.recap: Prof. Alder ayağa kalktı ve sözü istedi. Elinde siyah defter, yürüyerek sahneye çıktı. Voss'a döndü ve 'Bu sayıyı ilk bulan kim?' diye sordu. Salon sessizleşti.

text: Dr. Voss was in the middle of his fifth slide when a chair moved in the second row. A woman stood up. She was small, with grey hair. She held a black notebook against her chest.
"Excuse me, Dr. Voss," she said. Her voice was calm and strong. "I am Professor Margaret Alder. May I ask a question?"
A thousand people turned their heads. Dr. Voss's smile became stiff. "Of course, Margaret," he said. "But perhaps after my lecture..."

"It is a very short question," said Professor Alder. She walked slowly down the aisle to the stage. "You said that tau-star is your discovery. Please tell us: on which date did you first calculate it?"
Dr. Voss opened his mouth. He closed it. In the big hall, nobody moved.

text: "I do not have my notebooks with me," said Dr. Voss at last. His voice was a little too high. "Everything is in my office. It is not usual to carry notebooks to a lecture."
"I understand," said Professor Alder. "Luckily, I have brought one."

She held up the black notebook. She opened it at a page marked with a red paper clip. "This is the notebook of my student, Noah Kaya," she said. "On the ninth of March, he wrote the number tau-star for the first time. Here is the date. Here is his signature. And here is my signature, because I checked it the next day."
She turned the notebook to the audience. In the second row, somebody took a photograph. In the third row, somebody whispered.
A scientist from the middle of the hall stood up. "Dr. Voss," he said, "where is your notebook for the ninth of March?" Dr. Voss did not answer. Nobody was smiling any more.

eps.title: The Committee Enters
eps.recap: Tam o sırada salonun yan kapısından Etik Kurul Başkanı Prof. Lindqvist ve iki üye girdi. Başkan sahneye çıktı, mikrofonu aldı ve Dr. Voss'un tüm görevlerinden geçici olarak uzaklaştırıldığını ve resmî bir soruşturmanın başladığını açıkladı.

text: At that moment, a side door of the hall opened. Three people walked in. At the front was a tall man with white hair and a dark overcoat. It was Professor Lindqvist, the chairman of the Ethics Committee.
He walked up the steps to the stage. Nobody stopped him. He took the microphone from the stand.
"Ladies and gentlemen," he said, "please forgive this interruption. I must make a short announcement."
He turned to Dr. Voss. "Henrik, as of this moment, you are suspended from all your duties at the university. An official investigation into academic misconduct has begun."
The hall was silent for three seconds. Then a thousand voices began to speak at once. Dr. Voss put down the remote control, very slowly, on the table. His hand was shaking.
A2.proof: An official investigation into academic misconduct has begun

o: Voss gets an award.
The conference is cancelled by Voss.

Voss is suspended and an official investigation starts.
A2.hint: Bu sahnenin sonunda tam olarak ne oluyor?
A2.why: Voss görevden uzaklaştırılıyor ve resmî bir soruşturma başlıyor.

eps.title: Author Order

text: The investigation lasted three weeks. The committee read all the documents. They talked to Mr. Dalton, Mr. Okoye, Dr. Chen, and the editor of the journal. At the end, the result was clear. Dr. Voss had stolen the work.
The journal sent Professor Alder an apology. It cancelled the false submission and accepted the true one. The paper was published in the next issue.
On the first page, there were three names. Noah opened the journal in the library. He read slowly: 'N. Kaya, M. Alder, L. Chen.'
His name was first. For a doctoral student, it was the biggest moment of his life. Noah closed his eyes. Then he opened them again, to be sure.
Below the authors' names, there was a short note: 'The authors thank Mei Lin for her careful help and for her courage.' Mei, who was sitting next to him, began to laugh and cry at the same time.

eps.title: A Resignation
eps.recap: Voss, soruşturmanın sonunda üniversiteden istifa etti. Veda mektubunda hiçbir şey açıklamadı, yalnızca kısa bir cümle yazdı: 'Yanlış anladınız.' Prof. Alder mektubu okuyup masasına koydu ve bir daha bahsetmedi.

text: On a rainy Monday, the university sent an email to all staff. It was short. 'Dr. Henrik Voss has resigned from his position as Deputy Dean, effective immediately.'
In the evening, Professor Alder found an envelope in her pigeonhole. It had no stamp. On it was her name in neat handwriting. She knew the handwriting well. She had taught it, twenty-five years ago.
She opened the letter and read. It was one line only: 'You misunderstood. H.'
Professor Alder looked at it for a long time. She did not feel anger. She felt a deep, tired sadness. She had wanted to be proud of him. He had given her only an excuse.
She put the letter in her desk drawer, under old stamps and pencils. She never spoke about it again.
A2.q: What is Voss's final message?
o: A long apology.
A short excuse without any apology or explanation.
A thank-you letter.
A confession of everything.
A2.hint: Voss'un son mektubu nasıl bir mesaj?
A2.why: Özür ya da açıklama içermeyen, yalnızca kısa bir bahane.

o: That she is a handwriting expert.
That she learned it from a book.
That she had been Voss's teacher and recognises him by his writing.
That the letter was from a stranger.
B1.hint: Elyazısı detayı ne ortaya koyuyor?

B2.proof: a private grief that required no further evidence
B2.q: How does Professor Alder choose to deal with her sadness?
o: By holding a press conference.
By writing a book.
By confronting Voss.
Privately, without further discussion or investigation.
B2.hint: Prof. Alder üzüntüsüyle nasıl başa çıkmayı seçiyor?
B2.why: Bunu özel tutuyor ve konuyu bir daha açmıyor.

She put the letter in her desk drawer, under the old stamps and pencils, and never mentioned it again. C1.proof: nobody misunderstands a thing they have not already understood very well
C1.q: What does Noah later conclude about 'You misunderstood'?
o: That it unintentionally admits Voss understood the situation perfectly.
That it is an honest explanation.
That it is a joke.
That it is addressed to someone else.

C1.why: Cümle istemeden Voss'un durumu çok iyi anladığını itiraf ediyor.

eps.title: The First Sentence
eps.recap: Bahar geldiğinde Noah, kütüphanedeki masasında ilk bağımsız makalesini yazmaya başladı. Başlık hazırdı, ilk cümle de: 'Her sayı bir soruya cevaptır; asıl iş, hangi soru olduğunu hatırlamaktır.' Prof. Alder kapıdan baktı ve sessizce gülümsedi.

text: It was spring. Cherry trees were pink outside the library windows. Noah sat at his usual table, the one near the old window. In front of him, there was a clean white page and a sharpened pencil.
He had been thinking about this day for many months. His first paper without any help. His first paper with only his own name at the top. He did not know yet if he was ready.
He wrote the title. Then, slowly, with his best handwriting, he wrote the first sentence: 'Every number is an answer to a question; the real work is remembering which question it was.'
He read it twice. He was happy with it. Then he took a deep breath and began the second sentence.
At the door of the library, Professor Alder stopped. She watched him for a moment. She did not say anything. She only smiled, and walked away quietly, so as not to disturb him.
A2.q: What does Professor Alder's silent smile show?
o: She is angry with him.
She is lost.
She is proud of Noah and does not want to disturb him.
She is bored.
A2.hint: Prof. Alder'in sessiz gülümsemesi neyi gösteriyor?
A2.why: Noah'la gurur duyuyor ve onu rahatsız etmek istemiyor.

text: It was spring. Cherry trees were pink outside the library windows. Noah sat at his usual table beside the old window, with a clean white page and a sharpened pencil in front of him.
He had been thinking about this day for months: his first paper without any help, with only his own name at the top. He did not yet know if he was ready, and he suspected that nobody ever does.
He wrote the title. Then, slowly and in his best handwriting, he wrote the first sentence: 'Every number is an answer to a question; the real work is remembering which question it was.'

He read it twice and was pleased. It was a sentence that could only have been written by someone who had once seen a number stolen from its question. Then he took a deep breath and began the second sentence.
At the library door Professor Alder paused and watched him for a moment. She said nothing. She only smiled and walked quietly away, so as not to disturb him.
B2.proof: seen a number stolen from its question
B2.q: How does the first sentence reflect Noah's experience?
o: It shows what he learned from seeing his own work taken and misused.
It shows that he likes mathematics.
It shows that he hates numbers.
It is a copied quote.
B2.hint: İlk cümle Noah'ın yaşadıklarını nasıl yansıtıyor?
B2.why: Kendi çalışmasının çalınıp yanlış kullanılmasını görerek öğrendiği dersi yansıtıyor.

text: It was spring. Cherry trees were pink outside the library windows. Noah sat at his usual table beside the old window, with a clean white page and a sharpened pencil in front of him.
He had been thinking about this day for months: his first paper without any help, with only his own name at the top. He did not yet know if he was ready, and he suspected that nobody ever does.
He wrote the title. Then, slowly and in his best handwriting, he wrote the first sentence: 'Every number is an answer to a question; the real work is remembering which question it was.'

He read it twice and was pleased. It was a sentence that could only have been written by someone who had once seen a number stolen from its question. Then he took a deep breath and began the second sentence.

At the library door Professor Alder paused and watched him for a moment. She said nothing. She only smiled and walked quietly away, so as not to disturb him. She had given him, she reflected, the only things a teacher can give: a method, a notebook with a date in it, and the freedom to be wrong in his own handwriting. The rest was his, and always had been.
C1.proof: the freedom to be wrong in his own handwriting
C1.q: What does Professor Alder believe a teacher can give?
o: Money and fame.
Method, honest records, and the freedom for students to make their own mistakes.
All the answers.
Rules without reasons.
C1.hint: Prof. Alder'e göre bir öğretmen öğrencisine ne verebilir?
C1.why: Yöntem, dürüst kayıtlar ve öğrencinin kendi hatalarını yapma özgürlüğü.
